source.note: New recurrent hierarchy joined to the complete reviewed engineering extraction.

nodes.label: Actuation, Therapy, and Delivery
nodes.description: Functions whose primary purpose is to generate controlled physical, chemical, optical, electrical, biological, or therapeutic intervention or to deliver an active payload.

nodes.label: Communication and Data Transfer
nodes.description: Functions that transmit, receive, address, multiplex, identify, synchronize, store for transfer, or remotely interrogate information between system components or locations.

nodes.label: Computing, Control, and Decision Support
nodes.description: Digital or algorithmic functions that transform acquired data into features, estimates, classifications, decisions, feedback, scheduling, or intervention commands.

nodes.label: Electronics and Signal Conditioning
nodes.description: Electronic components and front-end circuits that bias, amplify, filter, multiplex, buffer, rectify, switch, condition, or route signals before higher-level computation or communication.

nodes.label: Fabrication and Assembly
nodes.description: Processes and assembly operations whose primary purpose is to create, pattern, release, transfer, align, replicate, or integrate material and device structures.

nodes.label: Modeling, Calibration, Validation, and Translation
nodes.description: Reusable methods for calibrating measurements, constructing or inverting models, validating mechanisms and performance, quantifying uncertainty, and assessing translation or application readiness.

nodes.label: Packaging, Deployment, and Lifecycle
nodes.description: Functions that protect, package, deploy, fix, conform, retrieve, reuse, biodegrade, resorb, or otherwise govern a device's operational environment and lifecycle.

nodes.label: Power and Energy
nodes.description: Functions that generate, harvest, convert, store, regulate, buffer, distribute, or thermally manage energy for system operation.

nodes.label: Sample Acquisition, Transport, and Fluidics
nodes.description: Functions that acquire, contain, condition, route, mix, separate, store, recover, or deliver fluids and samples through physical fluidic pathways.

nodes.label: Sensing, Transduction, Imaging, and Output
nodes.description: Functions that convert physical, chemical, biological, optical, or mechanical inputs into measured, imaged, indicated, or otherwise observable outputs.

nodes.label: Structures, Materials, and Interfaces
nodes.description: Reusable physical architectures, material behaviors, and interfaces that define mechanical, optical, electrical, chemical, biological, or transport boundary conditions independent of a specific fabrication step.

nodes.label: 3D Deformation-Amplified Pressure Transduction
nodes.description: Use compliant three-dimensional structures in which applied pressure deforms the structure, increases strain in integrated gauges, and changes their electrical resistance.
nodes.function: Measure or enhance local normal-pressure transduction in compliant interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Pressure deforms cavities, pillars, suspended membranes, or tent-like mesostructures, concentrating displacement or strain in an electrical transducer.

nodes.label: 3D Electrolyte-Access Electrode Architecture
nodes.description: Use an open, interconnected 3D electrode architecture with thin active layers to shorten ion-transport paths while retaining electronic connectivity.
nodes.function: Improve rate capability and preserve high active-material utilization in high-surface-area electrodes.
nodes.mechanism: Interconnected pores and walls expose internal active surfaces to electrolyte while connected current collectors provide electronic pathways.

nodes.label: 3D Multimodal Tissue Interface
nodes.description: Use a flexible three-dimensional electronic-tissue framework to colocate electrical and mechanical sensing at multiple defined locations and, in some implementations, provide electrical or pharmacological modulation.
nodes.function: Measure and perturb biological activity over a three-dimensional soft-tissue geometry.
nodes.mechanism: A shaped or compliant framework maintains tissue contact while electrical, mechanical, optical, thermal, chemical, or pharmacological channels operate with coordinated acquisition or control.
failure_modes: loading conditions that do not represent the intended physiology

nodes.label: Active Array Readout
nodes.description: Use local switches or buffers with sequential row and shared-column addressing to connect many distributed sensor sites to a smaller set of readout lines.
nodes.function: Reduce wiring and external acquisition burden while preserving access to dense sensor arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Row selection activates local unit cells; switches and optional local amplifiers route selected signals to shared column outputs.
failure_modes: Switching limited by control slew rate

nodes.label: Actuation-Coupled Modulus Sensing
nodes.description: Estimate local soft-tissue modulus by mechanically coupling an actuating element to one or more sensing elements and calibrating the electrical response against tissue mechanics.
nodes.function: Measure local stiffness or elastic modulus on compliant or curved biological surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Periodic actuation deforms the substrate and contacting tissue; coupled sensors measure the resulting response, which is mapped to modulus by a calibration model.
failure_modes: non-monotonic response at high or low modulus
reduced deformation and signal with overly stiff substrate

nodes.label: Adhesion-Bounded Relief Operating Window
nodes.description: Choose relief geometry, stiffness, adhesion, and preload within lower and upper bounds that support reversible collapse and reliable pickup or release.
nodes.function: Translate mechanics and interface parameters into a stable operating window for compliant transfer structures.
nodes.mechanism: The lower bound ensures elastic recovery overcomes adhesion after collapse; the upper bound limits restoring-force-driven delamination or self-collapse through energy balance.

nodes.label: Adhesion-Driven Conformal Contact
nodes.description: Use a sufficiently compliant thin device and interfacial adhesion or capillary energy to establish passive, conformal contact with a curved or textured surface.
nodes.function: Create low-force, intimate, and potentially reversible device-surface contact.
nodes.mechanism: Interfacial adhesion, van der Waals forces, or drying-induced capillary forces overcome the bending-energy penalty of a compliant film.
failure_modes: Poor contact on extreme curvature or hair

nodes.label: Adhesion–Elasticity Collapse Modeling
nodes.description: Predict equilibrium collapse, contact extent, and stability of compliant relief structures by minimizing elastic deformation energy minus adhesion-energy gain.
nodes.function: Relate relief geometry and material/interface properties to collapse onset, extent, and stability.
nodes.mechanism: A continuum or equivalent-crack representation computes deformation energy and subtracts adhesion energy over the contacting region; total-energy minimization determines the state.
failure_modes: Incorrect prediction if material nonlinearities or kinetics dominate
Model invalid when collapse length exceeds post spacing
model assumptions violated by non-cylindrical patterns
poor transfer of calibrated parameter across geometries

nodes.label: Adhesion-Guided Dry Transfer Printing
nodes.description: Transfer patterned films, networks, or discrete functional elements from a donor or compliant stamp to a receiver by using conformal contact and controlled relative interfacial adhesion.
nodes.function: Place fragile functional materials on selected substrates while preserving pattern and registration.
nodes.mechanism: A stamp or donor contacts the material, pickup and release are controlled by adhesion contrast, and peeling, sliding, curing, or mild thermal/contact conditions leave the material on the receiver.
failure_modes: Incomplete transfer to rough or low-energy surfaces

nodes.label: Reference-Normalized Optical Imaging
nodes.description: Use a recorded background or matched reference to correct spatial illumination variation and obtain quantitatively interpretable image values.
nodes.function: Improve comparability and quantitative reliability of optical images.
nodes.mechanism: Pixelwise or region-based normalization removes shared illumination, vignetting, and detector-path variation.
failure_modes: Incorrect background estimate can distort real spatial contrast
normalization does not remove all optical convolution
reference region may contain an unmodeled coating

nodes.label: Biofluid-Barrier Lifetime Validation
nodes.description: Expose encapsulated structures to defined PBS conditions and monitor electrical performance over the soak period to assess barrier stability.
nodes.function: Quantify barrier survival and identify failure onset.
nodes.mechanism: Fluid ingress or barrier degradation alters a measurable protected structure response; comparison with an unprotected control estimates the protection interval.
failure_modes: False lifetime attribution from reader-medium changes

nodes.label: Behavioral Validation of Biointerventions
nodes.description: Use controlled behavioral assays, matched controls, and performance-versus-chance or condition comparisons to validate perceptual, analgesic, functional, or deployment effects of a biointervention.
nodes.function: Establish organism-level detectability, efficacy, and behavioral artifacts.
nodes.mechanism: Intervention state is paired with evoked behavior, preference, discrimination, mobility, social, or task-performance measurements under controlled comparison conditions.
failure_modes: inability to directly measure subjective pain

nodes.label: Bending-Dominated Resonance Scaling
nodes.description: Use FEA to determine shape- and mode-dependent scaling factors in bending-dominated vibration modeling.
nodes.function: Guide resonator design across material systems and geometric scales.
nodes.mechanism: Relate effective bending stiffness and mass to frequency through dimensionless shape or mode factors, with calibration from FEA or experiment when needed.

nodes.label: Electrical Deformation-Tolerance Validation
nodes.description: Measure electrical response over repeated bending cycles at defined bend radii to assess flexible-device stability.
nodes.function: Assess curvature-dependent performance, retained function, and failure thresholds.
nodes.mechanism: A flexible device is bent to defined radii while electrical characteristics are measured and compared across bent and recovered states.

nodes.label: Bias-Controlled Ionic Barrier Protection
nodes.description: Control or suppress bias-driven ionic transport through an insulating barrier to stabilize an underlying electronic device in an ionic environment.
nodes.function: Explain and manage bias-induced ionic degradation and threshold drift.
nodes.mechanism: An applied electric field drives mobile ions toward or through the barrier; barrier composition and thickness regulate transport and charge accumulation near the active interface.

nodes.label: Thermoelectric Thermal Actuation
nodes.description: Generate reversible heating and cooling at a compliant interface by controlling current direction through thermoelectric junctions and managing waste heat.
nodes.function: Provide bidirectional thermal stimulation.
nodes.mechanism: The Peltier effect moves heat between junction sides according to current direction; heat sinking or thermal management limits backflow and accumulation.

nodes.label: Bilayer Mismatch-Deformation Modeling
nodes.description: Model or characterize bonded-bilayer bending and rolling angle from mismatch/prestrain and layer thickness or thickness ratio using analytic or finite-element approaches.
nodes.function: Translate layer mismatch and geometry into designed bilayer shape change.
nodes.mechanism: Represent differential expansion or contraction as eigenstrain or equivalent thermal strain, then enforce layered stress and moment equilibrium or solve nonlinear shell/solid mechanics.
failure_modes: model mismatch outside assumed constitutive or geometric regime

nodes.label: Biofluid-Barrier Encapsulation
nodes.description: Encapsulate functional electronics with one or more conformal barrier layers that limit water, ion, or biofluid ingress while preserving operation in the intended environment.
nodes.function: Protect electronics from fluid-induced leakage, corrosion, degradation, and mechanical exposure.
nodes.mechanism: Dense inorganic, polymeric, or hybrid layers interrupt permeation pathways and electrically isolate the device; multilayer stacks reduce through-thickness defect continuity.

nodes.label: Biofluid Conditioning and Antifouling Routing
nodes.description: Condition or route sweat before sensing to remove serum-soluble interferents and refresh the sensing site, improving measurement accuracy.
nodes.function: Improve sample quality and analytical accuracy before or during measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Preconcentration, incubation, selective barriers, hydrogel interfaces, refreshed sensing zones, or channel routing separate target fluid from interferents.

nodes.label: Bioresorbable Implanted Physiological Sensing
nodes.description: Use a bioresorbable implanted sensor whose barrier thickness and material hydrolysis determine its functional lifetime, with physiological-timescale lifetime estimated from accelerated testing.
nodes.function: Measure physiological variables during a defined implant interval and then resorb.
nodes.mechanism: A transient sensor combines a physiological transducer with dissolution-rate control and an external or optical readout interface.
aliases: transient implanted pressure and temperature sensing

nodes.label: BLE Wireless Monitoring Link
nodes.description: Transmit measurements autonomously or wirelessly via Bluetooth Low Energy from wearable or skin-mounted sensing systems to smartphones or other external interfaces.
nodes.function: Provide low-duty-cycle wireless monitoring and remote readout.
nodes.mechanism: A BLE radio or system-on-chip advertises or connects to a receiving interface and transports digitized sensor data.

nodes.label: Bonding-Pattern and Prestrain 2D-to-3D Programming
nodes.description: Program thin-film or ribbon 3D geometry by jointly selecting planar precursor layout, selective bonding pattern, and substrate prestrain.
nodes.function: Translate planar layout and assembly loading into a target buckled, folded, or otherwise transformed 3D architecture.
nodes.mechanism: Bonding sites constrain motion and delimit released regions; precursor geometry selects deformation modes; prestrain supplies compressive displacement and amplitude.
failure_modes: Cracking from overly narrow inactive regions
Very long inactivated regions causing short-wave modes

nodes.label: Colorimetric Chemical Readout
nodes.description: Convert analyte-dependent color changes into quantitative chemical estimates using calibrated optical or digital color measurements.
nodes.function: Provide low-complexity optical quantification of chemical analytes.
nodes.mechanism: Analyte-responsive chemistry changes color; calibrated image features such as CIELAB or RGB values are corrected for background or reference and mapped to concentration.

nodes.label: Capacitive Biointerface Through Barrier
nodes.description: Use a high-impedance or thin capping layer to protect electronics from biofluids and enable tissue or fluid interface measurements, with shielding used to reduce environmental coupling where demonstrated.
nodes.function: Record or stimulate biological potentials or measure nearby fluid while protecting electronics and reducing parasitic signals.
nodes.mechanism: Signals couple capacitively through a controlled dielectric barrier; barrier thickness and conductive shielding set desired and parasitic coupling.

nodes.label: Encapsulated Bioelectrical Interface
nodes.description: Use an insulating dielectric as both environmental barrier and capacitive coupling path between biological tissue and underlying electronics.
nodes.function: Record bioelectrical signals while isolating electronics from direct tissue or biofluid contact.
nodes.mechanism: Tissue potentials couple through a dielectric to an electrode or transistor gate; dielectric thickness, area, and integrity determine coupling and protection.
failure_modes: Signal attenuation from insufficient coupling capacitance
loss of signal after contamination or poor contact

nodes.label: Catalyst-Free Direct Nanowire Heteroepitaxy
nodes.description: Directly grow compositionally tunable one-dimensional semiconductor nanowire arrays on a crystalline or conducting substrate without metal catalyst particles or prepatterning.
nodes.function: Create ordered heterogeneous nanowire arrays integrated directly with a substrate.
nodes.mechanism: MOCVD enables direct epitaxial or mismatch-strain-driven self-assembly; nanowire geometry laterally relaxes lattice mismatch, while substrate, diameter, and growth conditions control coherence and yield.
failure_modes: Irregular nanoneedles or islands above the critical diameter

nodes.label: Chemical Surface-Directed BCP Assembly
nodes.description: Use spatially patterned surface chemistry and differential wetting to register and orient self-assembled block-copolymer domains.
nodes.function: Direct BCP domain orientation and spatial registration.
nodes.mechanism: Block-selective or neutral surface interactions alter interfacial free energy and guide domain morphology at designated regions.

nodes.label: Chemical Carrier-Polarity Control
nodes.description: Change the carrier polarity of a semiconducting channel through chemically induced charge transfer or doping, optionally with spatially selective coating.
nodes.function: Configure p-type, n-type, or ambipolar operation without changing the basic electrode layout.
nodes.mechanism: A chemically active coating, electrolyte, or dielectric transfers charge or alters injection at the semiconductor surface, shifting carrier polarity and threshold behavior.

nodes.label: Chemically Selective Contact Transfer
nodes.description: Transfer patterned solid material by conformal contact and selective chemical bonding that makes substrate–ink adhesion exceed ink–stamp adhesion.
nodes.function: Patterned material transfer with spatial selectivity.
nodes.mechanism: Conformal contact brings reactive interfaces together; patterned or uniform surface chemistry creates stronger bonding at selected substrate regions, and stamp removal leaves the material transferred.

nodes.label: Closed-Loop Bioelectronic Modulation
nodes.description: Sense biological state, infer a condition, and conditionally trigger or adjust a bioelectronic therapeutic actuator.
nodes.function: Provide state-dependent real-time biological intervention.
nodes.mechanism: Physiological sensors feed signal processing or inference; decision logic controls electrical, optical, thermal, or pharmacological actuation through local or wireless interfaces.

nodes.label: Closed-Loop Thermal Regulation
nodes.description: Regulate a local thermal actuator using temperature feedback and a controller to track a target temperature or thermal state.
nodes.function: Deliver repeatable thermal exposure while limiting overshoot and damage.
nodes.mechanism: A temperature sensor measures the actuator or target; a controller modulates heater power, duty cycle, or drive current against a set point.

nodes.label: Co-Registered Multimodal Biointerface
nodes.description: Integrate multiple sensing and actuation modalities on compliant or flexible biological interfaces for simultaneous recording and modulation.
nodes.function: Measure, stimulate, perturb, and monitor biological systems across multiple physical modalities.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical, optical, thermal, chemical, mechanical, or fluidic modules share a tissue-conforming substrate or three-dimensional framework while retaining modality-specific addressing.

nodes.label: Competing-Interface Fracture Transfer Criterion
nodes.description: Predict transfer direction or crack-path selection by comparing energy-release rates with the fracture toughnesses of competing interfaces.
nodes.function: Select pickup, printing, retrieval, or transfer conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Interfacial crack driving forces are calculated for competing paths and compared with their critical toughness; the interface with the larger driving-force-to-toughness ratio fails first.
failure_modes: 2D effective defect size not representing full 3D edge flaws
Breakdown of small-crack or linearized assumptions
incorrect crack-path prediction under significant mixed-mode dependence
incorrect prediction if local fracture effects dominate
mode-mixity dependence not accounted for in the simplified treatment

nodes.label: Transistor Logic Gate Architecture
nodes.description: Complementary n- and p-channel transistor inverter or NOT-gate circuits have been fabricated and characterized in reported device studies.
nodes.function: Implement digital logic inversion.
nodes.mechanism: Complementary transistor paths produce an output voltage opposite to the applied input.
failure_modes: Mobility mismatch can unbalance current outputs and reduce inverter performance

nodes.label: Compliant 3D Volumetric Biointerface
nodes.description: Use a compliant open or shape-matched three-dimensional framework to place distributed functional interfaces around or within a volumetric biological object.
nodes.function: Support distributed recording, stimulation, sensing, or local delivery while accommodating tissue geometry and infiltration.
nodes.mechanism: Porous or articulated 3D frameworks position tissue-proximal electrodes and other modules across multiple locations with compliant mechanical contact.
failure_modes: Loss of contact during growth or handling
Poor contact due to curvature mismatch

nodes.label: Geometric Stretchable Interconnect
nodes.description: Serpentine or buckled metal interconnects can absorb tensile, bending, and related substrate deformation while sustaining electronic connections over reported operating ranges; failure can occur beyond those ranges.
nodes.function: Provide deformation-tolerant electrical interconnection between rigid or semi-rigid regions.
nodes.mechanism: Nonlinear geometric deformation redistributes imposed extension and bending, limiting axial strain in the conductor.

nodes.label: Conformable Phase-Mask Patterning
nodes.description: Use a transparent compliant relief mask in conformal or near-field contact with a photosensitive layer to transfer a relief-defined optical intensity distribution into nanoscale, quasi-three-dimensional, or three-dimensional material patterns.
nodes.function: Fabricate nanoscale and three-dimensional polymer or resist structures by contact optical exposure.
nodes.mechanism: Relief-induced phase modulation, diffraction, and interference shape the near-field intensity; exposure, material response, and development convert that field into patterned relief.
failure_modes: Insufficient structure away from the mask surface
Loss of intensity visibility with depth

nodes.label: Conformal Distributed Electrophysiology Array
nodes.description: Distributed electrode arrays have been used to record electrical activity across biological surfaces, including curved beating hearts and cortical surfaces.
nodes.function: Provide spatially resolved electrophysiological recording and, where configured, localized stimulation with reduced motion and wiring penalties.
nodes.mechanism: Flexible or stretchable substrates, distributed electrodes, compliant interconnects, and external or local acquisition electronics maintain tissue contact during deformation.

nodes.label: Conformal Hybrid Microfluidic Platform
nodes.description: Skin-mounted microfluidic systems can preserve channel, valve, and chamber function during stretching, flexing, twisting, shaking, and device removal; low-modulus interfaces, waterproofing, and serpentine structural features are reported implementation elements.
nodes.function: Maintain fluid containment, mechanical compliance, optical access, or lifecycle compatibility under use constraints.
nodes.mechanism: Soft elastomers, hard skeletons, serpentine geometries, multilayer molding, waterproofing, or biodegradable materials are combined around channels and reservoirs.

nodes.label: Conformal Skin Interface
nodes.description: Create a soft, conformal, low-artifact interface that maintains intimate coupling between a device and moving skin.
nodes.function: Maintain contact, signal fidelity, comfort, and adhesion during body motion and repeated use.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical-property matching, ultrathin construction, adhesive or van der Waals coupling, and openings or breathable structures reduce interfacial motion and stress.

nodes.label: Continuous Wearable Monitoring Pipeline
nodes.description: Implement wearable monitoring with local storage or BLE streaming to a mobile device, local or cloud signal processing, and user-facing data display.
nodes.function: Turn continuous heterogeneous sensor streams into accessible physiological, behavioral, or clinical information.
nodes.mechanism: Sensors acquire continuously; embedded, mobile, or cloud components buffer, transmit, store, process, and present data through interoperable interfaces.

nodes.label: Coupled Mechanics–Multiphysics Modeling
nodes.description: Couple mechanical deformation models with electrical, optical, piezoelectric, or other functional models to predict performance changes under reconfiguration.
nodes.function: Interpret or co-design mechanically reconfigurable multifunctional devices.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical state predictions are transferred into coupled field, circuit, optical, or electromechanical calculations and validated against measured response.
failure_modes: Weak coupling at small coil size

nodes.label: Coverage–Stretchability Co-Optimization
nodes.description: Optimize island spacing and associated interconnect geometry to balance high areal coverage against system stretchability.
nodes.function: Select island–bridge layouts under deformation and fabrication constraints.
nodes.mechanism: Higher coverage requires smaller spacing and reduces available compliant interconnect length; geometry, hierarchy, and non-overlap constraints define the feasible tradeoff.
failure_modes: plastic yielding at bends or island junctions

nodes.label: Mechanics Model–Simulation–Experiment Validation
nodes.description: Validate a mechanics-based model or design rule by comparing predictions with an independent numerical formulation and, when available, controlled physical geometry, strain, force, or functional measurements under matched conditions.
nodes.function: Establish predictive adequacy, applicability limits, and design-relevant failure or performance bounds for reduced or full mechanics models.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical, reduced-order, or finite-element predictions are mapped to comparable observables from independent simulations and experiments across defined geometry, material, interface, and loading ranges.
failure_modes: Apparent agreement caused by shared assumptions
False agreement from mismatched boundary conditions

nodes.label: Crystalline-Substrate-Guided CVD Alignment
nodes.description: Use crystallographically or topographically anisotropic crystalline substrates during CVD to guide one-dimensional nanostructures into horizontally aligned arrays, optionally using patterned catalysts to define spatial geometry.
nodes.function: Produce aligned, spatially organized nanostructure arrays for downstream integration.
nodes.mechanism: Substrate crystallography, atomic steps, facets, or anisotropic surface interactions bias nucleation and growth direction; catalyst patterning constrains where growth occurs.
failure_modes: Bundling and multiwalled growth at excessive catalyst density
Disordered or amorphous surface suppresses a unique preferred direction
Excessive relief or roughness can reduce alignment
Growth outside the intended catalyst regions
Growth termination at surface relief or obstructing material
Reduced alignment from unreacted catalyst particles

nodes.label: Curved-Surface Transfer Integration
nodes.description: Transfer prefabricated thin devices or interconnected arrays onto curved receivers by conformal contact, controlled release, or shape-transforming compliant supports.
nodes.function: Enable integration of planar-fabricated electronics or optoelectronics on nonplanar substrates.
nodes.mechanism: A compliant stamp or membrane conforms to the donor and curved receiver, while adhesion control and elastic deformation preserve device registration and accommodate curvature.

nodes.label: Deformation Model–Measurement Validation
nodes.description: Validate analytical or numerical deformation models by comparing predicted geometry, strain, or response with measurements under controlled loading.
nodes.function: Test model accuracy and identify discrepancies in mechanics–device coupling.
nodes.mechanism: A known geometry and loading condition produces measured displacement, profile, strain, or functional response that is compared with analytical or FEM predictions.

nodes.label: Deterministic Array Transfer Printing
nodes.description: Use soft-stamp transfer printing to retrieve microdevices and assemble them into variable-density receiver layouts with high throughput and, in some implementations, micron-scale positioning accuracy.
nodes.function: Enable parallel, deterministic heterogeneous assembly of discrete microdevices.
nodes.mechanism: Donor-side release and retention are coupled with patterned or compliant stamp pickup, adhesion switching, and receiver placement.

nodes.label: Deterministic Transfer Printing
nodes.description: Retrieve selected solid micro- or nanostructures from a donor platform and deliver them in controlled locations and arrangements onto a receiver substrate.
nodes.function: Enable parallel, spatially registered heterogeneous assembly across incompatible material and substrate systems.
nodes.mechanism: An elastomeric or otherwise engineered transfer tool uses controlled adhesion, release, and receiver bonding to retrieve and place patterned solid inks.

nodes.label: Differential Reference Compensation
nodes.description: Compare matched measuring and reference channels and subtract their responses to suppress shared disturbances while retaining stimulus components that differ spatially or by sensitivity.
nodes.function: Reduce common-mode environmental, mechanical, thermal, or parasitic interference.
nodes.mechanism: A characterized reference experiences shared disturbance but differs in sensitivity or target exposure; differential processing removes the shared component.
failure_modes: Reduced duty cycle and depth when pulsing
Reference sensor coupling too strongly to heater

nodes.label: Diode-Isolated Matrix Addressing
nodes.description: Use diode-isolated unit cells with row-column biasing to select distributed sensing or stimulation sites while suppressing unselected paths.
nodes.function: Reduce wiring and prevent sneak currents in matrix-addressed arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Selected diode paths are forward-biased while unselected paths are reverse-biased; shared lines carry the selected response.

nodes.label: Directed-Flow Alignment of Elongated Nanostructures
nodes.description: Use directional fluid motion during deposition or assembly to orient mobile elongated nanostructures and create anisotropic networks or films.
nodes.function: Control orientation and directional connectivity of nanotube-based structures.
nodes.mechanism: Shear, laminar flow, or convective motion biases elongated structures toward a prescribed flow direction during deposition.
failure_modes: Weak alignment near poorly defined flow regions

nodes.label: Distributed Sensor Time Synchronization
nodes.description: Distribute or coordinate a shared timing reference across spatially separated sensor nodes so measurements can be aligned for multimodal comparison, fusion, or timing-derived inference.
nodes.function: Align distributed sensor measurements on a common timeline.
nodes.mechanism: A master, hub, or synchronization channel periodically transfers timing information; local nodes update or coordinate timestamps before measurement streams are fused downstream.
design_handles: Number and placement of sensor sites

nodes.label: Drop-on-Demand Inkjet Deposition
nodes.description: Pattern functional liquid materials by digitally triggering individual droplets from thermally or piezoelectrically actuated nozzles.
nodes.function: Place liquid functional materials with digital spatial control and material efficiency.
nodes.mechanism: A thermal bubble, piezoelectric pressure impulse, or controlled voltage event ejects discrete droplets from a reservoir through a nozzle.

nodes.label: Dual-Stage Optical Concentration
nodes.description: Combine primary imaging optics with miniature secondary optics to concentrate direct sunlight onto small photovoltaic receivers while managing irradiance uniformity.
nodes.function: Deliver high optical concentration to microscale photovoltaic receivers.
nodes.mechanism: Sequential imaging stages reduce the solar image onto the receiver and redistribute rays.
failure_modes: Voltage drop from low-irradiance sidewall collection

nodes.label: Duty-Cycled Operation
nodes.description: Schedule sleep intervals between sensing, actuation, processing, or transmission bursts to reduce average energy and thermal load while preserving required temporal sampling.
nodes.function: Reduce average power in intermittently active devices.
nodes.mechanism: A controller disables or downscales peripherals during idle intervals and activates selected functions during scheduled bursts.

nodes.label: Dynamic Bond-Exchange Polymer Networks
nodes.description: Use dynamic covalent bond exchange to enable self-bonding in b-DCPU and reprocessing, recycling, or reprogramming in cross-linked liquid-crystal-elastomer networks.
nodes.function: Provide reconfigurable, recyclable, or bioresorbable polymer packaging with controlled bonding.
nodes.mechanism: Thermally or chemically activated bond exchange rearranges the network while retaining network integrity.

nodes.label: Electrode-Skin Impedance Modeling
nodes.description: Represent electrode-skin impedance using a half-cell potential, double-layer or interfacial capacitance, charge-transfer resistance, and an additional series resistance term.
nodes.function: Interpret and fit electrical impedance at an electrode-skin or biointerface contact.
nodes.mechanism: An equivalent circuit separates interfacial electrochemical contributions from tissue or electrolyte series resistance and contact heterogeneity.

nodes.label: Electrohydrodynamic Jet Deposition
nodes.description: Use electric-field-driven electrohydrodynamic jets and Taylor-cone emission to print localized positive or negative charge patterns at micro- and nanoscale resolution.
nodes.function: Create fine spatially patterned deposits or charge distributions.
nodes.mechanism: Electrostatic stress deforms a liquid meniscus into a Taylor cone and ejects a jet when field and pressure overcome capillary forces.
failure_modes: Droplet breakup at the Rayleigh limit

nodes.label: Electromagnetic Vibrotactile Actuation
nodes.description: Convert alternating electrical current into oscillatory mechanical force or displacement through interaction between a current-carrying coil and a permanent magnet.
nodes.function: Produce localized vibration for skin-interfaced haptic stimulation.
nodes.mechanism: Time-varying coil current generates a magnetic field that interacts with a permanent magnet, with a compliant suspension guiding the moving element.

nodes.label: Embedded 3D Fluidic Interconnect Networks
nodes.description: Use a stretchable embedded fluidic interconnect with remote inlet/outlet ports to address multiple spatially distributed 3D microfluidic structures.
nodes.function: Distribute and collect fluids across remote, elevated, or branched 3D fluidic modules.
nodes.mechanism: Planar channels or precursors are connected and transformed into enclosed 3D networks with remote ports while preserving sealed fluidic paths.

nodes.label: Energy-Minimized Thin-Film Buckling Modeling
nodes.description: Predict buckling onset and post-buckling wavelength, amplitude, strain, and mode by minimizing coupled film and substrate energies under specified constitutive and interface assumptions.
nodes.function: Guide design and interpretation of prestrained or compressed thin-film buckling systems.
nodes.mechanism: Represent film deformation with beam, shell, or modal kinematics; formulate membrane, bending, substrate, and optional electromechanical energies; minimize total potential energy subject to boundary and interface conditions.
failure_modes: Incorrect predictions if slipping, plasticity, fracture, or finite-substrate effects dominate
Mode selection may require additional constraints or energy terms
Reduced accuracy at very low stiffness ratios
Simplified displacement functions may not capture bottom-layer deformation
Small-deformation model error at large prestrain
Unmodeled slip or local substrate heterogeneity

nodes.label: Dissolution-Lifetime Programming
nodes.description: Predict and tune transient-material dissolution rates by jointly controlling environmental chemistry and intrinsic material structure or processing.
nodes.function: Adjust or estimate degradation rate and resulting material lifetime under specified exposure conditions.
nodes.mechanism: pH, temperature, ion identity and concentration, doping, crystallinity, defects, porosity, geometry, thickness, and processing alter reaction and transport kinetics.

nodes.label: Epidermal Microfluidic Analysis
nodes.description: Collect, route, store, and analyze small-volume biofluid at a skin interface using a soft microfluidic network.
nodes.function: Provide localized biofluid sampling and chemical or biochemical analysis at the body surface.
nodes.mechanism: Skin openings, microchannels, reservoirs, capillary or perspiration pressure, and integrated assays manage fluid transport and measurement.

nodes.label: Exposure-Profile Porosity Grading
nodes.description: Program depth-dependent porosity or density by engineering the through-thickness exposure profile of a photosensitive material.
nodes.function: Create monotonic, periodic, or otherwise prescribed porosity gradients in structured polymer films.
nodes.mechanism: Coherence loss, angular or spectral averaging, absorption, and dose distribution alter exposure visibility or intensity with depth; development converts that profile into depth-dependent polymer retention and pore structure.
failure_modes: Excessive visibility loss near the surface or throughout the film
Loss of interconnected structure at excessive absorption
Weak gradient when bandwidth effects are small

nodes.label: External-Reference Measurement Validation
nodes.description: Assess a measurement system or derived result by comparing it with an independent reference instrument, assay, modality, or ground-truth observation under relevant operating conditions.
nodes.function: Establish agreement, accuracy, or applicability of a new measurement approach.
nodes.mechanism: Acquire matched outputs from the candidate and comparator, then evaluate agreement, correlation, error, or classification performance.
failure_modes: Different optical or mechanical sampling volumes

nodes.label: FEA–Experimental Deformation Validation
nodes.description: Validate predicted deformed shapes and strains by comparing finite-element results with full-field experimental measurements.
nodes.function: Assess mechanical model accuracy under deformation.
nodes.mechanism: FEA predicts displacement or strain fields that are compared with digital image correlation or related measurements.

nodes.label: Finite-Size Layered Strain-Transfer Modeling
nodes.description: Predict film strain and interfacial stresses under substrate bending while accounting for finite film dimensions, adhesive compliance, and layered elastic stress transfer.
nodes.function: Guide design of strain-isolated thin-film systems and assess cracking, slipping, or delamination risk.
nodes.mechanism: Use beam or plate mechanics with adhesive shear and normal compliance, force/moment equilibrium, finite-edge conditions, and strength-based failure evaluation.
failure_modes: model mismatch outside thin-layer or linear-elastic assumptions

nodes.label: Finite-Thickness Wrinkle Mechanics Modeling
nodes.description: Predict wrinkle period from film/substrate stiffness and thickness ratios, and in related bilinear models predict transition strain and elastic or tangent moduli with comparison to FEA and experiments.
nodes.function: Guide wrinkle wavelength selection and strain-limiting design.
nodes.mechanism: Film membrane and bending energies are coupled to finite-thickness substrate elasticity; analytical scaling or energy minimization yields wrinkle geometry and response.
failure_modes: using semi-infinite scaling when substrate thickness changes the response

nodes.label: Flexible-Device Deformation Fatigue Validation
nodes.description: Assess flexible-device durability by comparing electrical performance across controlled deformation states and repeated bend, stretch, or release cycles.
nodes.function: Validate deformation tolerance, performance retention, and fatigue stability of flexible electronics.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical metrics are compared with an undeformed or reference state as strain, curvature, deformation mode, and cycle count vary.
failure_modes: Localized failure hidden by aggregate metrics
failure outside tested strain or cycle range

nodes.label: Flexible Multi-Transistor Circuit Integration
nodes.description: Integrate flexible transistor stages to implement inverter, oscillator, differential-amplifier, and related circuit functions, while accounting for bending-induced stage mismatch and circuit-level sensitivity.
nodes.function: Provide circuit-level computation, oscillation, and signal amplification on mechanically flexible substrates.
nodes.mechanism: Transfer or print transistor devices onto a flexible receiver, electrically interconnect complementary or same-polarity devices into inverters, ring oscillators, current mirrors, differential pairs, and loads, and evaluate circuit-level performance under bending.
failure_modes: circuit-level failure before individual transistor failure

nodes.label: Fluid-Barrier Encapsulation
nodes.description: Use PIB/PDMS or inorganic/organic encapsulation layers as water or moisture barriers for flexible or implantable electronics exposed to saline, body fluids, or implantation conditions.
nodes.function: Prevent leakage, corrosion, and environmental degradation.
nodes.mechanism: Organic or inorganic barrier layers and sealed interfaces interrupt fluid pathways and isolate active conductors; barrier continuity and adhesion determine effectiveness.

nodes.label: Fluidic Conductive-Element Tuning
nodes.description: Move a conductive liquid within an enclosed microchannel to change an active device’s effective electrical geometry and response.
nodes.function: Dynamically tune transistor or RF-device behavior through controlled conductive-fluid motion.
nodes.mechanism: Pressure, pumping, or related actuation displaces conductive fluid, changing electrode overlap, channel geometry, or antenna length.

nodes.label: Free-Surface Expansion Accommodation
nodes.description: Introduce accessible internal or external free surfaces in a volume-changing active material so unconstrained deformation reduces stress and mechanical damage.
nodes.function: Accommodate reaction-induced volume change while preserving structural integrity and cycling stability.
nodes.mechanism: Free surfaces and internal voids permit surface-normal expansion or contraction and reduce mechanical constraint.

nodes.label: Frequency- and Timescale-Separated Signal Readout
nodes.description: Separate concurrently acquired signal processes or interference by exploiting differences in characteristic frequency or timescale.
nodes.function: Extract target signal components and reduce spectrally or temporally distinguishable artifacts.
nodes.mechanism: Backend filtering preserves target bands while attenuating unwanted components; signals from multiple locations may also be temporally aligned.

nodes.label: Full-Wave Electromagnetic Optical Modeling
nodes.description: Use full-wave electromagnetic simulation of specified optical geometries and material models to predict, interpret, validate, or optimize spectra and near fields.
nodes.function: Predict optical response, explain resonances and field distributions, and guide nanostructure design.
nodes.mechanism: Solve Maxwell equations numerically, commonly with 3D FDTD, using discretized multilayer or periodic geometries, material dispersion, illumination conditions, and appropriate boundary conditions; compare outputs with measurements when available.
failure_modes: Model-experiment discrepancies from dimensional or coating-thickness variation

nodes.label: Fully Transient Electronic System
nodes.description: Construct transient electronic devices whose constituent materials or layers dissolve, disperse, or resorb in water, biofluids, or culture conditions, with operation lasting for a reported or designed interval before degradation.
nodes.function: Provide finite-duration electronic operation without device retrieval or persistent material burden.
nodes.mechanism: Active, conductive, dielectric, substrate, and encapsulation materials are selected and dimensioned so the complete system disappears after use.

nodes.label: Geometric Strain-Accommodating Conductive Interconnect
nodes.description: Use geometrically compliant conductive paths or arrays to absorb substrate deformation through bending, unfolding, buckling, or curvature changes while preserving electrical continuity.
nodes.function: Route electrical signals or power between components across deformable platforms.
nodes.mechanism: Excess path length and compliant geometry convert macroscopic deformation into distributed geometric motion, limiting axial strain and stress in the conductor and attached devices.
failure_modes: Resonance shift from altered spacing or geometry

nodes.label: Graded-Index Antireflection Interface
nodes.description: Reduce optical reflection over broad wavelength and angular ranges by creating a gradual refractive-index transition at an optical surface.
nodes.function: Increase transmission and angular tolerance while reducing Fresnel reflection.
nodes.mechanism: A multilayer or depth-graded porous structure produces a refractive-index gradient that smooths the optical transition between media.
failure_modes: water filling pores and changing optical response

nodes.label: Heterogeneous Multicolor Quantum-Dot LED
nodes.description: Integrate distinct emissive quantum-dot populations in stacked or registered pixel geometries with compatible transport layers to tune multicolor electroluminescence.
nodes.function: Provide multicolor or spectrally tunable LED output.
nodes.mechanism: Different QD populations emit through stacked or spatially registered active regions; transport-layer alignment, injection resistance, and inter-population energy transfer determine spectral balance.
failure_modes: Higher resistance and reduced injected current
Suppressed emission from one QD population

nodes.label: Hierarchical Fractal Stretchable Interconnect
nodes.description: Use recursively self-similar conductive geometry to distribute deformation hierarchically and increase stretchability and compliance under stretching.
nodes.function: Provide compact, highly stretchable electrical routing with low conductor strain.
nodes.mechanism: Nested geometries buckle, bend, twist, and unravel sequentially from larger to smaller scales, increasing effective path length and deformation freedom.
design_handles: Height/spacing ratios at each fractal order
failure_modes: Irreversible entanglement or disorder under repeated overstrain

nodes.label: High-Capacitance Solid Gate Dielectric
nodes.description: Use a thin solid dielectric or dielectric bilayer with high areal capacitance and controlled leakage to gate thin-film semiconductors at low voltage.
nodes.function: Provide robust electrostatic gate coupling for thin-film devices.
nodes.mechanism: A high-capacitance insulating layer separates gate and semiconductor while supplying capacitive modulation with limited leakage.

nodes.label: Impedance-Based Contact and Tissue-State Readout
nodes.description: Infer contact, hydration, tissue state, or cell coverage from impedance changes produced by altered ionic conduction, capacitance, or tissue electrical properties.
nodes.function: Provide nonoptical readout of material contact and biological or tissue state.
nodes.mechanism: AC impedance reflects conductivity, permittivity, ionic access, and electrode-sample coupling, which change with contact, hydration, ablation, or cell coverage.
failure_modes: Sensitivity to contact interface and residual surface films

nodes.label: Local Sensor-Integrated Computing
nodes.description: Perform sensing and computation within the sensing node or material system to reduce data movement and enable local response.
nodes.function: Reduce communication burden and enable fast, energy-efficient local processing.
nodes.mechanism: Device physics, material state, or embedded computation performs adaptation, filtering, feature extraction, or inference at the sensing site.

nodes.label: In Vitro Cellular Compatibility Assessment
nodes.description: Assess material cytocompatibility using direct-contact and extract exposures with viability, apoptosis, attachment, proliferation, and morphology endpoints.
nodes.function: Identify cellular toxicity and compatibility of implant materials.
nodes.mechanism: Cultured cells are exposed to intact materials or dissolution extracts and evaluated with viability and morphology assays.
failure_modes: in-vitro results not predicting in-vivo response

nodes.label: In Vivo Physiological-Motion Energy Validation
nodes.description: Validate an implanted motion harvester by measuring output during multiple trotting behaviors over days 1–3 in mice, while assessing cardiac-device contact through contraction and relaxation.
nodes.function: Assess power generation, attachment stability, deployment compatibility, and durability under physiological motion.
nodes.mechanism: Implant or mount the harvester on or near a moving organ, vary motion or placement conditions, and record electrical output while assessing fixation and tissue/device interaction.

nodes.label: Responsive Indicator Optical Readout
nodes.description: Convert analyte- or stimulus-responsive indicator chemistry into a visible, colorimetric, or fluorescent signal that is interpreted optically and optionally calibrated quantitatively.
nodes.function: Provide low-complexity optical detection of chemical composition or environmental stimuli.
nodes.mechanism: A localized indicator or chromogenic reagent changes absorption, hue, intensity, or fluorescence after reacting with the target; visual or digital optical measurements map the response to the target quantity.

nodes.label: Individually Addressable Wireless Multichannel Stimulation
nodes.description: Use a wireless command and embedded-control layer to independently program multiple neural stimulation channels, sites, modalities, and timing parameters.
nodes.function: Provide real-time spatially and temporally resolved stimulation without wired tethering.
nodes.mechanism: RF, NFC, or digital commands update stored parameters; a local controller addresses selected actuator channels and executes synchronous or asynchronous programs.
failure_modes: Limited operating area or field nonuniformity

nodes.label: Injectable Multimodal Electronics
nodes.description: Combine multiple device modalities, including electrophysiological sensing and thermal measurements relevant to RF or cryoablation, with tissue-facing sensor placement when required.
nodes.function: Provide minimally invasive, colocated sensing and actuation at tissue depth.
nodes.mechanism: Thin flexible substrates or needles carry multiple sensor, emitter, or actuator modalities while supporting insertion and electrical readout.
failure_modes: Insufficient penetration without a guide needle
Mechanical interference if stiffness is excessive

nodes.label: Integrated Multianalyte Sweat Monitoring Platform
nodes.description: Combine sweat capture and routing, multiple biochemical assays, auxiliary physical sensing, and shared readout in one skin-interfaced platform.
nodes.function: Measure multiple biomarkers together with sweat dynamics or related physiological context.
nodes.mechanism: Shared or coordinated fluidic and sensing modules route sweat to distinct assay regions while electrochemical, optical, thermal, or motion channels provide complementary measurements.

nodes.label: Interface-Controlled Contact Injection
nodes.description: Control and interpret contact resistance by treating dielectric, electrode, semiconductor diameter, work function, and gate bias as determinants of injection barriers.
nodes.function: Explain and reduce contact-limited transport in field-effect devices.
nodes.mechanism: Chemical interactions and band alignment at dielectric/electrode/semiconductor interfaces alter Schottky-like barriers and make contact resistance dependent on interface chemistry, gate bias, work function, and element bandgap.
failure_modes: Barrier interpretation is confounded by contact geometry
Morphology or other parasitics dominate transport

nodes.label: Interfacial-Energy Block-Copolymer Morphology Model
nodes.description: Predict block-copolymer orientation and morphology by balancing surface and interfacial energies, chain entropy, and confinement geometry.
nodes.function: Explain and predict nonclassical block-copolymer morphologies near patterned or substrate boundaries.
nodes.mechanism: Candidate morphologies are evaluated by free-energy contributions from substrate and block wetting, block–block interfaces, chain stretching, polymer–air interfaces, and three-dimensional confinement.
failure_modes: qualitative rather than quantitatively predictive at high modeled surface energies

nodes.label: Electrically Assisted Biofluid Sampling
nodes.description: Generate localized biofluid on demand by electrically transporting a stimulant or secretagogue through skin before collection or sensing.
nodes.function: Decouple sample availability from spontaneous secretion, exercise, or ambient conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Controlled current drives a sweat-inducing agent across skin, producing localized fluid for downstream collection or sensing.

nodes.label: Island–Bridge Strain-Isolating Interconnect
nodes.description: Connect relatively rigid active islands with mechanically compliant bridges so substrate deformation is concentrated in the interconnects rather than the active regions.
nodes.function: Provide deformable electrical integration while protecting strain-sensitive device islands.
nodes.mechanism: Narrow, long, buckled, or otherwise compliant bridges provide geometric excess length and deform out of plane or laterally while stiffer islands remain comparatively low strain.

nodes.label: Relief-Structured Strain Isolation
nodes.description: Use raised, relatively stiff active-device islands separated by recessed compliant regions to localize deformation away from strain-sensitive elements.
nodes.function: Protect rigid or brittle active devices while enabling stretchable, high-coverage integration.
nodes.mechanism: Relief geometry and stiffness contrast concentrate strain in recessed trenches and interconnect regions while reducing strain on island tops.
failure_modes: interconnect metal fracture at large deformation

nodes.label: Laser-Assisted Thermal Material Transfer
nodes.description: Use localized optical heating at a donor or stamp interface to overcome adhesion and transfer a selected solid film or microstructure to a receiver.
nodes.function: Pattern or place solid materials by noncontact, additive thermal transfer.
nodes.mechanism: Absorbed laser energy generates interfacial vaporization, differential thermal expansion, or thermo-mechanical crack driving force that releases material toward a receiver.

nodes.label: Layered Thin-Source Thermal Modeling
nodes.description: Use analytical or finite-element thermal conduction models for thin heat-generating micro-LEDs, including axisymmetric, pulsed, or steady-state conditions, to predict temperature behavior under specified material and power parameters.
nodes.function: Estimate device, interface, and surrounding-medium temperatures and compare thermal designs.
nodes.mechanism: Represent the active source as a thin planar or equivalent axisymmetric source in a multilayer medium and solve steady or pulsed conduction with layer properties and interfacial continuity.
failure_modes: Breakdown of thin-source or axisymmetric approximation
Neglect of blood-flow heat loss in living tissue
accuracy degrades outside thin-device or large-substrate assumptions
localized gap temperature measurements can differ from active-device temperature
neglect of convection when it is non-negligible

nodes.label: Local Adaptive Sensor Analytics
nodes.description: Process sensor signals on-device or in-sensor and apply real-time feature aggregation or decision logic, with reduced transmission-bandwidth requirements under the stated operating conditions.
nodes.function: Extract actionable information and maintain reliable operation under resource constraints.
nodes.mechanism: Embedded filtering, feature extraction, adaptive baselines or thresholds, and local inference produce features, predictions, or control decisions before or alongside wireless transmission.

nodes.label: Localized Resistive Thermal Actuation
nodes.description: Generate localized heat by driving a resistive element with controlled electrical power.
nodes.function: Deliver a local thermal stimulus or thermal field.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical power dissipated in a conductive trace or resistor produces Joule heat; geometry, timing, and addressing shape the thermal field.

nodes.label: Low-Adhesion Pattern-Release Interface
nodes.description: Use a chemically inert, low-surface-energy or fluorinated patterning interface to reduce adhesion and enable nondestructive release from masters.
nodes.function: Improve mold release while preserving replicated pattern fidelity.
nodes.mechanism: Weak interfacial interactions and fluorinated surface chemistry lower adhesion between patterned elastomers and master or resist surfaces.
failure_modes: adhesion and pattern tearing without treatment
incomplete transfer if adhesion is too weak
potential loss of fidelity if treatment damages relief

nodes.label: Mechanically Guided 2D-to-3D Assembly
nodes.description: Transform a planar precursor into a designed three-dimensional architecture by applying programmed mechanical strain, constraint, or substrate relaxation.
nodes.function: Create deterministic 3D microsystems from planar precursors.
nodes.mechanism: Compression, buckling, delamination, or related mechanically induced deformation converts stored strain or imposed loading into controlled out-of-plane geometry.
failure_modes: Excessive strain in metal or polymer

nodes.label: Mechanics-Based Inverse Shape Design
nodes.description: Infer precursor geometry or actuation conditions from a target shape or strain profile using mechanics-based inverse design under stated approximations and constraints.
nodes.function: Generate layouts and material or loading parameters for target geometries.
nodes.mechanism: A forward mechanics model is iterated or analytically inverted to minimize deformation or strain error relative to a target.
failure_modes: High computational cost for nonlinear models

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Buckling and 3D Shape Design
nodes.description: Use analytical or nonlinear finite-element mechanics to predict and design buckling, postbuckling, or triggered transformation from planar structures to target three-dimensional geometries.
nodes.function: Select layouts and loading conditions that produce desired 3D shapes while controlling strain and instability.
nodes.mechanism: Nonlinear deformation and postbuckling calculations map planar geometry, loading, and material properties to final configuration and strain distribution.

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Curved-Array Mapping
nodes.description: Predict how planar arrays or layered structures map onto curved or transformed geometries, including element positions, strain, and displacement.
nodes.function: Guide geometry selection and validate placement and strain during planar-to-curved transformation.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical plate or layered mechanics and finite-element models map imposed deformation to spatial positions, curvature, and strain distributions.
failure_modes: Mismatch between ideal and fabricated geometry
Model error outside assumed deformation regime
Model mismatch from uncertain adhesion or material properties
Neglected local effects at detector/interconnect boundaries

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Fluidic Geometry Design
nodes.description: Use mechanics/FEA to evaluate fluidic or elastomeric geometry under imposed strain and identify designs with limited deformation, as demonstrated for selected geometries under uniaxial stretching.
nodes.function: Design mechanically stable fluidic structures and channels.
nodes.mechanism: Finite-element or continuum mechanics predicts deformation and volume change of elastomeric or compliant fluidic components under loading.

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Kirigami 3D Assembly
nodes.description: Transform patterned planar membranes into designed three-dimensional structures by combining compliant cuts or hinges, selective anchoring, compressive loading, and controlled release.
nodes.function: Create deterministic 3D architectures from planar thin-film precursors.
nodes.mechanism: Selective bonding transfers stored strain or compression to patterned, released regions, producing localized bending, buckling, translation, and rotation.

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Stretchable Layout Design
nodes.description: Use quantitative mechanics models to select stretchable layout geometry and materials while limiting strain, fracture, interference, or damage in functional layers.
nodes.function: Optimize flexible arrays, interconnects, and layered layouts for mechanical reliability and coverage.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical or finite-element strain and stress predictions guide geometric iteration, material selection, and constraint placement.

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Tissue and Interface Design
nodes.description: Use mechanics and anatomical or interface models to match device deformation, pressure, stress, or loading to tissue geometry and mechanical response.
nodes.function: Design conformal, low-trauma, tissue-compatible devices and interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Geometry, adhesion, stiffness, and loading are selected using continuum or finite-element models of tissue, contact, and interface behavior.
failure_modes: inaccurate prediction for strongly non-axisymmetric geometries

nodes.label: Model-Based Device Validation
nodes.description: Evaluate a physical or device model by comparing its predictions with independent numerical simulations, reference measurements, or experiments under matched conditions.
nodes.function: Test whether a proposed mechanism or model explains measured behavior.
nodes.mechanism: Generate predictions over controlled conditions and compare quantitative observables against simulation or experimental references.
failure_modes: Mismatch between bending approximation and nonlinear FEA mechanics

nodes.label: Multi-Configuration Thermal State Inference
nodes.description: Infer internal thermal states or layered thermal properties from multiple thermal measurements with deliberately different spatial, temporal, or environmental sensitivities.
nodes.function: Estimate subsurface temperature, convection, or layer-specific thermal properties.
nodes.mechanism: A thermal forward model maps measurements from sensors or configurations with distinct sensitivities to unknown states; the unknowns are solved by fitting the combined observations.
failure_modes: Error magnification in the inverse problem
Model error from unmodeled 3D heat conduction
thick superficial layer blocking deeper sensitivity

nodes.label: Multiband Mechano-Acoustic Monitoring
nodes.description: Use mechanically coupled inertial or vibration sensing across frequency bands and axes to derive physiological, behavioral, and acoustic observables from body motion and vibration.
nodes.function: Extract multiple vital-sign, activity, orientation, or acoustic features from mechanical signals.
nodes.mechanism: Accelerometers, IMUs, or vibration microphones capture low-frequency motion and higher-frequency mechanical or acoustic events; filtering and feature extraction separate observables.

nodes.label: Multilevel In-Vivo Intervention Validation
nodes.description: Validate an in-vivo intervention by combining local physiological measurements with independent anatomical, downstream, behavioral, thermal, or reference-system evidence.
nodes.function: Establish intervention mechanism, tissue response, signal fidelity, and functional consequence.
nodes.mechanism: Synchronized or matched measurements connect applied stimulation or therapy to local activity, downstream response, behavior, lesion ground truth, or wired-reference performance.

nodes.label: Multimodal Contact and Transport Diagnosis
nodes.description: Combine complementary electrical, spectroscopic, photoemission, and capacitance measurements to identify contact properties and distinguish transport pathways.
nodes.function: Diagnose barrier height, contact heterogeneity, functionalization effects, and active transport mechanisms.
nodes.mechanism: Different modalities weight electrical transport, optical excitation, spectral signatures, and depletion capacitance differently; their correlation constrains interpretation.
failure_modes: Contact or substrate changes confound electrical response.
Global conductance alone cannot identify the active pathway.

nodes.label: Multimodal Epidermal Monitoring
nodes.description: Use one attached wearable sensor to simultaneously measure heart rate, SpO2, skin temperature, sweat chloride, and blue-light exposure during exercise.
nodes.function: Measure multiple variables while reducing device count and preserving synchronized context.
nodes.mechanism: Distinct sensors or transduction modes share a mechanically integrated substrate, readout, and sometimes wireless link.
failure_modes: Different modalities retain different depth sensitivities
Surface residual films can affect impedance more strongly than thermal measurements

nodes.label: Nanotube-Enabled Semiconductor Contact
nodes.description: Use conjugated high-aspect-ratio nanotube or nanotube-polymer electrodes to reduce contact resistance and improve carrier injection into organic semiconductors.
nodes.function: Provide near-ohmic source/drain coupling to an organic semiconductor.
nodes.mechanism: Nanotube geometry and conjugated interfacial chemistry promote favorable morphology, field focusing, and reduced injection barriers at the semiconductor contact.
failure_modes: Contact resistance can become significant with roughness or nonuniform layers

nodes.label: Nanotube-FET Molecular Transduction
nodes.description: Convert molecular adsorption, binding, or surface-charge perturbation at a nanotube FET into a drain-current or transfer-characteristic change.
nodes.function: Provide electrical sensing of chemical or molecular interactions.
nodes.mechanism: Surface interactions alter carrier density, electrostatic gating, scattering, or contact coupling in a gate-controlled nanotube network.
failure_modes: Contact resistance can dominate apparent sensing response
contact-resistance modulation can confound channel-transduction interpretation
heterogeneity in tube diameter and length

nodes.label: Nanowire Heterojunction Photovoltaics
nodes.description: Use a semiconductor nanowire-array heterojunction solar-cell architecture to generate measurable photovoltaic output under illumination.
nodes.function: Generate photovoltaic current and voltage using nanowire heterojunctions.
nodes.mechanism: A rectifying p–n interface separates photocarriers while nanowire geometry enhances absorption and collection; radial junctions are a geometry-specific implementation variant.

nodes.label: Neutral-Plane Active-Layer Strain Management
nodes.description: Position strain-sensitive functional layers near the neutral mechanical plane of a multilayer structure, using layer stiffness and thickness to minimize deformation-induced strain and preserve function.
nodes.function: Protect brittle or strain-sensitive active layers and stabilize operation during bending, stretching, twisting, buckling, or pressure loading.
nodes.mechanism: The multilayer stiffness-thickness distribution places the active layer near the zero-axial-strain plane; compliant substrates, encapsulation, or interconnect geometries accommodate residual global deformation.
failure_modes: Active layer displaced from neutral plane
Active-layer strain exceeding fracture or performance limits

nodes.label: Neutral-Plane Strain Isolation
nodes.description: Place brittle or strain-sensitive functional layers near the neutral mechanical plane of a multilayer package to reduce bending-induced strain and improve bendability or fracture resistance.
nodes.function: Improve bend tolerance, fatigue stability, and mechanical reliability of thin functional layers and interconnects.
nodes.mechanism: Layer thicknesses and elastic properties are balanced so the neutral-plane location approaches the active layer, reducing tensile and compressive strain during curvature.
failure_modes: Active layer displaced from neutral plane
Neutral-plane shift caused by unmodeled interfaces or nonlinear behavior
active layer displaced from neutral plane

nodes.label: Near-Field Wireless Power-and-Data Systems
nodes.description: Use inductive near-field coupling to deliver power and exchange sensor or control data through a shared or coordinated NFC interface.
nodes.function: Enable battery-free or low-power sensing, actuation, multiplexed readout, and smartphone communication.
nodes.mechanism: Resonant magnetic coupling transfers RF energy and bidirectional data between an external reader and one or more embedded NFC nodes.
failure_modes: Data loss if buffering is inadequate

nodes.label: Noncoplanar Serpentine Strain Isolation
nodes.description: Use noncoplanar serpentine layouts to accommodate large substrate deformation while keeping device regions near low strain.
nodes.function: Isolate functional device elements from applied substrate strain.
nodes.mechanism: Out-of-plane deformation and serpentine compliance absorb extension, reducing strain transmitted to planar nodes or active regions.

nodes.label: Open Mesh Strain Accommodation
nodes.description: Accommodate large deformation by routing strain into compliant open-mesh or island-bridge geometries while limiting strain in functional regions.
nodes.function: Provide reversible stretchability and conformal compliance in distributed electronic systems.
nodes.mechanism: Openings, serpentine or fractal bridges, and compliant interconnects deform geometrically so global strain is absorbed without direct proportional strain in functional islands.

nodes.label: Optogenetic Neural Modulation
nodes.description: Deliver spatially and temporally controlled light to genetically sensitized neural populations to activate or inhibit neural function.
nodes.function: Produce targeted neural modulation in living tissue or freely moving subjects.
nodes.mechanism: Optical energy, supplied wirelessly or externally and delivered directly or through a converter, drives opsin-expressing cells to alter neural activity.

nodes.label: Overlapping Compliant Scale Covering
nodes.description: Use overlapping or imbricate scale layouts to combine reversible bending/stretchability with high or full areal coverage.
nodes.function: Provide deformable, high-coverage protective or functional surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Scale overlap changes during deformation while posts or compliant backing retain contact and coverage.
failure_modes: Scale contact with the substrate during concave bending

nodes.label: Passive LC Resonant Readout
nodes.description: A stimulus-responsive passive LC resonator converts changes in capacitance, inductance, or dielectric loading into a remotely interrogated resonance shift.
nodes.function: Provide battery-free wireless sensing.
nodes.mechanism: Stimulus-dependent L or C changes shift resonance, which an external inductive reader detects through impedance, phase, or frequency response.
failure_modes: drift from water permeation or material degradation

nodes.label: Percolation-Network Thin-Film Transistor
nodes.description: Use SWNT networks as semiconductor layers in top-gate thin-film transistors, with selective etching or patterning available to define electrically isolated regions.
nodes.function: Provide scalable field-effect switching with controlled network connectivity and reduced parasitic pathways.
nodes.mechanism: A percolating semiconducting network bridges source and drain while selective removal or isolation interrupts neighboring and metallic-only paths; gate bias modulates the remaining channel.
failure_modes: contact resistance domination at short channel lengths

nodes.label: Perforated Compliant Skin Interface
nodes.description: Use deliberate openings in a compliant skin-mounted device to reduce mechanical constraint and improve breathability and inspection access.
nodes.function: Support mechanically compliant, breathable, inspectable skin integration of flexible electronics.
nodes.mechanism: Distributed perforations interrupt the encapsulation or support layer, accommodating deformation and creating pathways for vapor transport and visual access while preserving device integration.
failure_modes: excessive water ingress or poor adhesion

nodes.label: Photocurable Post-Assembly Fixation
nodes.description: After an arrangement or transfer operation is complete, photocure the surrounding adhesive or matrix to convert temporary retention into a fixed structure.
nodes.function: Preserve a transiently assembled or transferred spatial arrangement.
nodes.mechanism: Post-assembly UV exposure polymerizes or crosslinks a photocurable medium, producing permanent bonds or a solid matrix around the arranged objects.
failure_modes: Insufficient exposure can leave the arrangement unstable

nodes.label: Photocurable Tissue–Device Adhesive Interface
nodes.description: Place a soft photocurable adhesive between a device and tissue, then cure it in situ to create a conformal, mechanically stable interface.
nodes.function: Anchor tissue-contacting electronics while reducing penetration and mechanical mismatch.
nodes.mechanism: A liquid precursor wets device and tissue surfaces and polymerizes under controlled illumination, forming a bonded conformal interface.

nodes.label: Physics-Based Model Inference and Calibration
nodes.description: Infer material, geometric, or device parameters from measured responses using an analytical or numerical physics-based model.
nodes.function: Estimate otherwise inaccessible parameters and calibrate predictive models.
nodes.mechanism: Map measured voltage, resonance, thermal, flow, or transport responses through a forward model and solve the inverse or fitting problem.

nodes.label: Piezoresistive Deformation Transduction
nodes.description: Convert mechanical deformation into resistance change by altering conductive-path geometry, separation, or connectivity in a compliant conductor.
nodes.function: Measure strain, pressure, motion, or organ expansion electrically.
nodes.mechanism: Deformation changes conductive-filler percolation or embedded-conductor geometry while an electrical circuit measures resistance.

nodes.label: Fluid-Pressure Membrane Deformation
nodes.description: Use fluid pressure to deform a compliant membrane carrying functional elements into a controlled curved geometry.
nodes.function: Actuate, tune, or set the curvature of integrated devices and membranes.
nodes.mechanism: Pressure in a sealed chamber stretches and deflects an elastomer against geometric constraints, producing a prescribed curved state.
failure_modes: high fill factor reduces achievable apex height
regions near constrained corners may remain flat

nodes.label: Polarization-Directed Laser Patterning
nodes.description: Control the orientation or geometry of laser-patterned structures by selecting polarization state and orientation relative to anisotropic material or mask features.
nodes.function: Use optical polarization as a design variable for directional or anisotropic pattern formation.
nodes.mechanism: Polarization-dependent absorption or mask response selectively changes ablation and exposure across oriented anisotropic features; circular polarization removes directional selectivity.
failure_modes: Angular mismatch beyond the ablation window prevents removal
Thermal or collateral damage at excessive exposure
Unwanted anisotropy when polarization-insensitive geometry is desired

nodes.label: Process-Decoupled Heterogeneous Integration
nodes.description: Fabricate or optimize functional materials and device elements under source-side conditions, then integrate them with a separately selected host substrate or subsystem.
nodes.function: Combine performance-optimized materials or processes with substrates and components that impose different thermal, mechanical, or chemical constraints.
nodes.mechanism: Source-side growth, patterning, or processing is decoupled from host assembly, allowing independent process windows and heterogeneous system construction.

nodes.label: Programmable Lorentz-Force Morphing
nodes.description: Program current distributions in a conductive network exposed to a magnetic field to generate spatially distributed Lorentz forces and controllable out-of-plane or three-dimensional deformation.
nodes.function: Produce programmable surface or membrane shape change from electrical control.
nodes.mechanism: Current density interacting with a magnetic field generates Lorentz force; force transfer through liquid-metal channels or conductive traces displaces a compliant mechanical structure.
failure_modes: Exceeding elastic limit can leave irreversible deformation

nodes.label: Programmed Transient Device Lifetime
nodes.description: Design transient devices for controlled dissolution, degradation, disintegration, resorption, or multistaged functional transformation through material, layer-thickness, and architecture choices.
nodes.function: Provide temporary operation with planned disappearance or reduced residual burden.
nodes.mechanism: Material composition, geometry, component sequencing, and encapsulation regulate environmental access and degradation kinetics.
failure_modes: insufficient dissolution due to solubility limits
loss of function before intended lifetime
