loss of function before target interval

nodes.label: Ray-Tracing Optical Transport Validation
nodes.description: Validate optical transport by tracing rays through measured or designed geometry and material properties, then comparing predicted observables with experiments.
nodes.function: Assess optical losses, efficiency, imaging, angular response, and design performance.
nodes.mechanism: Ray propagation accounts for relevant interface, absorption, dispersion, reflection, emission, or scattering behavior, and simulated observables are compared with measurements.
failure_modes: Mismatch between simulated and fabricated geometry
Unmodeled geometric contact or gap defects

nodes.label: Reactive-Diffusion Dissolution and Lifetime Modeling
nodes.description: Use reactive-diffusion models to describe or predict dissolution rates and remaining thickness of transient layers under specified aqueous or thermal conditions.
nodes.function: Estimate material loss, dissolution rate, and time to a defined physical or functional failure threshold.
nodes.mechanism: Water or other environmental species diffuse through one- or multilayer structures, react within the material, and generate thickness or resistance trajectories subject to boundary and interface conditions.
failure_modes: Ignoring intermediate eigenvalue regimes can substantially alter predicted thickness loss
Parameter transfer across environments without recalibration
Thin-layer approximation can be inaccurate for thick encapsulation
continuum approximation may not capture atomic-scale reactivity
extrapolation outside tested pH and temperature ranges

nodes.label: Recognition-Gated FET Chemical Sensing
nodes.description: Convert analyte recognition at a functionalized FET interface into threshold, transconductance, or current changes through binding-induced electrostatic gating.
nodes.function: Provide label-free electrical detection of chemical or biomolecular species.
nodes.mechanism: Recognition-induced charge or surface-potential changes modulate the semiconductor channel or gate electrostatics.

nodes.label: Rectification-Based Contact Validation
nodes.description: Assess contact symmetry and injection behavior by comparing electrical response under opposite bias polarities, optionally with illumination.
nodes.function: Validate ohmic, rectifying, or polarity-asymmetric contact behavior.
nodes.mechanism: Opposite-polarity sweeps reveal passing and blocking branches; similarity supports symmetric injection, while strong asymmetry indicates rectification or directional injection.

nodes.label: Reduced Mechanics Model Validation
nodes.description: Validate reduced deformation, strain, buckling, or stretchability models by comparing analytical predictions with finite-element fields and mechanical observations.
nodes.function: Assess whether simplified mechanics predicts deformation and failure behavior.
nodes.mechanism: Run analytical or reduced models and FEA under matched geometry and loading, then compare strain, shape, force, or failure metrics with experiments.
failure_modes: Agreement does not establish experimental confirmation.
Agreement limited to tested parameter range
Model discrepancy at very compliant crease or base regions

nodes.label: Redundant Sensing for Robustness
nodes.description: Acquire a target signal through multiple independent or mechanically differentiated sensing channels so estimates can be cross-checked, fused, or retained when one channel is corrupted.
nodes.function: Improve signal availability, artifact detection, and robustness of sensing.
nodes.mechanism: Parallel channels provide independent observations or a reference measurement for fusion, cancellation, or fallback under channel-specific disturbances.

nodes.label: Reference-Based Measurement Calibration
nodes.description: Map a device response to a quantitative measurand by acquiring calibration data alongside a reference standard or known state.
nodes.function: Convert raw sensor or optical output into calibrated physical, chemical, or physiological values.
nodes.mechanism: Measure candidate and reference responses over known conditions, then fit or apply a calibration relation.

nodes.label: Reference-Channel Differential Compensation
nodes.description: Use a reference channel, baseline, or auxiliary environmental measurement to subtract confounding variation from a primary sensor signal.
nodes.function: Improve measurement specificity and stability under thermal, positional, or coupling disturbances.
nodes.mechanism: Measure the confounder through a reference or auxiliary channel and compensate the primary response computationally or by differential subtraction.
failure_modes: Large local gradients at the reference site
Reference sensor receives substantially different environmental conditions
baseline site differs materially from target site

nodes.label: Reference-Normalized Optical Calibration
nodes.description: Normalize a sample-dependent optical signal using a stable co-located, co-imaged, or paired reference signal before quantitative calibration.
nodes.function: Reduce illumination, detector, geometry, loading, and baseline variability in optical measurements.
nodes.mechanism: A reference emitter, color marker, channel, chamber, background, or reference state experiences comparable measurement conditions; ratios, differences, or calibrated transformations suppress common-mode variation.

nodes.label: Reference-to-Replica Optical Fidelity Validation
nodes.description: Assess replication or assembly fidelity by comparing reference and replica structures using geometric or metrological checks and, where relevant, functional optical measurements.
nodes.function: Determine whether fabrication, replication, or assembly preserves structure and optical performance.
nodes.mechanism: Matched reference and counterpart samples are characterized geometrically and optically under comparable conditions, and discrepancies are quantified.
failure_modes: inability to resolve sub-3 nm widths

nodes.label: Registered Multinozzle Multimaterial Printing
nodes.description: Use multiple nozzles, including potentially individually addressable nozzle arrays, to print multiple materials or components.
nodes.function: Produce registered multimaterial arrays while increasing deposition throughput.
nodes.mechanism: Separate reservoirs and nozzles are individually addressed; nozzle placement, stage motion, timing, and optionally vision feedback control material deposition and overlay alignment.

nodes.label: Relief-Patterned Adhesion Optimization
nodes.description: Optimize patterned relief geometry and contact fraction to set effective adhesion and achieve a desired pickup-release contrast.
nodes.function: Design structured interfaces with prescribed adhesion regimes.
nodes.mechanism: Relief geometry changes contact area and deformation or collapse energy, thereby modifying the effective interfacial energy release rate.
failure_modes: Pickup and printing inequalities cannot be simultaneously satisfied

nodes.label: Optical Biofluid Readout
nodes.description: Collect biofluid in a wearable microfluidic structure and perform optical or colorimetric readout either on-body or after removal.
nodes.function: Enable quantitative chemical analysis with compact optical assays or external instruments.
nodes.mechanism: Fluorometric, spectroscopic, or colorimetric reagents produce measurable optical signals in reservoirs or collected samples.

nodes.label: Resistive Strain Transduction
nodes.description: Convert mechanical deformation into a measurable electrical resistance change through a strain-sensitive conductive or semiconductor element mechanically coupled to the target structure.
nodes.function: Sense mechanical strain, deformation, or motion using resistance readout.
nodes.mechanism: Strain changes the resistance of a conductive path or piezoresistive semiconductor through geometry, stress state, or carrier-response changes; calibrated resistance variation yields a strain estimate.
failure_modes: Mechanical constraint of the target organ
Reduced gauge factor from balanced tensile and compressive stresses

nodes.label: Resistive Thermal Sensing
nodes.description: Measure temperature by calibrating a temperature-dependent electrical resistance or voltage response of a conductive element.
nodes.function: Convert local temperature into an electrical measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Temperature-dependent resistance, characterized by a temperature coefficient or calibration relation, produces a measurable resistance or bridge-output change.

nodes.label: Resistive Thermal Flow Sensing
nodes.description: Infer fluid flow from flow-dependent heat transport generated by a controlled thermal perturbation and measured through temperature or resistance changes.
nodes.function: Measure local flow magnitude, direction, or presence without a dedicated mechanical velocity element.
nodes.mechanism: A resistive heater or heated resistive element creates a thermal field; convection changes temperature spatially or temporally; calibrated temperature or resistance signals are mapped to flow.

nodes.label: Resistive Thermal Field Mapping
nodes.description: Use arrays of temperature-sensitive sensors for spatial thermal mapping, with voltage-to-temperature calibration demonstrated for thin-film thermal sensors.
nodes.function: Measure spatially resolved temperature on surfaces, tissues, or fluidic structures.
nodes.mechanism: Local temperature changes alter resistance through the temperature coefficient of resistance; individually addressed or multiplexed elements are calibrated and spatially assembled into a thermal map.
failure_modes: Diffusivity is less precisely fitted than conductivity
Layered geometry and convection require calibration

nodes.label: Wireless Electromagnetic Power Transfer
nodes.description: Transfer usable electrical power wirelessly from an external RF or magnetic transmitter to a compact receiver for untethered operation of an implant or microscale device.
nodes.function: Provide battery-free power across a tissue or environmental gap.
nodes.mechanism: An external transmitter couples electromagnetic energy into a tuned receiver coil or antenna; rectification, regulation, and optional modulation produce device power.

nodes.label: Reusable Mold Replication
nodes.description: Replicate patterned geometries through reusable masters or elastomeric molds followed by curing and release of a replica material.
nodes.function: Fabricate repeated patterned structures with reduced tooling cost and wear on the original master.
nodes.mechanism: A patterned master or secondary stamp defines a mold; a curable material fills or contacts the relief, cures, and is released as a faithful replica.

nodes.label: Reversible Adhesive Transfer Printing
nodes.description: Control pickup and release of fragile structures by mechanically switching adhesion at a compliant elastomeric stamp interface.
nodes.function: Transfer discrete structures between donor and receiver substrates with controlled adhesion.
nodes.mechanism: Stamp geometry and loading alter contact area, crack propagation, stress localization, or viscoelastic recovery to produce distinct pickup and release states.
failure_modes: Adhesion loss from viscoelastic rate effects
insufficient stress localization with wider posts
pad bowing from residual curing stress

nodes.label: Reversible Soft Contact Lamination
nodes.description: Form, use, release, and re-form an intimate conformal electrical or measurement interface through soft adhesion without permanent bonding or aggressive processing.
nodes.function: Enable nondestructive assembly, repeated measurement, and reconfiguration of fragile or compliant devices.
nodes.mechanism: An elastomeric or compliant contact surface wets and conforms to the target; van der Waals or weak interfacial adhesion establishes contact that can be actively peeled and reattached.

nodes.label: Sacrificial Corrosion Indicator for Barrier Validation
nodes.description: Place a water-reactive sacrificial conductor beneath a barrier and detect its optical or electrical degradation to estimate ingress and barrier lifetime.
nodes.function: Rapidly screen, compare, and time water-barrier breakthrough.
nodes.mechanism: Permeating water corrodes or dissolves the indicator, producing visible morphology changes, resistance change, or disconnection; the first defined signal marks an operational lifetime.
failure_modes: inability to distinguish bulk from pinhole failure
indicator response after an already-existing defect

nodes.label: Sacrificial-Layer Release for Device Transfer
nodes.description: Use a selectively removable sacrificial layer to free fabricated device elements for subsequent transfer or integration.
nodes.function: Release device layers while preserving their functional structure and enabling reuse or relocation.
nodes.mechanism: Selective chemical or physical removal undercuts or dissolves the sacrificial layer, producing free-standing device elements that can be transferred.

nodes.label: Sacrificial-Release Semiconductor Structures
nodes.description: Fabricate transferable or suspended semiconductor microstructures by patterning a functional layer and selectively removing an underlying sacrificial or support layer.
nodes.function: Produce free-standing, tethered, or transferable semiconductor membranes and microelements for later device integration.
nodes.mechanism: Define geometry by lithography or templating, shape the functional semiconductor or coating, then selectively etch or dissolve the sacrificial support while preserving intended anchors or handling supports.

nodes.label: Sacrificial-Tether Registration
nodes.description: Retain partially released patterned elements with sacrificial bridges, anchors, or tethers until controlled pickup to preserve donor-defined position and orientation.
nodes.function: Maintain registration and prevent premature motion or loss during release and transfer preparation.
nodes.mechanism: Selective etching removes support beneath the active structure while designed attachment regions remain intact and fracture or detach under controlled transfer forces.

nodes.label: Selective-Bond Island–Bridge Strain Isolation
nodes.description: Use differential bonding to anchor functional islands while allowing compliant interconnects to buckle out of plane and absorb deformation.
nodes.function: Integrate strain-sensitive devices into highly stretchable circuits.
nodes.mechanism: Strongly bonded islands remain constrained while weakly bonded, sufficiently long interconnects lift or buckle under prestrain release and subsequent deformation.
failure_modes: island fracture under highly localized folding

nodes.label: Selective Thermal-Exposure Array Purification
nodes.description: Use material-selective localized heating to expose one class in a heterogeneous array and remove the exposed class by etching or ablation.
nodes.function: Purify mixed one-dimensional conductor arrays while preserving the retained material class and spatial alignment.
nodes.mechanism: Differential electrical, microwave, or optical absorption generates localized heating; thermocapillary flow or direct ablation exposes or removes the targeted members.

nodes.label: Separated Sensor–Electronics Architecture
nodes.description: Place tissue-matched sensing elements near the target while relocating power, processing, and communication electronics to a remote module connected by compliant wired or wireless links.
nodes.function: Reduce local tissue burden and improve placement of hard electronics.
nodes.mechanism: A sensor head and electronics base are partitioned spatially and coupled through flexible interconnects or wireless communication.

nodes.label: Sequential Multilayer Functional Integration
nodes.description: Construct multilayer functional architectures by repeatedly adding or transferring layers, with bonding or engineered interconnects used to preserve continuity between layers.
nodes.function: Create multilayer, stacked, or three-dimensional functional systems.
nodes.mechanism: Patterned layers are sequentially transferred, printed, laminated, or bonded; interlayer adhesion, dielectric isolation, cold welding, and registration maintain structural and functional coupling.

nodes.label: Sequential Dry Multilayer Integration
nodes.description: Construct multilayer devices by sequential dry transfer, ablation, or patterning of solid or preformed layers; registration is demonstrated in some implementations.
nodes.function: Integrate heterogeneous patterned layers while avoiding wet-layer incompatibility.
nodes.mechanism: Solid donor layers or prepared films are transferred and registered through repeated pickup, ablation, lamination, or deposition cycles.

nodes.label: Sequential Passive Fluid Sampling
nodes.description: Use passive pressure-thresholded valves or related delayed flow controls to fill separate reservoirs sequentially with limited mixing.
nodes.function: Provide time- or volume-resolved sampling without requiring continuously powered valves.
nodes.mechanism: Geometry-defined capillary bursting thresholds or passive flow delays activate collection paths sequentially and reduce temporal mixing.
failure_modes: incomplete assay stabilization before subsequent valve bursts

nodes.label: Sequential Threshold-Valve Fluid Routing
nodes.description: Use pressure- or absorption-triggered valves to route fluid through spatially separated chambers in a controlled sequence.
nodes.function: Encode time or volume information and reduce mixing between sequential samples.
nodes.mechanism: Valves with ordered burst pressures or swelling-driven closure redirect incoming fluid after a reservoir fills.
failure_modes: backflow or reagent washout if closure fails

nodes.label: Shared-Instrument Sequential Channel Readout
nodes.description: Sequentially connect multiple measurement channels to one shared instrument and reconstruct channel-specific outputs from the time-ordered measurements.
nodes.function: Reduce duplicated acquisition hardware while retaining distributed channel access.
nodes.mechanism: A multiplexer or relay selects one channel at a time, routes shared excitation or measurement circuitry, and time-orders the resulting signals.

nodes.label: Short-Channel Contact Effects
nodes.description: As channel dimensions shrink, series contact resistance becomes a larger fraction of total resistance and biases apparent transport performance.
nodes.function: Guide channel scaling and interpretation of short-channel measurements.
nodes.mechanism: Length-independent contact resistance dominates as channel resistance decreases with physical channel length, producing an effective added length and distorted extracted mobility.
failure_modes: Operating regime is outside the fitted model
mistaking contact-limited mobility for intrinsic mobility

nodes.label: Conformal Biointegrated Electronic Platform
nodes.description: Use a thin, soft or mechanically compliant electronic sensor platform that conformally integrates with skin for continuous or wireless physiological measurement.
nodes.function: Provide unobtrusive body-integrated electronics for sensing, actuation, communication, and monitoring.
nodes.mechanism: Ultrathin or stretchable active elements and interconnects are combined with compliant substrates, encapsulation, and skin interfaces to accommodate body motion.

nodes.label: Skin-Coupled Mechanoacoustic Monitoring
nodes.description: Use a conformal skin-coupled inertial or multimodal sensing platform to acquire body motion and tissue-conducted acoustic-mechanical signals across complementary frequency bands for physiological or behavioral inference.
nodes.function: Provide unobtrusive multimodal monitoring of body motion, vibration, and physiological sounds.
nodes.mechanism: Direct mechanical coupling transfers low- and high-frequency body vibrations to accelerometers and, where needed, coordinated microphones; bandwidth-aware processing separates signals and wireless links support untethered monitoring.
failure_modes: Insufficient IMU sensitivity for subtle sounds

nodes.label: Soft-Hard Functional Composite Integration
nodes.description: Integrate rigid high-performance functional phases with compliant soft phases to combine functional performance with deformability or conformal deployment.
nodes.function: Enable multifunctional systems that unite hard-phase performance with soft-phase compliance.
nodes.mechanism: Contrasting constituent properties distribute functional and mechanical roles across a stable soft–hard interface; the mismatch can be managed or exploited for system performance.

nodes.label: Soft Mechanoacoustic Monitoring
nodes.description: Use a soft, conformal sensor to capture mechanical or acoustic signals from moving body surfaces.
nodes.function: Monitor motion, swallowing, respiration, cardiac mechanics, vibration, or touch-related signals.
nodes.mechanism: Flexible accelerometers, strain elements, or acoustic transducers couple to skin motion and transmit or process the resulting signals.
failure_modes: insufficient temperature accuracy in short measurements

nodes.label: Soft Multilayer Multichannel Microfluidic Probe
nodes.description: Use bonded thin elastomeric layers with independently addressable channels to route fluids to localized outlets in a compliant probe.
nodes.function: Deliver one or more fluids through a thin conformal interface.
nodes.mechanism: Molded or patterned elastomer layers are aligned, bonded, and connected to reservoirs through vertical and horizontal channels.

nodes.label: Soft Neural Interface
nodes.description: Provide a mechanically compliant interface for bidirectional electronic measurement or stimulation of neural tissue.
nodes.function: Record from or stimulate neural systems while accommodating tissue motion and reducing mechanical mismatch.
nodes.mechanism: Soft, low-bending-stiffness probes or implanted platforms couple electrodes or optoelectronic elements to tissue.

nodes.label: Compliant Protective Encapsulation
nodes.description: Combine fluid protection with a soft, conformal outer interface that matches tissue mechanics and supports prolonged wear or implantation.
nodes.function: Protect device components while reducing tissue irritation, motion mismatch, and interface damage.
nodes.mechanism: Thin barrier layers isolate fluids while soft elastomeric overcoats provide compliance, modulus matching, and conformal contact.

nodes.label: Solution-Based Selective SWCNT Sorting
nodes.description: Separate or enrich target SWCNT electronic or structural classes in liquid using selective polymer/surfactant interactions, buoyant-density differences, or chromatographic partitioning, with optional selector removal.
nodes.function: Increase semiconducting SWCNT purity while preserving compatibility with downstream deposition or device fabrication.
nodes.mechanism: Chemical selectors interact differentially with nanotube geometry or electronic type, enabling fractionation; degradable selectors can subsequently be removed to yield cleaner nanotubes.
failure_modes: Polymer is too stiff to conformally wrap
Residual polymer increases inter-tube or contact resistance

nodes.label: Sparse-Array Optical Concentration
nodes.description: Use a registered or optically coupled concentrator architecture to redirect incident light from sparse array area onto microscale photovoltaic or optoelectronic receivers.
nodes.function: Increase local optical flux and useful output while exploiting sparse microcell placement.
nodes.mechanism: Lenslet, waveguide-reflector, or reflective parabolic elements collect light from gaps or broad apertures and deliver it to registered microcell active areas.

nodes.label: Spatially Programmed Porous-Silicon Optical Gradient
nodes.description: Program spatial refractive-index or optical-thickness gradients in porous silicon by controlling geometry and local electrochemical formation conditions.
nodes.function: Create position-dependent optical resonance or three-dimensional GRIN elements.
nodes.mechanism: Semiconductor topography defines the etch path while local or time-varying current density controls porosity, refractive index, and optical thickness.
failure_modes: Etch-rate variation can compromise uniform geometries.

nodes.label: Spatially Uniform Wireless Activation
nodes.description: Use a double-loop antenna arrangement to achieve stable, uniform wireless illumination across multiple designated locations under specified operating conditions.
nodes.function: Reduce position- and orientation-dependent loss of activation or harvested power.
nodes.mechanism: Multiple or spatially arranged transmit antennas create overlapping radiation or magnetic fields whose coverage is evaluated across receiver positions and orientations.

nodes.label: Stiffened Compliant Relief Stamp
nodes.description: Combine a stiff relief-forming layer or dimensionally stable backing with a compliant elastomeric contact layer to preserve patterned geometry while enabling handling, conformal contact, and release.
nodes.function: Improve relief fidelity, dimensional stability, and practical contact of reusable soft stamps and molds.
nodes.mechanism: The stiff layer or backing suppresses in-plane deformation, sagging, thermal distortion, or relief collapse, while the compliant layer preserves conformability and controlled release.

nodes.label: Stimulus-Responsive Colorimetric Readout
nodes.description: Convert a target-triggered molecular or material state change into a visually measurable color transition.
nodes.function: Provide simple optical detection of biological or chemical stimuli.
nodes.mechanism: Stimulus-induced molecular activation or conformational change alters chromophore conjugation and visible color.

nodes.label: Stimulus-Responsive Bilayer Actuation
nodes.description: Encode differential stimulus response in bonded or printed layers so external stimulation produces predictable folding, rolling, or shape change.
nodes.function: Transform planar multilayer precursors into responsive three-dimensional forms.
nodes.mechanism: Mismatch in swelling, thermal expansion, or programmed strain generates curvature and folding.
failure_modes: insufficient bending force to overcome substrate friction
slow recovery when contraction densifies the layer

nodes.label: Deformation-Accommodating Stretchable Antenna
nodes.description: Use antenna geometries whose deformation is accommodated by lateral-spring or serpentine restructuring rather than direct increase of the conductive path length.
nodes.function: Support wireless communication or inductive coupling on deformable platforms.
nodes.mechanism: Serpentine or lateral-spring conductor geometries redistribute deformation while preserving electrical continuity and antenna operation.
failure_modes: loss from substrate or body loading
metal cracking under direct tensile strain
resonant-frequency shift from geometry or tissue loading

nodes.label: Compliant Active-Electronics Integration
nodes.description: Integrate active electronic or optoelectronic elements with compliant materials and deformation-accommodating structures so sensing, actuation, or interconnection remains functional on curved or moving surfaces.
nodes.function: Provide deformable electronic functionality at compliant or biological interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Active elements are embedded, supported, or interconnected by elastomeric, polymeric, mesh, buckled, or otherwise compliant structures that accommodate applied deformation while preserving electrical function.

nodes.label: Multimodal Physiological State Inference
nodes.description: Time-synchronized multimodal sensors and multiparametric algorithms can support comprehensive physiological or behavioral monitoring; joint feature-level fusion for state estimation is not established by the supplied excerpts.
nodes.function: Improve state inference beyond isolated modality pipelines.
nodes.mechanism: Distinct modalities or sensing channels are co-registered or time-aligned, transformed into features, and jointly interpreted or classified.

nodes.label: Temperature-Compensated Resistive Readout
nodes.description: Use a measured, suitably coupled temperature channel to correct temperature-dependent resistive or conductivity measurements before estimating the target quantity.
nodes.function: Reduce thermal bias and drift in quantitative resistive sensing.
nodes.mechanism: A calibration model or correction factor maps the measured electrical response and temperature to a reference-temperature-equivalent estimate.

nodes.label: Temporal Channel Multiplexing
nodes.description: Assign distinguishable time windows or switching patterns to multiple channels so a shared detector or readout path can recover channel-specific signals.
nodes.function: Share readout infrastructure without simultaneous channel contention.
nodes.mechanism: Channel excitation or access is scheduled in distinct time slots or frequencies and the shared output is demultiplexed by timing or spectral separation.

nodes.label: Thermal Anisotropy Normalization
nodes.description: Normalize directional temperature differences by an actuator, reference, or common thermal state to separate flow-dependent information from common-mode heating.
nodes.function: Make thermal-flow measurements comparable across actuation and ambient conditions and support flow-rate or regime estimation.
nodes.mechanism: Compute upstream/downstream or sensor/reference temperature differences and normalize them against actuator or reference temperature, often pairing directional and mean features.

nodes.label: Thermal Flow Inversion
nodes.description: Infer vascular flow or perfusion from measured thermal responses using a calibrated heat-transfer model that links flow-dependent heat removal to temperature.
nodes.function: Convert surface or near-surface temperature dynamics into flow-related quantities.
nodes.mechanism: Solve conductive and flow-dependent convective or perfusive heat transfer, then fit model parameters to transient or steady-state thermal measurements.
failure_modes: confounding between fluid content and velocity
large sensor-heater distance causing high relative error

nodes.label: Thermal-Isolating Encapsulation
nodes.description: Add an insulating or phase-change encapsulation layer to reduce heat transfer or thermally induced noise between a device and its environment.
nodes.function: Limit tissue heating and thermal interference during operation.
nodes.mechanism: Low-conductivity or phase-changing layers increase thermal resistance and buffer transient heat flow.

nodes.label: Thermal Isolation Barrier
nodes.description: Place an insulating or phase-change barrier between a heat source and a protected interface to reduce heat transfer during overheating.
nodes.function: Reduce thermal exposure and burn risk at contacted interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Insulating layers impede conduction, while phase-change materials absorb heat or increase thermal resistance.

nodes.label: Thermal Model Validation Architectures
nodes.description: Validate or calibrate thermal and coupled thermomechanical models by comparing analytical predictions, finite-element results, and measurements across controlled operating conditions.
nodes.function: Assess model adequacy and identify thermal design limits.
nodes.mechanism: Compare predicted temperature, heat-flow, deformation, or safety metrics with numerical and experimental references, optionally fitting uncertain parameters.
failure_modes: Mismatch between experimental and modeled heating conditions

nodes.label: Thermal Model–Measurement Validation
nodes.description: Validate modeled thermal behavior by comparing analytical or numerical temperature predictions with spatial or temporal measurements under defined operating conditions.
nodes.function: Bound model error and assess operating temperature or thermal cross-talk.
nodes.mechanism: Compare measured thermal maps or histories with analytical, superposed, or finite-element predictions for the same geometry, power, and boundary conditions.
failure_modes: model mismatch in tissue or boundary conditions
unmodeled convection or biological heat transfer

nodes.label: Thermal Time-Series Physiological-State Inference
nodes.description: Infer inflammatory or rejection-related states in murine tissues from transient, longitudinal, and frequency-domain features of local temperature time series.
nodes.function: Convert thermal time series into early disease-state indicators or warnings.
nodes.mechanism: Feature extraction using transient-event, daily-minimum, wavelet, or FFT analyses relates temperature dynamics to validated biological state.
failure_modes: temperature features may be affected by surgery, analgesia, ambient conditions, motion, or medication

nodes.label: Thermally Reconfigurable Optical Relief
nodes.description: Use thermal transitions in a polymer optical relief to erase, program, or recover surface geometry and its optical function.
nodes.function: Control the reversibility and lifecycle of optically functional surface relief.
nodes.mechanism: Heating enables polymer relaxation or shape-memory recovery; backbone crosslinking can stabilize written relief against unwanted thermal erasure.

nodes.label: Programmable Thermal and Haptic Feedback
nodes.description: Generate programmable thermal stimulation and vibration patterns at a skin-compatible interface.
nodes.function: Deliver spatially and temporally controlled thermal cues.
nodes.mechanism: Thermal actuators change skin temperature under electrical control; optional mechanical actuators add vibratory cues.

nodes.label: Resonant Optical Temperature Sensing
nodes.description: Sense local temperature from temperature-dependent resonance or lasing wavelength shifts in silicon Fabry–Pérot or dye-doped cholesteric optical cavities.
nodes.function: Provide spectrally resolved, electrically isolated temperature measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Temperature changes refractive index, photonic pitch, or another resonant optical property, shifting the resonance or emission wavelength detected spectrally.

nodes.label: Thermocapillary Thin-Film Flow Modeling
nodes.description: Couple localized heat transport with thin-film lubrication dynamics to predict thermocapillary film evolution and feature geometry.
nodes.function: Guide thermal-flow process conditions and interpret trench or film measurements.
nodes.mechanism: A heat-source model predicts temperature gradients; temperature-dependent surface tension drives a lubrication-model film-thickness evolution, often expressed with dimensionless scaling parameters.
failure_modes: approximation breakdown outside essentially unidirectional flow
invalidity when central film thickness reaches zero
poorly known viscosity or surface tension

nodes.label: Thermocapillary Trench Formation
nodes.description: Convert localized heating of a thin mobile film into a self-aligned trench or opening through temperature-dependent surface-tension-driven flow.
nodes.function: Create registered nanoscale openings or relief features over localized heat sources.
nodes.mechanism: A thermal gradient changes surface tension, driving lateral viscous flow away from the heated region and forming displaced ridges and an exposed trench.
failure_modes: complete depletion of film at the heated center
excessive viscosity or insufficient processing time
insufficiently low viscosity for appreciable flow
trench width too large for dense arrays

nodes.label: Thickness-Dependent Quantum Confinement
nodes.description: Use sub-10-nm semiconductor thickness to alter dimensionality-dependent electronic transport and optical band-gap behavior through thickness effects and quantum confinement.
nodes.function: Explain or guide thickness-dependent transport, switching, and optical response.
nodes.mechanism: Reducing thickness confines carriers or excitations and shifts the dominant transport or optical regime away from bulk-like behavior.
failure_modes: surface-state or termination effects complicating bandgap assignment

nodes.label: Thin-Film Buckling Mechanics Model
nodes.description: Predict buckling wavelength and amplitude of a stiff thin film or beam on a compliant substrate from film/substrate properties, thickness, and strain using analytical or finite-element mechanics.
nodes.function: Guide deformation-mode selection, geometry design, and strain or stretchability estimation.
nodes.mechanism: Coupled film bending, membrane, and substrate elastic energies are represented analytically or numerically and minimized to obtain equilibrium wavelength, amplitude, mode, and strain.
failure_modes: Inadequate profile for very long inactivated regions
disagreement between thermal and actual film strain
fracture when predicted peak strain exceeds material limit
long herringbone wavelength may be energetically weakly selected

nodes.label: Threshold-Based Exposure Decision and Reporting
nodes.description: Use a predefined exposure threshold to classify or trigger reporting of accumulated measurements.
nodes.function: Reduce communication and energy demand while reporting actionable exposure states or dose values.
nodes.mechanism: An accumulated or instantaneous exposure signal is compared with a threshold; crossing it initiates classification, output conditioning, or wireless transmission.
design_handles: Channels affected by the state rule
failure_modes: Loss of valid channel data during state suppression
Threshold not representative of the deployment environment

nodes.label: Top-Down Anisotropic Semiconductor Element Fabrication
nodes.description: Define semiconductor wire or ribbon geometry by lithographic masking and anisotropic etching of a bulk crystalline wafer.
nodes.function: Fabricate ordered, dimensionally controlled semiconductor wires, ribbons, or related released structures.
nodes.mechanism: A patterned mask exposes selected crystal regions; crystallographic etch-rate anisotropy removes the surrounding material and can undercut or release the defined elements while retaining anchors or registration features.
failure_modes: Loss of registration if connection points are removed prematurely

nodes.label: Top-Down Semiconductor Microelement Release
nodes.description: Pattern and etch bulk crystalline wafer material to create freestanding semiconductor ribbons or microelements, with selective undercutting where applicable.
nodes.function: Create deterministic, transferable crystalline microstructures from wafer-scale films or devices.
nodes.mechanism: Lithographic masks define the elements; dry or anisotropic etching shapes the film or wafer; selective undercutting removes the sacrificial support while anchors preserve registration until transfer.

nodes.label: SWNT-Network Thin-Film Transistor
nodes.description: Use a transferred single-walled carbon-nanotube network as the semiconducting channel of a flexible gated thin-film transistor.
nodes.function: Switch and modulate current in a flexible transistor.
nodes.mechanism: Gate bias electrostatically modulates transport through a connected nanotube network between source and drain electrodes.

nodes.label: Transient Bioelectronic Lifecycle Validation
nodes.description: Evaluate temporary bioelectronic systems across functional operation, degradation or resorption, mechanical integrity, and biological or physiological response over the intended deployment lifecycle.
nodes.function: Establish retained function, lifecycle behavior, safety, and application-level feasibility of transient bioelectronic systems.
nodes.mechanism: Coordinate electrical or functional measurements with mechanical, aqueous degradation, material-disappearance, cellular, tissue, animal, or application-level assessments, using defined stages, controls, and endpoints.
failure_modes: Failure criterion dependent on measurement choice
Failure to separate function loss from material disappearance
False functional pass from device output without tissue capture

nodes.label: Transient Energy Subsystem
nodes.description: Transient energy components can exhibit finite operation or output under physiological conditions and undergo subsequent dissolution or bioresorption under specified conditions.
nodes.function: Power transient electronic systems without persistent energy hardware.
nodes.mechanism: Water-soluble or bioresorbable electrodes, dielectrics, separators, and active layers deliver energy before degradation.

nodes.label: Transient Resorbable Fluid Barrier
nodes.description: Use degradable or bioresorbable materials as temporary biofluid barriers, with functional lifetime and resorption timing governed by material chemistry and, for some encapsulants, composition and thickness.
nodes.function: Protect transient implants for a prescribed operating lifetime while avoiding permanent encapsulation.
nodes.mechanism: Hydrophobicity, composition, thickness, and multilayer structure regulate water penetration, degradation, and barrier lifetime.

nodes.label: Transient Sensing and Therapeutic Platform
nodes.description: Use degradable materials to assemble functional devices that dissolve after a predetermined operating duration; implantable examples can provide wireless, sensing, or therapeutic functions over finite intervals.
nodes.function: Provide temporary biomedical intervention or monitoring without retrieval surgery.
nodes.mechanism: Transient materials and packaging support the required function, then dissolve or bioresorb in vivo.

nodes.label: Transient Thermal Property Inference
nodes.description: Infer effective thermal conductivity, diffusivity, or related transport properties from a calibrated temperature response to controlled thermal excitation.
nodes.function: Translate a heating or cooling transient into thermal-property estimates.
nodes.mechanism: Apply known power, measure temperature over time, and fit or solve a calibrated transient heat-transfer model.

nodes.label: Vertical Layer Electrical Interconnect
nodes.description: Connect conductors on vertically separated device layers by forming aligned openings through insulating or planarizing layers and bridging them with conductive material.
nodes.function: Provide electrical paths between stacked circuit levels.
nodes.mechanism: Patterned or etched openings expose buried contacts; deposited metal or conductive fill bridges the openings and connects the layers.

nodes.label: Optical Tissue Oxygenation Readout
nodes.description: Estimate tissue oxygenation or hemoglobin variation from wavelength-dependent illumination and scattered or reflected optical detection interpreted through a tissue-absorption model.
nodes.function: Monitor local tissue oxygenation and perfusion state.
nodes.mechanism: Red and near-infrared light interrogate tissue; wavelength- and geometry-dependent optical signals are detected and converted into hemoglobin or oxygen-saturation estimates.
failure_modes: Adhesive or encapsulation durability in clinical use remains unvalidated
Local tissue heterogeneity can cause interdevice differences
Optical scattering assumptions can reduce StO2 precision
Potential tissue or hematoma effects not represented by the model

nodes.label: Geometric Waviness Strain Accommodation
nodes.description: Convert substrate deformation into changes in out-of-plane waviness or buckling so a stiff functional layer undergoes substantially less material strain than the supporting structure.
nodes.function: Enable stretchable or compressible integration of strain-intolerant thin films and membranes.
nodes.mechanism: A thin stiff layer is bonded to, or conformed with, a compliant substrate; prestrain release or prefabricated relief creates excess geometric length that unfolds or changes curvature under applied deformation.
failure_modes: Fracture of the functional layer if geometric accommodation is insufficient
Interfacial delamination when bonding is inadequate
film yielding when maximum strain exceeds critical strain

nodes.label: Wearable State Feedback
nodes.description: Use wearable sensing and state interpretation to provide user-facing feedback, alerts, or conditional intervention.
nodes.function: Translate continuously measured physiological or mechanical state into actionable feedback.
nodes.mechanism: Wearable measurements are processed using thresholds or inference models and routed to haptic, visual, auditory, or therapeutic outputs.

nodes.label: Wearable Ultrasonic Deep-Tissue Mapping
nodes.description: Use stretchable ultrasound arrays for deep-tissue beam focusing or steering, and use wearable ultrasound measurements of vessel dynamics to infer hemodynamic state such as blood pressure.
nodes.function: Provide noninvasive deep-tissue sensing on curved or moving biological surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Ultrasound transmission and echo reception resolve tissue or vessel structures; array control can steer and focus beams, while calibrated models convert temporal or spatial echo information into tissue maps or physiological estimates.

nodes.label: Wireless Implantable Optical Stimulation
nodes.description: Use externally powered and controlled implanted optical emitters to deliver localized stimulation or photochemical activation.
nodes.function: Provide programmable optical actuation at implanted biological sites without an onboard battery.
nodes.mechanism: Near-field wireless power and control drive implanted microscale light emitters through compliant implanted circuitry.

nodes.label: Wireless Optofluidic Neural Intervention
nodes.description: Coordinate wireless optical stimulation and localized fluid or drug delivery through a compact implantable neural interface.
nodes.function: Provide programmable spatially co-localized optical and pharmacological intervention in freely moving subjects.
nodes.mechanism: Wireless power and commands operate optical emitters and independently addressable fluidic reservoirs or pumps integrated with a compliant probe.

nodes.label: Wireless Skin-Integrated Electronics
nodes.description: Provide wireless power, data transfer, or control in a soft body-conformal electronic platform.
nodes.function: Enable untethered sensing, monitoring, actuation, and user interaction.
nodes.mechanism: Near-field coupling, energy harvesting, antennas, wireless telemetry, or wireless control are integrated with compliant skin-mounted electronics.

nodes.label: Wireless Temporary Cardiac Stimulation
nodes.description: Use inductive magnetic coupling from an external transmitter to wirelessly power an implanted pacemaker for cardiac stimulation.
nodes.function: Provide wireless multisite cardiac stimulation without permanent leads.
nodes.mechanism: An external RF field powers and controls implanted optical or electrical actuators fixed to cardiac tissue.

nodes.label: 3ω Thermal-Property Readout
nodes.description: Drive a temperature-dependent resistive heater with AC and infer local thermal properties from the frequency-dependent third-harmonic voltage response.
nodes.function: Estimate effective thermal conductivity or related thermal transport properties near a contacted material.
nodes.mechanism: AC Joule heating produces temperature oscillations; resistance modulation mixes with the drive current to generate a third-harmonic voltage related to thermal transport.
failure_modes: Proximity thermal coupling between adjacent heater segments
geometry-dependent error for non-linear heater layouts

nodes.label: Absorption-Gated Valve Routing
nodes.description: Redirect fluid sequentially by allowing swelling absorbent elements to close upstream paths after filling.
nodes.function: Create time-separated samples or event-sequenced assays without active pumps.
nodes.mechanism: Hydration-driven expansion of superabsorbent elements occludes an upstream channel and diverts fluid downstream.
failure_modes: backflow or reagent washout if closure fails

nodes.label: Accelerated Biofluid Barrier Lifetime Validation
nodes.description: Estimate long-term barrier-limited device lifetime by accelerated aqueous exposure with direct ingress, degradation, and electrical-failure measurements calibrated to physiological conditions.
nodes.function: Quantify barrier protection, identify failure mechanisms, and project operational lifetime.
nodes.mechanism: Use elevated-temperature immersion, electrical monitoring, leakage or ion measurements, material characterization, and temperature or thickness scaling models.

nodes.label: Access-Controlled Sealed Packaging
nodes.description: Partition fluid-exposed interfaces from protected electronics or fully seal the system when external access is unnecessary.
nodes.function: Prevent environmental exposure while retaining only the required sensing or wireless interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Selective exposure, continuous sealing, and connector-free wireless access control the paths through which fluids and contaminants can reach electronics.

nodes.label: Active-Layer Strain and Failure Mapping
nodes.description: Use layered or finite-element mechanics to map deformation into active-layer strain, curvature, or directional loading and use the result to guide material placement or calibration.
nodes.function: Protect or characterize functional layers within deformable stacks.
nodes.mechanism: Neutral-plane, layered bending, and finite-element models transform global deformation into local active-layer strain or mode-specific loading.

nodes.label: Active Multiplexed Conformal Array
nodes.description: Integrate local active electronics with distributed conformal electrodes to buffer, multiplex, or address electrophysiological channels on dynamic tissue surfaces.
nodes.function: Provide high-density spatial electrophysiology with reduced external wiring and optional localized intervention.
nodes.mechanism: Thin-film transistors, amplifiers, multiplexers, or other active components are co-integrated with compliant electrode arrays and encapsulation to preserve signal access during deformation.

nodes.label: Addressable Resistive Heating
nodes.description: Use electrically addressed resistive traces or pixels to generate spatially or temporally controlled localized heat without requiring the heater itself to provide the primary temperature readout.
nodes.function: Apply programmable local warming or selectively activate thermal regions.
nodes.mechanism: Controlled current through patterned conductors produces Joule heat, with trace geometry or addressing determining the heated location and intensity.

nodes.label: Adhesion-Selective Patterned-Film Transfer
nodes.description: Pattern and deposit thin films or multilayer functional coatings by transferring material from a relief or compliant stamp to a receiver through adhesion contrast.
nodes.function: Create patterned films, contacts, networks, or multilayer structures without direct subtractive processing on the receiver.
nodes.mechanism: A stamp carries deposited material; conformal contact, surface chemistry, thermal treatment, or interface-energy contrast favors retention on the receiver during separation.
failure_modes: Incomplete transfer to rough or low-energy surfaces

nodes.label: Adhesive-Embedded Transfer
nodes.description: Transfer functional microstructures into a curable adhesive receiver so curing bonds and mechanically stabilizes the organized structures on a flexible substrate.
nodes.function: Integrate transferred functional elements while preserving placement and functional access.
nodes.mechanism: A compliant stamp transfers structures into a wet adhesive or prepolymer; conformal wetting and curing create a bonded receiver matrix.
failure_modes: Thermal or chemical damage during curing

nodes.label: Air-Cavity Piezoresistive Pressure Sensing
nodes.description: Convert pressure difference across a sealed or trapped-air cavity into electrical resistance change using membrane-induced strain in a piezoresistive gauge.
nodes.function: Measure pressure relative to a trapped reference pressure.
nodes.mechanism: Pressure deflects a flexible diaphragm over an air cavity, straining a piezoresistive gauge whose resistance is electrically read out.

nodes.label: Aligned Parallel-Nanotube Channel
nodes.description: Use aligned parallel one-dimensional conductors as a gated thin-film transistor channel for aggregated, anisotropic transport.
nodes.function: Provide high-current and comparatively uniform field-effect switching in a thin-film format.
nodes.mechanism: Parallel aligned nanotubes bridge source and drain while gate bias modulates semiconducting-channel transport and reduces junction-related variability.
failure_modes: contact resistance domination at short channel lengths

nodes.label: Analytic Bilayer Equilibrium Modeling
nodes.description: Predict bilayer curvature or rolling angle from mismatch strain, layer geometry, and material properties using force and moment equilibrium.
nodes.function: Translate bilayer mismatch and geometry into designed curvature or rolling angle.
nodes.mechanism: Layer eigenstrain or prestretch is represented in beam or laminate kinematics, and axial force and bending-moment equilibrium determine the shape.
failure_modes: model mismatch outside assumed constitutive or geometric regime

nodes.label: Analytic–FEA Cross-Validation
nodes.description: Test reduced analytical mechanics by comparing deformation, strain, stiffness, or dynamic predictions with matched finite-element results.
nodes.function: Assess accuracy and applicability limits of simplified mechanics models.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical or reduced-order predictions are evaluated against FEA fields or responses across controlled geometry, material, and loading conditions.
failure_modes: Agreement does not establish experimental confirmation.
Agreement limited to tested parameter range
Model discrepancy at very compliant crease or base regions

nodes.label: Analytical Curved-Array Mapping
nodes.description: Map planar array coordinates and layout parameters to curved-surface positions, curvature, and strain using analytical geometry or reduced-order mechanics.
nodes.function: Guide curved-array layout and reconstruct element placement during conformal transformation.
nodes.mechanism: Geometric coordinate transformations, plate or beam relations, and energy minimization predict final positions, curvature, displacement, and strain.
failure_modes: Mismatch between ideal and fabricated geometry
Model error outside assumed deformation regime
Model mismatch from uncertain adhesion or material properties
Neglected local effects at detector/interconnect boundaries

nodes.label: Analytical Geometric Inverse Design
nodes.description: Derive planar geometry, fold patterns, or loading parameters for a target 3D shape using analytical geometry and reduced-order mechanics.
nodes.function: Generate precursor layouts for prescribed assembled geometries.
nodes.mechanism: Target curvature, fold pathways, equilibrium, and geometric constraints are analytically mapped to planar dimensions, thickness, bonding, or force conditions.
failure_modes: High computational cost for nonlinear models

nodes.label: Analytical–Numerical–Experimental Cross-Validation
nodes.description: Cross-check reduced analytical models and higher-fidelity numerical simulations against matched experimental observables to assess predictive adequacy.
nodes.function: Validate multiphysics or mechanics models across abstraction levels.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical or reduced models and FEA, computational flow, or optical simulations predict matched quantities that are compared with controlled measurements.
failure_modes: Mismatch between bending approximation and nonlinear FEA mechanics

nodes.label: Anchored anisotropic wire-array fabrication
nodes.description: Fabricate ordered semiconductor wire arrays by anisotropic etching while retaining anchors or unetched connections for positional registration.
nodes.function: Create aligned, registered semiconductor wire arrays with controlled geometry.
nodes.mechanism: Lithographic masking exposes crystal regions to anisotropic etching, while retained connections or anchors hold the wires in their patterned positions.
failure_modes: Loss of registration if connection points are removed prematurely

nodes.label: Anisotropic Etch Morphology Tuning
nodes.description: Select mask materials and etchants to control the morphology and crystallographic surfaces, including cross-section, of released GaAs wires.
nodes.function: Control morphology and crystallographic surfaces during anisotropic etching.
nodes.mechanism: Mask and etchant chemistry change relative crystal-plane, vertical, and lateral etch rates, thereby changing sidewall angles, cross-section, roughness, and interface quality.

nodes.label: Auxiliary-Sensor Model Compensation
nodes.description: Use a coupled auxiliary temperature measurement as a correction variable in a compensation model for another sensing channel.
nodes.function: Reduce temperature-dependent drift and bias in pressure readout.
nodes.mechanism: Pressure and temperature outputs are acquired together, and a calibrated correction relation converts pressure response to a temperature-compensated estimate.
failure_modes: Large local gradients at the reference site
Reference sensor receives substantially different environmental conditions
baseline site differs materially from target site

nodes.label: Balanced encapsulation strain isolation
nodes.description: Surround a strain-sensitive device or interconnect with mechanically balanced compliant layers to place it near the neutral plane and limit deformation transfer.
nodes.function: Protect thin functional layers from bending strain while providing encapsulation.
nodes.mechanism: Upper and lower layers shift the zero-axial-strain plane toward the active layer while absorbing residual deformation.
failure_modes: Active layer displaced from neutral plane
Neutral-plane shift caused by unmodeled interfaces or nonlinear behavior
active layer displaced from neutral plane

nodes.label: Band-Limited Component Separation
nodes.description: Use band-selective filtering to isolate concurrently acquired signal components with distinct characteristic frequency ranges.
nodes.function: Disambiguate physiological or multiphysics signal components in a composite measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Low-pass, band-pass, or other spectral filters retain target frequency bands while attenuating components associated with competing processes.

nodes.label: Barrier-Controlled Transient Lifetime
nodes.description: Control transient-device functional lifetime through encapsulation permeability and degradation kinetics, including staged degradation of encapsulation and active components.
nodes.function: Maintain function during the required interval and initiate predictable degradation afterward.
nodes.mechanism: Encapsulation permeability, thickness, composition, and staged degradation delay or expose active materials.
failure_modes: Loss of function before intended endpoint
barrier persisting after device function is no longer needed

nodes.label: Baseline- and Batch-Normalized Calibration
nodes.description: Normalize sensor responses using batch, unit-specific, or subject-specific baseline calibration before quantitative interpretation.
nodes.function: Compensate fabrication, baseline, or subject variability in subsequent measurements.
nodes.mechanism: Known-state or predeployment responses establish lookup tables, normalization factors, or calibration coefficients applied to later signals.

nodes.label: Bioresorbable Therapeutic Platform
nodes.description: Deliver temporary therapy through bioresorbable implants that integrate power, control, stimulation, heating, or drug release and then disappear.
nodes.function: Provide finite-duration intervention without chronic implant burden or retrieval surgery.
nodes.mechanism: Wireless or externally triggered transient electronics actuate neural, thermal, mechanical, or pharmacological therapy while degradable materials coordinate functional and resorption lifetimes.

nodes.label: Breakaway Anchor-Bridge Registration
nodes.description: Retain undercut semiconductor elements with sacrificial anchors or bridges until controlled pickup, then fracture or remove the attachments for deterministic transfer.
nodes.function: Maintain donor-defined position and array order during release and retrieval.
nodes.mechanism: Selective etching frees the active structure while narrow corner, end, or buried-oxide attachments remain intact until pickup forces break them.

nodes.label: Buckled Geometric Interconnect
nodes.description: Use prestrained or prebuckled conductive traces whose out-of-plane geometry unfolds under applied deformation to preserve electrical continuity.
nodes.function: Provide stretchable electrical connections between separated functional regions.
nodes.mechanism: Prestrain release creates buckles or noncoplanar arcs; subsequent loading changes their curvature and amplitude instead of imposing equivalent axial conductor strain.

nodes.label: Buckled Thin-Film Strain Reservoir
nodes.description: Use a prestrained compliant substrate and a bonded thin functional film or ribbon so substrate deformation is accommodated by reversible out-of-plane buckling and curvature change rather than direct film strain.
nodes.function: Enable stretchable, compressible, or bendable integration of strain-intolerant thin films.
nodes.mechanism: Prestrain release induces buckling; subsequent deformation changes buckle amplitude, wavelength, or curvature while limiting membrane strain in the thin film.
failure_modes: Film fracture at excessive curvature or deformation
Fracture when peak strain exceeds material fracture strain

nodes.label: Buckling-Wavelength Modulus Metrology
nodes.description: Infer an element's effective elastic modulus by fitting measured buckling wavelength and geometry to a mechanics model with characterized substrate properties.
nodes.function: Estimate difficult-to-measure mechanical properties from observed buckling geometry.
nodes.mechanism: A mechanics relation maps element geometry, substrate stiffness, and modulus to wavelength; inverse fitting solves for the unknown modulus.
design_handles: Choice of wavelength versus amplitude observable
failure_modes: Bias from slipping, alignment error, finite-length effects, or incorrect constitutive assumptions
Slip or residual roughness affecting geometry
Uncertainty from geometric measurement and model fitting
roughness preventing the assumed buckling mode

nodes.label: Buffered Row-Column Readout
nodes.description: Use pixel-local switches and buffers with sequential row selection and shared column outputs to acquire dense distributed sensor signals through reduced wiring.
nodes.function: Scale high-density array acquisition while limiting interconnect count and signal crosstalk.
nodes.mechanism: Local transistor cells buffer or amplify sensor signals; row-select circuitry activates cells and shared columns route selected outputs to external acquisition.
failure_modes: Switching limited by control slew rate

nodes.label: Calibrated Filling-Front Flow Readout
nodes.description: Infer cumulative fluid volume or flow rate from the position or extent of a visible front advancing through a channel or reservoir of known geometry with calibration.
nodes.function: Provide low-complexity visual estimation of fluid volume, loss, or flow rate.
nodes.mechanism: A dye, marker, or visible liquid front advances through calibrated fluidic geometry; front position or filled volume is mapped to transported volume and, when time-resolved, rate.

nodes.label: Capillary-Bursting Sequential Fluid Routing
nodes.description: Use geometry-defined capillary bursting thresholds to route continuously arriving liquid through spatially separated reservoirs or assay chambers in a defined sequence for time- or volume-resolved sampling.
nodes.function: Provide passive sequential fluid routing and chronologically separated samples without powered valves or pumps.
nodes.mechanism: Valves open when local pressure exceeds distinct geometry- and wetting-dependent thresholds; ordered thresholds control reservoir filling and downstream routing.

nodes.label: Capillary Conformal Wrapping
nodes.description: Use drying-induced capillary forces to wrap a low-bending-stiffness thin device into conformal contact with a textured or curved surface.
nodes.function: Create passive intimate contact with irregular biological or engineered surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Liquid wetting or dissolution followed by drying generates capillary forces that overcome the film's bending-energy penalty and pull it onto the receiver.
failure_modes: Poor contact on extreme curvature or hair

nodes.label: Capillary-Threshold Reservoir Routing
nodes.description: Route continuously arriving fluid into temporally ordered reservoirs using passive capillary bursting thresholds.
nodes.function: Provide chronometric sample separation without powered valves.
nodes.mechanism: Geometry-defined bursting pressures open valves in sequence as the filling pressure rises, isolating successive aliquots.
failure_modes: incomplete assay stabilization before subsequent valve bursts

nodes.label: Catalyst-Assisted Anisotropic Semiconductor Etching
nodes.description: Use a patterned metal catalyst and oxidizing etchant to locally oxidize and dissolve semiconductor material, producing patterned three-dimensional relief.
nodes.function: Fabricate site-selective semiconductor nanostructures and relief features by catalyst-assisted wet etching.
nodes.mechanism: The catalyst mediates oxidant reduction and hole injection; holes oxidize the semiconductor beneath or near the catalyst, and acid dissolves the oxidized products. Transport balance controls vertical versus lateral etching.
failure_modes: Polishing or loss of discernible structures
nonuniform etching from contaminated catalyst/semiconductor interfaces
porous sidewalls at excessive oxidant levels
sidewall roughness inherited from catalyst-edge roughness

nodes.label: Channel-Charge Modulation
nodes.description: Transduce molecular adsorption or surface-charge perturbation into nanotube-channel carrier modulation and drain-current change.
nodes.function: Convert molecular or interfacial charge changes into an electrical FET signal.
nodes.mechanism: Adsorbates, bound molecules, or recognition-associated charges alter channel doping, electrostatic gating, scattering, or percolative transport.
failure_modes: Contact resistance can dominate apparent sensing response
contact-resistance modulation can confound channel-transduction interpretation
heterogeneity in tube diameter and length

nodes.label: Chemical-Coating Polarity Switching
nodes.description: Apply a charge-transfer chemical coating to switch or tune semiconductor carrier polarity without changing electrode geometry.
nodes.function: Convert or configure channel polarity through surface functionalization.
nodes.mechanism: A polymer coating transfers charge or changes injection barriers at exposed semiconductor regions, shifting threshold and carrier type.

nodes.label: Chronometric Biofluid Storage
nodes.description: Store sequential sweat samples in separated chambers using passive capillary-bursting-valve microfluidics.
nodes.function: Enable time-resolved analysis of changing biofluid composition.
nodes.mechanism: Channels and reservoirs fill in sequence, isolating collected fractions from one another.

nodes.label: Co-Imaged Color-Reference Calibration
nodes.description: Normalize image-derived colorimetric assay signals against co-imaged standards, markers, or background references before quantitative mapping.
nodes.function: Reduce illumination, camera, geometry, and background-color variation in colorimetric readout.
nodes.mechanism: Known color references or baseline regions are captured with the assay; corrected color features are compared with calibrated standards.

nodes.label: Coherence-Mediated Depth Grading
nodes.description: Use coherence, angular bandwidth, or spectral bandwidth to vary exposure visibility through depth and grade porosity.
nodes.function: Create monotonic, periodic, or nonmonotonic density gradients during optical patterning.
nodes.mechanism: Angular and spectral averaging alter interference visibility or exposure contrast with depth; development converts the resulting profile into porosity.
failure_modes: Excessive visibility loss near the surface or throughout the film
Loss of interconnected structure at excessive absorption
Weak gradient when bandwidth effects are small

nodes.label: Colorimetric Indicator Readout
nodes.description: Convert analyte- or stimulus-dependent indicator chemistry into calibrated color, absorbance, or visible-intensity measurements.
nodes.function: Provide low-complexity quantitative optical detection of chemical or environmental targets.
nodes.mechanism: A responsive reagent changes hue, absorption, or RGB intensity after analyte interaction, and image-derived optical features are mapped to the target quantity.

nodes.label: Competitive Lateral-Flow Immunoassay
nodes.description: Use a competitive cortisol immunoassay with nanoparticle-based lateral-flow readout and line-ratio quantification.
nodes.function: Provide portable quantitative immunoassay detection for low-molecular-weight targets.
nodes.mechanism: Sample analyte occupies labeled antibody binding sites, modulating capture at the test line; control and test line signals or ratios are optically read to estimate concentration.

nodes.label: Complementary Multilayer Fluid-Barrier Stack
nodes.description: Stack dissimilar barrier layers or phases to interrupt water, vapor, and ion transport pathways and extend protected operation.
nodes.function: Increase fluid-barrier lifetime and reduce defect-mediated leakage or degradation.
nodes.mechanism: Layers with complementary permeability, dissolution, defect, or mechanical properties create tortuous and discontinuous transport paths to active electronics.

nodes.label: Complementary Pull-Up Pull-Down Inverter
nodes.description: Pair complementary p- and n-channel transistors to produce voltage inversion with pull-up and pull-down paths.
nodes.function: Implement NOT logic in flexible or printed electronics.
nodes.mechanism: Opposite-polarity transistor paths respond complementarily to the input and generate an inverted output.
failure_modes: Mobility mismatch can unbalance current outputs and reduce inverter performance

nodes.label: Compliant Cavity and Soft-Shell Encapsulation
nodes.description: Use a low-stiffness cavity or soft outer shell to protect electronics while preserving interconnect mobility and tissue-compatible deformation.
nodes.function: Combine fluid protection with mechanical decoupling and compliance.
nodes.mechanism: An air cavity or compliant elastomeric outer layer reduces mechanical loading and mismatch while maintaining an environmental enclosure.

nodes.label: Compliant Conductive-Path Strain Gauge
nodes.description: Use a mechanically compliant conductive path whose geometry or connectivity changes under deformation to produce a resistance signal.
nodes.function: Measure strain on deformable surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Deformation changes conductive-path geometry, buckled-nanowire configuration, or percolation connectivity.
failure_modes: Mechanical constraint of the target organ
Reduced gauge factor from balanced tensile and compressive stresses

nodes.label: Compliant Conformal Thermal Interface
nodes.description: A low-modulus conformal coating can provide intimate thermal contact to skin and tolerate repeated application and removal without adverse device or skin effects.
nodes.function: Couple heaters or thermal sensors to moving biological surfaces while reducing air gaps and placement variability.
nodes.mechanism: Low-modulus encapsulation deforms to increase contact conformity; thermal insulation and controlled interface geometry direct heat toward the sensing surface.

nodes.label: Compliant Contact-Area Adhesion Switching
nodes.description: Reversibly modulate adhesion by collapsing and recovering compliant surface relief to change real contact area.
nodes.function: Enable deterministic pickup, retention, and release of objects.
nodes.mechanism: Compression increases contact area and adhesion; retraction and elastic or viscoelastic recovery reduce contact area for release.
failure_modes: Excessive restoring force and failed pickup

nodes.label: Compliant Encapsulation of Preformed Deformable Structures
nodes.description: Fill around a preformed flexible or buckled structure with a compliant curable encapsulant to stabilize geometry while retaining deformation capacity.
nodes.function: Protect and mechanically confine deformable structures during loading.
nodes.mechanism: A flowable precursor fills gaps around the structure and cures after conformal filling, reducing sliding or detachment without substantially flattening the programmed geometry.
failure_modes: Fracture if confinement transfers excessive stress
Post-encapsulation stretchability not established in this paper
Potential deformation if the prepolymer imposes load before curing

nodes.label: Compliant neural tissue coupling
nodes.description: Use low-stiffness materials or compliant structures to accommodate neural-tissue micromotion while maintaining bidirectional electrical coupling.
nodes.function: Reduce mechanical mismatch during chronic neural recording or stimulation.
nodes.mechanism: Ultrathin, low-modulus, or compliant interfaces deform with tissue motion and support electrode-electrolyte signal transfer.

nodes.label: Compliant-Stamp Discrete-Element Transfer
nodes.description: Retrieve released discrete structures with a compliant stamp and place them on a receiver using controlled pickup and receiver-side bonding.
nodes.function: Register and integrate fragile microdevices or microstructures across incompatible substrates.
nodes.mechanism: Conformal stamp contact retrieves elements through adhesion; receiver adhesive, curing, cold welding, or controlled peeling causes release and attachment.
failure_modes: Incomplete transfer to rough or low-energy surfaces

nodes.label: Compressive Substrate-Release Assembly
nodes.description: Transform a planar precursor into a designed 3D architecture by anchoring selected regions to a compliant substrate and releasing stored compressive strain.
nodes.function: Create deterministic nonplanar microsystems from planar precursors.
nodes.mechanism: Substrate relaxation transfers compression through patterned constraints, driving buckling, folding, translation, and rotation of released regions.
failure_modes: Excessive strain in metal or polymer

nodes.label: Conformable Phase-Mask 3D Patterning
nodes.description: Use a conformable relief phase mask in optical contact with a photosensitive material to generate a depth-dependent near-field intensity distribution that is converted by exposure and development into nanoscale or three-dimensional structures.
nodes.function: Fabricate mask-defined nanoscale and three-dimensional polymer structures.
nodes.mechanism: Relief-induced phase modulation and diffraction create near-field interference; photosensitive material response and development convert the intensity field into material relief.
failure_modes: Developer and photocatalyst diffusion not captured by simplified models
Pulse broadening and imperfect overlap at sufficiently large thickness

nodes.label: Conformal Deformation-Tolerant Sensing
nodes.description: Integrate sensing elements into thin, compliant, conformal structures so signal acquisition remains functional across curvature and body motion.
nodes.function: Maintain sensing contact and output on moving or curved surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Flexible substrates, soft encapsulation, and deformable transducer architectures accommodate bending, stretching, folding, or twisting.

nodes.label: Conformal Elastomeric Barrier Encapsulation
nodes.description: Use a continuous conformal polymer or elastomer layer to isolate electronics or surfaces from fluid exposure while preserving flexible contact.
nodes.function: Provide flexible environmental or biofluid protection through a continuous conformal barrier.
nodes.mechanism: A continuous cured or deposited coating interrupts fluid and ion pathways while mechanically surrounding and protecting the active system.

nodes.label: Conformal Organ-Surface Multimodal Array
nodes.description: Co-locate complementary sensors and actuators on a conformal platform matched to an organ surface for spatially aligned monitoring and intervention.
nodes.function: Map physiological state and deliver localized therapy or perturbation on moving organs.
nodes.mechanism: Distributed electrical, chemical, thermal, optical, or therapeutic elements share a deformable anatomical membrane.

nodes.label: Conformal phase-shift resist lithography
nodes.description: Pattern photoresist by ultraviolet exposure through a relief-bearing elastomeric phase mask held in conformal contact with the resist.
nodes.function: Generate nanoscale or submicrometer resist features over broad areas.
nodes.mechanism: Relief-induced phase shifts create near-field intensity structure that selectively exposes the resist near mask features.

nodes.label: Conformal piezoelectric actuator-sensor modulus sensing
nodes.description: Estimate local soft-material or tissue mechanical properties from electromechanically coupled responses of conformally mounted piezoelectric actuator–sensor pairs.
nodes.function: Measure local elastic or viscoelastic properties of compliant substrates without invasive sampling.
nodes.mechanism: Actuator excitation produces mechanically coupled deformation through the substrate; neighboring piezoelectric sensors generate amplitude and phase responses that are mapped to modulus using calibration or an analytical inverse model.
failure_modes: Interfacial shear at very low sample modulus
model mismatch for strongly heterogeneous substrates

nodes.label: Conformal Serpentine 3ω Thermal Sensor
nodes.description: Use AC third-harmonic lock-in readout for thermal-property sensing, with sensing/heating elements placed in a mechanically isolated neutral plane; serpentine heater geometries can provide stretchability on soft substrates.
nodes.function: Measure thermal conductivity or diffusivity on curved, deformable surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Serpentine geometry accommodates strain, polymer encapsulation isolates the heater and protects the interface, and AC excitation with harmonic detection yields thermal-property estimates.

nodes.label: Connected BLE Telemetry
nodes.description: Acquire and periodically or continuously transfer sensor data over a maintained or coordinated BLE telemetry link.
nodes.function: Provide remote monitoring from wearable or implanted sensing systems.
nodes.mechanism: Embedded acquisition electronics digitize and buffer measurements, then exchange packets with a nearby BLE receiver or smartphone.

nodes.label: Contact-Limited Transport Interpretation
nodes.description: Interpret measured short-channel transport after accounting for series contact resistance that distorts apparent current and mobility.
nodes.function: Prevent overestimation of intrinsic channel transport.
nodes.mechanism: Length-independent source/drain contact resistance becomes a substantial fraction of total resistance as channel length decreases.
failure_modes: Operating regime is outside the fitted model
mistaking contact-limited mobility for intrinsic mobility
