nodes.label: Contact-Modulated Impedance Readout
nodes.description: Infer physical contact or tissue and cell state from impedance changes caused by altered ionic conduction paths and electrode-sample coupling.
nodes.function: Detect contact, hydration, viability, or cell coverage electrically.
nodes.mechanism: Contact or cell coverage changes ionic access and conduction between paired electrodes, producing calibrated impedance shifts.
failure_modes: Sensitivity to contact interface and residual surface films

nodes.label: Contact-modulated nanotube FET chemical sensing
nodes.description: In Cr–SWNT-contacted SNFETs, CO exposure can produce gas-detection signals dominated by changes in the electrode–SWNT contact rather than channel conductance or direct SWNT doping.
nodes.function: Detect chemical exposure through contact-limited transistor transport.
nodes.mechanism: Adsorbates or bound receptors modify contact barriers or junction properties, changing injection and drain current independently of bulk channel doping.
failure_modes: Channel-doping interpretation may be confounded with contact modulation
Contact-specific response may limit generality across electrode materials

nodes.label: Controlled Deformation Durability Validation
nodes.description: Validate deformable devices and structures by applying controlled deformation states or cycles and measuring electrical, functional, or RF-property retention under specified conditions.
nodes.function: Assess deformation-dependent performance, reversibility, fatigue resistance, and durability boundaries.
nodes.mechanism: A calibrated mechanical fixture imposes known curvature, strain, pressure, stretching, twisting, or compression while a functional or structural response is measured against an undeformed or pre-cycle reference.

nodes.label: Controlled Device-Testbed Validation
nodes.description: Test model-based device predictions under controlled loading, material, geometry, or operating conditions using fabricated devices or physical testbeds.
nodes.function: Determine whether a proposed device mechanism explains measured behavior.
nodes.mechanism: A model predicts device output over controlled conditions, and calibrated measurements from devices, artificial samples, or flow rigs are compared with those predictions.
failure_modes: Mismatch between bending approximation and nonlinear FEA mechanics

nodes.label: Controlled Transient Disappearance
nodes.description: Operate for a finite interval and then undergo planned dissolution, degradation, disintegration, or resorption.
nodes.function: Provide temporary device operation without permanent material burden or retrieval.
nodes.mechanism: Material composition, geometry, environmental exposure, and protective layers determine degradation and disappearance timing.
failure_modes: insufficient dissolution due to solubility limits
loss of function before intended lifetime
loss of function before target interval

nodes.label: Controller-Driven Thermal Optofluidic Probe
nodes.description: Use an external wireless controller to address resistive-heater fluid pumps and optical emitters integrated into a compliant neural probe.
nodes.function: Deliver localized fluids and light through a programmable soft implant.
nodes.mechanism: IR-controlled electronics independently drive thermal pumps and μ-LEDs embedded in flexible multichannel microfluidic probes.

nodes.label: Coordinated Multimodal Neural Platform
nodes.description: Coordinate electrophysiology with optical, chemical, environmental, behavioral, or fluidic modalities on one neural platform.
nodes.function: Jointly interrogate, manipulate, and contextualize neural circuits.
nodes.mechanism: Independent neural sensing, stimulation, environmental-control, and monitoring channels share synchronized control and readout.

nodes.label: Coupled Multiphysics Thermal Safety Modeling
nodes.description: Use coupled thermal, mechanical, optical, electrical, fluidic, tissue, or material-scale models to predict safety-relevant thermal behavior and compare it with observations where available.
nodes.function: Assess thermal safety, placement limits, multiphysics interactions, and failure or performance bounds.
nodes.mechanism: Multiple interacting physics or scales are solved together or sequentially, incorporating realistic materials, anatomy, flow, deformation, heat sources, or phase change and benchmarking resulting thermal predictions against measurements or design limits.
failure_modes: Mismatch between experimental and modeled heating conditions

nodes.label: Crystallographic Surface-Guided Growth
nodes.description: Use anisotropic crystalline surfaces to bias one-dimensional nanostructure nucleation and growth along a preferred in-plane direction during CVD.
nodes.function: Produce horizontally aligned nanostructure arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Lattice directions, atomic steps, facets, and orientation-dependent surface interactions create energetically preferred growth directions.
failure_modes: Bundling and multiwalled growth at excessive catalyst density
Disordered or amorphous surface suppresses a unique preferred direction
Excessive relief or roughness can reduce alignment
Growth outside the intended catalyst regions
Growth termination at surface relief or obstructing material
Reduced alignment from unreacted catalyst particles

nodes.label: Crystallographic undercut release
nodes.description: Release patterned crystalline semiconductor microelements by exploiting directional crystal-plane etching and retaining anchors for registration.
nodes.function: Create freestanding crystalline ribbons, bars, platelets, or devices from bulk wafers.
nodes.mechanism: Lithographic and dry etching expose selected crystal planes; anisotropic wet etching removes support along fast-etching directions and self-terminates on slow-etching planes.

nodes.label: Cyclic Bending Electrical Durability
nodes.description: Assess electrical retention during controlled bending and repeated bend–unbend cycling.
nodes.function: Quantify curvature-dependent stability and bending fatigue of flexible electronic devices.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical metrics are normalized to a reference state and tracked across bend radius, strain, and cycle count.
failure_modes: Localized failure hidden by aggregate metrics
failure outside tested strain or cycle range

nodes.label: Deformable Nanotube Percolation Network
nodes.description: Use a connected network of deformable conductive one-dimensional elements to preserve percolating electrical transport during substrate deformation.
nodes.function: Provide mechanically compliant electrical conduction or active channels.
nodes.mechanism: Element rearrangement and persistent element–element contacts maintain a conducting path while the network conforms to strain.

nodes.label: Depth-Resolved Optical Model Validation
nodes.description: Validate a depth-dependent density or exposure profile by comparing a depth-resolved optical signal with a calculated intensity profile.
nodes.function: Test whether an observed gradient follows the predicted optical mechanism.
nodes.mechanism: A reflected optical signal correlated with density is measured through sample depth and compared with modeled average intensity.

nodes.label: Dielectric Capacitive Biointerface
nodes.description: Use a tissue-facing dielectric as both biofluid barrier and capacitive coupling layer for isolated electrophysiological recording.
nodes.function: Record biopotentials without direct conductive contact between tissue and electronics.
nodes.mechanism: Tissue potentials couple through an insulating dielectric to an underlying electrode or transistor gate while the dielectric blocks fluid ingress and direct current.
failure_modes: Signal attenuation from insufficient coupling capacitance
loss of signal after contamination or poor contact

nodes.label: Differential Electrical Reference Readout
nodes.description: Subtract a stimulus-sensitive electrical channel from a matched reference channel to reject shared electrode, parasitic, environmental, or mechanical disturbances.
nodes.function: Isolate local electrical or impedance changes from common-mode interference.
nodes.mechanism: A sensing channel responds to the target while a matched reference is shielded or differently exposed; differential processing removes shared contributions.
failure_modes: Reduced duty cycle and depth when pulsing
Reference sensor coupling too strongly to heater

nodes.label: Differential-Expansion Bilayer Folding
nodes.description: Bond layers with mismatched stimulus-induced expansion or swelling so a planar bilayer bends, folds, or rolls into a three-dimensional form.
nodes.function: Transform planar bilayers into responsive 3D shapes.
nodes.mechanism: A stimulus creates a strain mismatch between bonded layers, generating curvature and localized folding.
failure_modes: insufficient bending force to overcome substrate friction
slow recovery when contraction densifies the layer

nodes.label: Differential Multi-Distance Thermal Inversion
nodes.description: Infer internal temperature or thermal state by combining measurements from thermally distinct sensor locations or coupling paths.
nodes.function: Reduce ambient sensitivity while estimating subsurface or core temperature.
nodes.mechanism: Differential readings from separated or asymmetrically coupled thermal nodes provide independent heat-transfer constraints that are fitted with a thermal model.
failure_modes: Error magnification in the inverse problem
Model error from unmodeled 3D heat conduction
thick superficial layer blocking deeper sensitivity

nodes.label: Differential Thermal Flow Sensing
nodes.description: Infer flow from spatial or directional temperature differences around a thermal actuator.
nodes.function: Measure flow direction or magnitude.
nodes.mechanism: A heater creates a thermal field; convection skews heat transport; separated sensors measure differential responses mapped to flow.

nodes.label: Differential Thermal Reference Readout
nodes.description: Subtract a nearby or temporally matched thermal reference from an active thermal measurement to suppress ambient and baseline-temperature drift.
nodes.function: Stabilize thermal measurements under changing environmental conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Active and reference regions share ambient variation but differ in heating or target exposure; subtraction removes the shared temperature component.
failure_modes: Reduced duty cycle and depth when pulsing
Reference sensor coupling too strongly to heater

nodes.label: Dimensional Thermal-Lubrication Model
nodes.description: Predict heat-driven thin-film evolution by coupling a localized heat-source temperature field with a dimensional lubrication-flow equation.
nodes.function: Estimate trench geometry and time evolution under specified process conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Localized heating creates temperature gradients and surface-tension stresses that drive viscous film-thickness evolution solved with material and boundary parameters.
failure_modes: approximation breakdown outside essentially unidirectional flow
invalidity when central film thickness reaches zero
poorly known viscosity or surface tension

nodes.label: Diode-Isolated Sensor Matrix Addressing
nodes.description: Use diode-isolated row-column addressing to sequentially select distributed sensor cells while suppressing unselected paths.
nodes.function: Reduce wiring while preserving access to distributed sensor outputs.
nodes.mechanism: Row and column biasing forward-biases selected diode sensor paths and reverse-biases unselected paths; shared columns carry the selected sensor response.

nodes.label: Direct Conformal Stamp Transfer
nodes.description: Use a compliant stamp or stretchable array to establish conformal contact with a three-dimensional receiver and release the device without requiring a molded flattening-and-relaxation cycle.
nodes.function: Transfer devices onto curved, cylindrical, spherical, or inflated receivers.
nodes.mechanism: Rolling, pressing, wrapping, or stamp-mediated pickup and placement conforms the device to the receiver while adhesion and compliant deformation preserve registration and connectivity.

nodes.label: Direct Indicator Color Readout
nodes.description: Use a stimulus-responsive indicator matrix whose visible color state is read directly by eye or ambient-light imaging to detect chemical exposure or composition.
nodes.function: Enable simple visual or image-based chemical detection with minimal instrumentation.
nodes.mechanism: Analyte interaction changes the indicator's optical state, and the resulting color is interpreted directly or through basic digital imaging.

nodes.label: Distributed Resistive Thermography
nodes.description: Map spatial temperature fields using calibrated distributed resistive or thermistor sensing elements.
nodes.function: Reconstruct a spatial temperature field.
nodes.mechanism: Local temperature changes resistance at addressable sites, which are multiplexed or sequentially read to form a map.
failure_modes: Diffusivity is less precisely fitted than conductivity
Layered geometry and convection require calibration

nodes.label: Distributed Wireless Skin-Sensor Networks
nodes.description: Coordinate multiple soft wireless skin-mounted nodes to acquire motion and physiological signals across body locations.
nodes.function: Support distributed, time-coordinated wearable monitoring over extended operation.
nodes.mechanism: Miniaturized sensor nodes use local acquisition and wireless synchronization or transmission to combine measurements from informative body sites.
failure_modes: Different modalities retain different depth sensitivities
Surface residual films can affect impedance more strongly than thermal measurements

nodes.label: Donor-to-Receiver Transfer Integration
nodes.description: Release performance-optimized films, membranes, wires, or finished devices from a donor platform and place them onto a separately selected receiver.
nodes.function: Integrate donor-fabricated high-performance elements with flexible, transient, curved, or otherwise process-incompatible substrates.
nodes.mechanism: Source-side growth and device processing are completed before sacrificial release, adhesion-mediated pickup, transfer printing, or mechanical membrane release onto the receiver.

nodes.label: Dry Donor-Layer Transfer
nodes.description: Transfer preformed patterned solid layers from donors to receivers in repeated dry assembly steps.
nodes.function: Assemble heterogeneous multilayer devices without wet-layer incompatibility.
nodes.mechanism: Donor films or patterned stacks are retrieved and placed by dry contact, thermal imaging, or controlled interfacial release while preserving layer registration.

nodes.label: Dry-Transferred Silicon TFT
nodes.description: Dry-transfer single-crystal silicon microstructures onto plastic substrates to form flexible silicon devices.
nodes.function: Provide field-effect switching on flexible substrates without high-temperature processing on the final substrate.
nodes.mechanism: An elastomeric stamp transfers positioned silicon microstrips or ribbons; gate dielectric and source/drain electrodes form a transistor whose channel is modulated by gate bias.
failure_modes: Silicon or interface failure under bending

nodes.label: Dual-Wavelength Backscatter Oximetry
nodes.description: Estimate local tissue oxygenation from red and near-infrared illumination, backscatter detection, and hemoglobin-sensitive Beer–Lambert analysis.
nodes.function: Monitor tissue oxygen saturation using compact dual-wavelength optical measurements.
nodes.mechanism: Alternating red and infrared light interrogates tissue; detected backscatter amplitudes are separated and converted into oxygenation estimates from differential hemoglobin absorption.
failure_modes: Adhesive or encapsulation durability in clinical use remains unvalidated
Local tissue heterogeneity can cause interdevice differences
Optical scattering assumptions can reduce StO2 precision
Potential tissue or hematoma effects not represented by the model

nodes.label: Dual-Wavelength Hemoglobin Oximetry
nodes.description: Use complementary red and near-infrared optical measurements with hemoglobin-sensitive modeling to estimate local oxygenation and related pulsatile or hemoglobin-change metrics.
nodes.function: Estimate tissue or blood oxygenation from wavelength-dependent optical response.
nodes.mechanism: Time-multiplexed wavelength emitters illuminate tissue; detected transmission or backscatter is processed with a Beer–Lambert-type model using calibration or pathlength assumptions.
failure_modes: absorption and scattering reduce detected signal

nodes.label: Elastomer-Supported Active Integration
nodes.description: Embed or support rigid active electronic materials in elastomeric structures that provide compliance while preserving device operation.
nodes.function: Combine high-performance active electronics with stretchable mechanical support.
nodes.mechanism: Ribbons, meshes, segmented conductors, serpentine interconnects, or other active structures are embedded in or supported by elastomers that absorb deformation.

nodes.label: Elastomeric adhesion transfer printing
nodes.description: Use a compliant elastomeric stamp and engineered interfacial adhesion to retrieve patterned solid structures from a donor and place them on a receiver while preserving registration.
nodes.function: Transfer fragile patterned materials or devices between incompatible substrates.
nodes.mechanism: Conformal stamp contact and controlled adhesion or peeling selectively fracture the donor-stamp and stamp-receiver interfaces.

nodes.label: Elastomeric Stamp Object Transfer
nodes.description: Use a compliant elastomeric stamp and controlled interfacial adhesion to retrieve discrete or patterned solid elements and place them on a receiver.
nodes.function: Enable registered heterogeneous integration of prefabricated solid elements.
nodes.mechanism: Conformal stamp contact, adhesion contrast, donor release, and receiver bonding coordinate pickup and placement.

nodes.label: Electrical continuity lifetime readout
nodes.description: Determine the functional lifetime of a transient conductor by monitoring resistance or continuity during controlled degradation rather than relying only on physical thickness.
nodes.function: Translate conductor degradation into an electrically defined lifetime or time-to-failure metric.
nodes.mechanism: A conductive trace is monitored during aqueous exposure; resistance change or continuity loss defines electrical degradation and functional lifetime.
failure_modes: confusing resistance drift with complete disappearance
electrical failure before complete physical dissolution

nodes.label: Electrical Sacrificial Corrosion Indicator
nodes.description: Detect barrier breakthrough by monitoring resistance or continuity loss in a sacrificial conductor beneath the barrier.
nodes.function: Quantify ingress and provide an electrical failure endpoint.
nodes.mechanism: Water-driven corrosion or hydrolysis changes conductor resistance and eventually causes disconnection.
failure_modes: inability to distinguish bulk from pinhole failure
indicator response after an already-existing defect

nodes.label: Electrohydrodynamic Jet Printing
nodes.description: Use EHD-induced fluid jets through fine nozzles, with voltage-controlled raster scanning, to print programmed micro- and nanoscale patterns.
nodes.function: Additively pattern materials with feature sizes below conventional nozzle dimensions.
nodes.mechanism: Electric-field charge and Maxwell stress deform the meniscus; electrostatic stress overcomes capillary tension and emits droplets or a fine jet while controlled motion defines the pattern.
design_handles: Ink viscosity, surface tension, conductivity, and evaporation rate
failure_modes: Charged-droplet effects are not discussed in this paper chunk

nodes.label: Electromechanical Modulus Sensing
nodes.description: Infer soft-material modulus from periodic actuator-induced deformation measured by an integrated strain gauge.
nodes.function: Quantitatively characterize elastic or effective modulus of soft tissue or material.
nodes.mechanism: Periodic mechanical excitation deforms the sample and gauge; resistance or voltage amplitude is calibrated to modulus.
failure_modes: Dependence on underlying-layer stiffness and sample thickness
Poor contact on extreme curvature or hair-bearing locations

nodes.label: Embedded ML State Inference
nodes.description: Run machine-learning inference locally on extracted biosignal features to classify state and generate low-latency decisions or intervention recommendations.
nodes.function: Convert physiological signals into actionable state estimates under constrained resources.
nodes.mechanism: Feature transforms feed compressed, supervised, or unsupervised models; scores or classifications are aggregated and passed through decision thresholds or treatment logic.

nodes.label: Encapsulation-Coupled Buckling Modeling
nodes.description: Predict how a mechanically coupled encapsulation layer changes buckling morphology, strain, and stretchability of thin-film or interconnect systems.
nodes.function: Guide encapsulant selection and geometry design while preserving buckling-based compliance and protection.
nodes.mechanism: Interconnect or film bending and membrane energies are coupled with substrate and encapsulation elastic energies; energy minimization and a material failure criterion determine deformation limits.
failure_modes: fracture or interface failure occurs before predicted membrane-strain limit
model assumptions fail for large plasticity or delamination

nodes.label: Energy-Balance Collapse Stability
nodes.description: Determine collapse onset, equilibrium, and stability by comparing deformation energy with adhesion-energy gain.
nodes.function: Classify open, unstable-collapse, or stable-collapse states of compliant interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Total potential energy combines elastic deformation or preload-release energy with adhesion energy; minimization or energy comparison identifies the favored state.
failure_modes: Incorrect prediction if material nonlinearities or kinetics dominate
Model invalid when collapse length exceeds post spacing
model assumptions violated by non-cylindrical patterns
poor transfer of calibrated parameter across geometries

nodes.label: Environment-Controlled Dissolution
nodes.description: Tune transient-material lifetime by controlling environmental chemistry and exposure conditions.
nodes.function: Adjust dissolution rate and disappearance time for a specified environment.
nodes.mechanism: Temperature, pH, ion identity, concentration, and byproduct chemistry alter reaction and transport kinetics.

nodes.label: Environmentally Loaded Passive LC Readout
nodes.description: Convert environmental, fluidic, thermal, or material-dependent loading into a remotely detected passive resonant response.
nodes.function: Provide battery-free wireless sensing of environmental or physiological state.
nodes.mechanism: Changes in dielectric properties, conductivity, temperature, or material loading alter resonator L or C and shift the externally interrogated response.
failure_modes: drift from water permeation or material degradation

nodes.label: Enzymatic Peroxide-Coupled Optical Readout
nodes.description: Use enzyme-catalyzed analyte conversion to generate hydrogen peroxide that is converted into an optical reporter signal.
nodes.function: Provide selective biochemical detection through enzyme recognition and peroxide-linked optical reporting.
nodes.mechanism: An oxidoreductase converts the target and generates H2O2; peroxide reacts with a dye or chromogenic reporter to produce a calibrated color or fluorescence response.

nodes.label: Fabricated Optical Model–Measurement Validation
nodes.description: Validate an electromagnetic model by comparing predicted optical response with measurements from a matched fabricated structure.
nodes.function: Establish model adequacy for optical interpretation and design exploration.
nodes.mechanism: Measured transmission, reflection, or absorption is compared with FDTD, RCWA, or transfer-matrix predictions under corresponding geometry and illumination conditions.

nodes.label: Failure-Limited Compliant Layout Optimization
nodes.description: Use mechanics predictions of strain, stress, contact, and deformation to select compliant interconnects, component placement, and substrate layouts that remain within failure limits.
nodes.function: Optimize stretchable device layouts for mechanical reliability.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical or finite-element models identify strain concentrations, collisions, coupling, and yield or fracture risk; geometry and material choices are iteratively revised.

nodes.label: FDTD Electromagnetic Field Modeling
nodes.description: Use finite-difference time-domain solution of Maxwell equations on a geometry and material model to predict spatial electromagnetic fields and optical response.
nodes.function: Model electromagnetic fields in structured optical samples.
nodes.mechanism: Time-domain electromagnetic fields are propagated on a discretized geometry with material dispersion and absorbing boundaries, yielding field maps or spectra.
failure_modes: Material or geometry approximations can limit agreement
Probe interaction may not be fully represented
Tip convolution can cause geometry mismatch

nodes.label: FDTD–Measurement Spectral Cross-Validation
nodes.description: Assess fabricated structured optical fidelity by comparing measured reflection or transmission spectra with FDTD predictions from a representative geometry and material model.
nodes.function: Validate fabricated photonic structures and diagnose geometry or material mismatch.
nodes.mechanism: FDTD computes spectra for a modeled structure, which are compared with measured spectra to assess agreement and identify discrepancies.
failure_modes: Disagreement from roughness, beam nonuniformity, shrinkage, or model mismatch
finite-size effects not represented by infinite-pattern assumptions
model mismatch from geometry or material nonuniformity

nodes.label: FEA-Guided Buckling Assembly Validation
nodes.description: Use linear and nonlinear finite-element mechanics to predict buckling-driven 3D assembly or reconfiguration, then validate geometry, strain, failure limits, or retained function against fabricated structures and measurements.
nodes.function: Guide mechanically transformed architecture design and verify assembly outcomes and safety limits.
nodes.mechanism: FEA identifies instability modes and simulates postbuckled or reconfigured states with substrate, contact, strain, and failure criteria; optical, mechanical, electrical, or RF measurements provide independent checks.
failure_modes: Apparent agreement caused by shared assumptions
False agreement from mismatched boundary conditions

nodes.label: Finite-Deformation Segmented-Ribbon Buckling Model
nodes.description: Use analytic or finite-deformation models of segmented or non-uniform ribbon/beam structures to analyze deformation and the stability of buckling modes under specified loading and geometry conditions.
nodes.function: Guide geometry selection and mechanically guided assembly of nonuniform ribbon structures.
nodes.mechanism: Use beam or ribbon kinematics, segment-wise equilibrium, rotation/moment/force continuity, geometric constraints, and energy minimization or perturbation solutions.
failure_modes: Model discrepancy for wide precursors due to neglected transverse shear
model assumptions invalid for significant twisting
neglect of finite width or deformation

nodes.label: Finite-Deformation Substrate Buckling Model
nodes.description: Predict buckling geometry and strain under large prestrain by coupling thin-film mechanics with nonlinear finite-strain substrate constitutive behavior.
nodes.function: Guide thin-film geometry and stretchability limits when substrate deformation is nonlinear.
nodes.mechanism: Use nonlinear strain-displacement relations and finite-strain substrate constitutive laws within a total-energy minimization framework.
failure_modes: Incorrect predictions if slipping, plasticity, fracture, or finite-substrate effects dominate
Mode selection may require additional constraints or energy terms
Reduced accuracy at very low stiffness ratios
Simplified displacement functions may not capture bottom-layer deformation
Small-deformation model error at large prestrain
Unmodeled slip or local substrate heterogeneity

nodes.label: Finite-Element Thermal Field Validation
nodes.description: Validate finite-element thermal predictions by comparing simulated temperature fields or transients with calibrated measurements under matched operating conditions.
nodes.function: Quantify thermal behavior, operating limits, spatial confinement, or design sensitivity.
nodes.mechanism: A finite-element heat-transfer model represents device layers and boundary conditions; predicted temperatures or histories are compared with infrared, voltage-derived, thermistor, probe, or other experimental measurements.
failure_modes: Mismatch between experimental and modeled heating conditions

nodes.label: Fractal Island-Interconnect Routing
nodes.description: Connect functional regions with recursively self-similar serpentine conductors that distribute deformation across multiple geometric scales while maintaining low conductor strain.
nodes.function: Provide compact, highly stretchable electrical routing between functional regions.
nodes.mechanism: Nested serpentine levels add geometric path length and undergo staged buckling, bending, twisting, or unraveling under applied deformation.
design_handles: Height/spacing ratios at each fractal order
failure_modes: Irreversible entanglement or disorder under repeated overstrain

nodes.label: Frequency-Selective Wireless Thermal Addressing
nodes.description: Use distinguishable resonant channels to selectively wirelessly power spatially separated resistive heaters or thermal modules.
nodes.function: Provide independent wireless thermal actuation with reduced cross-talk.
nodes.mechanism: External RF or magnetic excitation couples preferentially to receivers tuned to selected frequencies, producing local resistive heating.
failure_modes: off-state heating above the release threshold

nodes.label: Frequency-Separated Resonant Sensor Array
nodes.description: Use distinct resonance frequencies to enable separate readout of multiple co-located sensors without crosstalk.
nodes.function: Provide multimodal or multidirectional wireless sensing with reduced channel crosstalk.
nodes.mechanism: Different LC resonance frequencies encode separate sensing elements for spectral or phase-selective readout.

nodes.label: Full-Wave Geometry Optimization
nodes.description: Vary geometry parameters in full-wave electromagnetic simulations to select periodic optical structures with targeted spectral bandwidth, reflection, transmission, or plasmonic response.
nodes.function: Guide optical-structure geometry selection before or alongside fabrication.
nodes.mechanism: Solve Maxwell equations for parameterized periodic or multilayer geometries and use predicted spectral response to compare design alternatives.
failure_modes: Model-experiment discrepancies from dimensional or coating-thickness variation

nodes.label: Full-Wave Spectral and Near-Field Prediction
nodes.description: Use full-wave electromagnetic simulation to predict wavelength-dependent spectra, resonances, and spatial field distributions in detailed periodic optical geometries.
nodes.function: Explain optical response and field-mediated sensing or resonance behavior.
nodes.mechanism: Numerically propagate dispersive electromagnetic fields through periodic multilayer unit cells with appropriate boundary conditions, then calculate spectra, flux, and near-field distributions.
failure_modes: Model-experiment discrepancies from dimensional or coating-thickness variation

nodes.label: Fully Dissolvable Functional Electronics
nodes.description: Integrate transient active, passive, and support materials into complete electronic systems that provide finite-duration function and then dissolve, resorb, disperse, or otherwise disappear.
nodes.function: Provide temporary sensing, processing, communication, power, stimulation, or therapy without retrieval or persistent device burden.
nodes.mechanism: Material composition, dimensions, layer sequencing, and environmental exposure coordinate useful operation with controlled degradation of the complete device.

nodes.label: Geometric Deformation Profile Validation
nodes.description: Validate deformation and buckling models by comparing predicted structural profiles or amplitudes with measured geometries under controlled loading.
nodes.function: Assess whether mechanics models reproduce observed structural deformation.
nodes.mechanism: Controlled loading produces measurable heights, focal positions, or buckled profiles that are compared with analytical or FEM predictions.

nodes.label: Geometry-Parameterized Conductive-Convective Flow Inversion
nodes.description: Infer flow-related transport parameters by fitting heated-surface or multilayer thermal responses to conductive–convective models parameterized by geometry and material properties.
nodes.function: Translate thermal measurements into flow rate, velocity, or related transport parameters.
nodes.mechanism: Conduction establishes the thermal field while flow-dependent convection removes heat; analytical or finite-element forward models are fit to measured thermal features, often with geometry calibration.
failure_modes: confounding between fluid content and velocity
large sensor-heater distance causing high relative error

nodes.label: Geometry-Programmed Sequential Chambers
nodes.description: Use programmed channel and chamber geometry to deliver incoming biofluid to spatially separated assay regions in sequence.
nodes.function: Provide controlled sequential biofluid acquisition and analysis.
nodes.mechanism: Network geometry, reservoir arrangement, and flow-direction constraints establish the order of chamber filling and assay exposure.
failure_modes: backflow or reagent washout if closure fails

nodes.label: Ground-Truth, Control, and Outcome Benchmarking
nodes.description: Validate a sensing, intervention, or inferred result against observed outcomes, behavioral labels, controls, spatial ground truth, or performance benchmarks.
nodes.function: Establish physiological, behavioral, spatial, biological, or functional validity beyond direct comparator-instrument agreement.
nodes.mechanism: Pair device outputs with synchronized observations, control groups, images, tracked motion, clinical labels, outcome measures, or defined benchmarks and assess correspondence.
failure_modes: Different optical or mechanical sampling volumes

nodes.label: Hard-Skin Soft-Support Mold
nodes.description: Form a high-modulus relief-bearing skin on a softer compliant support to preserve fine features while enabling tough handling and conformal transfer.
nodes.function: Maintain high-fidelity relief in reusable soft molds and patterning elements.
nodes.mechanism: The hard patterned layer resists collapse and reproduces fine geometry, while the soft support supplies toughness, compliance, and handling stability.

nodes.label: Helical Buckling Assembly
nodes.description: Form stretchable helical coils or helical interconnects from planar precursors through mechanically guided buckling and substrate constraint.
nodes.function: Create compliant three-dimensional helical structures and interconnects.
nodes.mechanism: Programmed compression and selective constraint drive out-of-plane rotation and coiling of serpentine or ribbon precursors.

nodes.label: Herringbone Biaxial Stress Relaxation
nodes.description: Under approximately equibiaxial compression, a herringbone morphology relaxes in-plane stress by trading modest bending and substrate deformation for a larger reduction in membrane energy.
nodes.function: Accommodate biaxial compressive strain in bonded thin-film systems.
nodes.mechanism: Coupled waves and jogs redistribute compressive strain into out-of-plane deformation while lowering membrane energy relative to competing buckling modes.
failure_modes: 1D mode may dominate near free edges
Alternative 1D or checkerboard modes near threshold
Disordered morphology near centers or boundaries
herringbone is not necessarily preferred for non-equibiaxial strain states
long wavelength may not be uniquely selected by energy minimization

nodes.label: Hierarchical Multilayer Buckling
nodes.description: Tune multilevel 3D buckling geometries by distributing prestrain or constraints across multiple structural layers or length scales.
nodes.function: Control buckling height and hierarchical architecture.
nodes.mechanism: Differential layer prestrain and coupled buckling modes produce multiple elevation scales and tunable out-of-plane displacement.
failure_modes: Insufficient base stiffness causes top-structure shape loss
Very compliant crease regions may not accommodate all deformation energy

nodes.label: Hybrid Local–Cloud Monitoring
nodes.description: Maintain continuous wearable acquisition by switching between local storage or nearby transfer and later cloud upload for remote analytics.
nodes.function: Support unattended monitoring across intermittent connectivity, charging, and power-constrained conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Sensor data are buffered locally or transferred by BLE during an available connection, then uploaded through a gateway to cloud analytics and dashboards.

nodes.label: Hybrid Resolution-Function Patterning
nodes.description: Allocate critical high-resolution features and material-intensive regions to complementary patterning processes whose combined capabilities satisfy device requirements.
nodes.function: Combine resolution, material compatibility, registration, and throughput across fabrication processes.
nodes.mechanism: A high-resolution method defines critical features while a complementary process patterns broader or active-material regions, with cross-process registration controlling integration.

nodes.label: Illumination-Field Normalization
nodes.description: Normalize an image against a separately acquired or matched illumination field to remove spatial source, optical-path, and detector variation.
nodes.function: Recover quantitatively comparable optical image values across the field of view.
nodes.mechanism: Pixelwise division or contrast normalization against a background, blurred reference, or matched mirror image suppresses smooth illumination nonuniformity.
failure_modes: Incorrect background estimate can distort real spatial contrast
normalization does not remove all optical convolution
reference region may contain an unmodeled coating

nodes.label: Imprint-and-Etch Relief Transfer
nodes.description: Use imprint lithography followed by etching to produce isolated features, and use soft nanoimprinting to form submicrometer periodic surface relief.
nodes.function: Define patterned electrodes, optical structures, channels, or other functional features.
nodes.mechanism: Imprinting creates thickness contrast; selective or anisotropic etching removes exposed regions and transfers the relief into the substrate or functional layer.

nodes.label: In-Surface Nanowire Buckling
nodes.description: Generate in-surface lateral waves in aligned nanowires by transferring them to a prestrained compliant substrate and releasing the prestrain.
nodes.function: Create laterally compliant nanowire arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Aligned wires experience compressive mismatch and select the lower-energy in-surface buckling mode.
failure_modes: No buckling when prestrain is absent or below critical strain
yield or fracture at excessive strain

nodes.label: Independent Subsystem Duty Cycling
nodes.description: Control sensing and actuation subsystems with separate activation schedules so each operates only during its informative or required interval.
nodes.function: Reduce subsystem-specific energy use and unwanted thermal or electrical load.
nodes.mechanism: Switches or independent control channels isolate or activate sensors, heaters, and related peripherals at distinct duty cycles.

nodes.label: Injectable Wireless Optical Stimulation Interface
nodes.description: Supply power to implanted microscale LEDs through remote RF harvesting or a flexible subdermal antenna-and-rectifier interface.
nodes.function: Provide localized untethered optical stimulation.
nodes.mechanism: An m-LED on a flexible needle or filament is electrically connected to a remote receiver, harvester, rectifier, or wireless control module.

nodes.label: Integrated Resistive Sensor-Heater
nodes.description: Use an integrated resistive element or colocated heater-sensor structure to apply controlled heat while measuring local temperature for feedback.
nodes.function: Provide localized thermal stimulation with simultaneous temperature measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Joule heating creates a thermal stimulus and temperature-dependent resistance or a colocated thermistor provides the electrical temperature signal.

nodes.label: Integrated Self-Phase-Mask Lithography
nodes.description: Use relief molded directly into the photosensitive recording layer as the phase optic, eliminating a separate external mask while generating a three-dimensional exposure field.
nodes.function: Fabricate three-dimensional polymer structures with an integrated phase mask and recording medium.
nodes.mechanism: Molded relief diffracts and phase-shifts the incident field; single- or multiphoton response records the resulting volumetric intensity distribution in the same material.

nodes.label: Integrated Wireless Epidermal Sensor Platforms
nodes.description: Integrate heterogeneous physiological and environmental sensors with shared flexible electronics, power, processing, and wireless communication on one skin interface.
nodes.function: Provide synchronized multimodal monitoring with minimal tethering and mechanical burden.
nodes.mechanism: Multiple sensing modules share compliant interconnects, encapsulation, energy management, local acquisition, and telemetry.
failure_modes: Different modalities retain different depth sensitivities
Surface residual films can affect impedance more strongly than thermal measurements

nodes.label: Interface-Bonding Deformation Design
nodes.description: Model layered, bonded, or partially delaminating interfaces to design conformal deformation and control strain, adhesion, and interfacial failure.
nodes.function: Design and assess mechanically coupled device–tissue or layered interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Energy, shell, layered-elastic, and finite-element models map stiffness, bonding, geometry, prestrain, and interface energy to deformation, delamination, and transferred stress.
failure_modes: inaccurate prediction for strongly non-axisymmetric geometries

nodes.label: Iontophoretic Sweat Induction
nodes.description: Drive a sweat-inducing agent through skin electrically to generate localized sweat on demand for collection or sensing.
nodes.function: Provide controllable analyte-bearing sweat independent of exercise or ambient heat.
nodes.mechanism: Current transports a secretagogue such as pilocarpine or carbachol across skin, activating local eccrine secretion.

nodes.label: Island-Bridge Buckling Mesh
nodes.description: Connect relatively rigid functional islands with compliant bridges that buckle or move out of plane to absorb global deformation.
nodes.function: Provide stretchable electrical integration while protecting active islands.
nodes.mechanism: Selective node bonding, excess bridge length, and out-of-plane motion concentrate deformation in interconnects and open regions.

nodes.label: Buckled-Interconnect Strain Reservoir
nodes.description: Connect relatively rigid active islands with compliant bridges that buckle or reconfigure out of plane so macroscopic deformation localizes in the interconnects and active islands remain comparatively strain-isolated.
nodes.function: Preserve active-device function in highly deformable electronic arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Differential adhesion and bridge compliance cause interconnects to lift, buckle, or unfold during prestrain release and subsequent deformation while islands remain anchored.

nodes.label: Island–Bridge Strain Isolation
nodes.description: Place strain-sensitive or mechanically compliant functional regions on relatively stiff islands and route deformation through compliant bridges to isolate active regions from global motion.
nodes.function: Protect functional components or interfaces while preserving electrical connection and system deformability.
nodes.mechanism: Stiffness contrast localizes deformation in compliant interconnect bridges, reducing strain and load transfer into functional islands or modules.
failure_modes: Delamination or fracture under repeated motion

nodes.label: Island–Serpentine Strain-Isolating Interconnect
nodes.description: Connect relatively rigid functional islands with compliant serpentine interconnects so global deformation is absorbed by routing geometry while islands remain mechanically protected and electrically connected.
nodes.function: Provide deformable routing and strain isolation for distributed rigid components.
nodes.mechanism: Localized island bonding and serpentine traces allow geometric bending, rotation, or extension between separated islands, reducing strain transfer into active components.

nodes.label: Joule-Heated Thermocapillary Trenching
nodes.description: Use selective electrical heating of embedded conductors to form aligned trenches in a thin film through thermocapillary flow.
nodes.function: Create openings aligned to electrically addressable heat sources.
nodes.mechanism: Joule heating generates local temperature and surface-tension gradients that drive viscous film redistribution away from the heated conductor.
failure_modes: complete depletion of film at the heated center
excessive viscosity or insufficient processing time
insufficiently low viscosity for appreciable flow
trench width too large for dense arrays

nodes.label: Kirigami Cut Geometry Programming
nodes.description: Use kirigami cut characteristics, including symmetry and cut width, to influence deformation localization and resulting 3D geometry.
nodes.function: Guide geometry selection for planar-to-3D mechanically assembled structures.
nodes.mechanism: Cuts create compliant joints and redirect membrane deformation into designed bending, twisting, buckling, and topology-selection modes.

nodes.label: Laminated Epidermal Sensing Platform
nodes.description: Laminate a thin, compliant electronic sheet onto skin to maintain intimate, low-burden contact for physiological or environmental sensing.
nodes.function: Provide unobtrusive epidermal sensing during body motion.
nodes.mechanism: Ultrathin low-modulus layers conform to skin through adhesion, van der Waals coupling, or compliant encapsulation while integrated sensors acquire signals.

nodes.label: Laminated Functional Multilayer Stack
nodes.description: Assemble independently formed functional layers into laminated stacks using compliant or insulating interlayers to combine mechanical, electrical, optical, or energy functions.
nodes.function: Increase functional density, robustness, output, or frequency capability without proportional planar expansion.
nodes.mechanism: Preformed layers are vertically separated and coupled through lamination, compliant interlayers, dielectric isolation, spatial offsets, or series connections.

nodes.label: Laser-Triggered Noncontact Transfer
nodes.description: Trigger delamination of a solid object or ink from a compliant transfer tool with a laser pulse and propel it toward a nearby receiver without direct receiver contact.
nodes.function: Place micro- or nanoscale solids across a small gap while avoiding direct receiver contact.
nodes.mechanism: Localized laser heating and thermo-mechanical mismatch generate interfacial stress or energy release sufficient to detach and eject the object.

nodes.label: Layered Finite-Element Thermal Validation
nodes.description: Validate multilayer-device thermal behavior by comparing finite-element heat-transfer predictions with spatial or duty-cycle temperature measurements.
nodes.function: Assess heating, localization, and thermal safety in layered devices and interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Device, encapsulation, substrate, and surrounding tissue domains are modeled with finite elements and compared against measured thermal responses.
failure_modes: model mismatch in tissue or boundary conditions
unmodeled convection or biological heat transfer

nodes.label: Layered or Cavity-Isolating Barrier Encapsulation
nodes.description: Combine multiple barrier layers, seals, or an internal cavity to interrupt fluid pathways and preserve transient device function.
nodes.function: Extend temporary protection and contain fragile structures or degradation products during implantation.
nodes.mechanism: Inorganic-organic stacks, edge seals, wax sandwiches, oil layers, or air gaps create serial diffusion resistance and isolate active regions from biofluid.

nodes.label: Layered-Substrate Elastic Buckling Model
nodes.description: Predict thin-film buckling geometry by minimizing film bending and membrane energies coupled to elastic energy in a compliant or layered substrate.
nodes.function: Estimate wavelength, amplitude, onset, and strain response for conventional elastic buckling systems.
nodes.mechanism: Assume a prescribed wave shape, formulate analytical film and substrate energy terms, and minimize total energy over amplitude and wave number.
failure_modes: Incorrect predictions if slipping, plasticity, fracture, or finite-substrate effects dominate
Mode selection may require additional constraints or energy terms
Reduced accuracy at very low stiffness ratios
Simplified displacement functions may not capture bottom-layer deformation
Small-deformation model error at large prestrain
Unmodeled slip or local substrate heterogeneity

nodes.label: Loading-Path 2D-to-3D Programming
nodes.description: Use different deformation or loading sequences to alter the resulting 3D buckled geometry.
nodes.function: Create switchable or multistable 3D states.
nodes.mechanism: Nonlinear buckling energy landscapes and path-dependent loading alter the accessible stable configurations and transition probabilities.
failure_modes: parasitic adhesion or stiction causes unintended mode selection
positive energy barrier prevents mode transition

nodes.label: Local–Global Buckling Mode Selection Criterion
nodes.description: Select local or global buckling by comparing mode-specific critical strains or a critical geometric length.
nodes.function: Guide geometry selection and prevent unintended buckling modes.
nodes.mechanism: Calculate competing local and global instability thresholds; their equality defines the transition boundary.
failure_modes: Applying the criterion outside the assumed boundary conditions
Global buckling when local buckling is intended
Incorrect mode prediction if shear or geometry assumptions fail
Using a local-buckling model when global buckling dominates

nodes.label: Local Wireless Real-Time Monitoring
nodes.description: Continuously acquire wearable signals, transmit them wirelessly to a nearby device, and perform immediate display or automated interpretation.
nodes.function: Provide real-time monitoring and event interpretation from continuously acquired wearable signals.
nodes.mechanism: Embedded processing or digitization sends sensor data over a short-range wireless link to a nearby interface where signals are displayed or analyzed.

nodes.label: Localized Pulsed Thermal Source Modeling
nodes.description: Use analytical or finite-element scaling models for pulsed localized heating to predict temperature rise as a function of pulse duration, spot size, incident power, and interfacial thermal resistance.
nodes.function: Select heating conditions and estimate thermal exposure or damage.
nodes.mechanism: Represent the source spatially, solve transient conduction through layered materials with interface resistance, and nondimensionalize the result where appropriate.
failure_modes: Model error outside the stated geometric or pulse-regime assumptions
Overheating or ablating retained semiconducting elements
large uncertainty from poorly known absorption
thermal damage at excessive peak temperature

nodes.label: Localized Transient Heater-Response Fitting
nodes.description: Estimate effective thermal properties by fitting the time-dependent response of a calibrated localized heater to a transient heat-transfer model.
nodes.function: Convert controlled heating transients into conductivity, diffusivity, heat-capacity, hydration, or related property estimates.
nodes.mechanism: Known Joule heating produces a local temperature-time response that is interpreted with plane-source, point-source, analytical, numerical, or calibrated inverse models.

nodes.label: Master-Clock Broadcast Synchronization
nodes.description: Broadcast a master or primary node clock periodically to remote sensor nodes so their timestamps remain aligned.
nodes.function: Correct clock drift and establish a common timing reference across separated nodes.
nodes.mechanism: A primary device transmits local clock information over a wireless link at fixed intervals; secondary nodes update local clocks before timestamping measurements.
design_handles: Number and placement of sensor sites

nodes.label: Measurement-Calibrated Full-Wave Modeling
nodes.description: Match full-wave predictions to measured optical response to calibrate models, retrieve effective properties, or quantify modeled contributions to observed spectra.
nodes.function: Connect measured transmission, reflection, or absorption to modeled optical properties and device behavior.
nodes.mechanism: Simulate the measured geometry with dispersive materials and compare calculated spectra or derived absorption with experiments, optionally extracting effective indices or component contributions.
failure_modes: Model-experiment discrepancies from dimensional or coating-thickness variation

nodes.label: Mechanically matched conformal skin coupling
nodes.description: Match device thickness, modulus, and stretchability to skin so the interface follows body motion with low relative displacement.
nodes.function: Maintain stable, low-artifact coupling to moving skin.
nodes.mechanism: Ultrathin low-modulus substrates, stretchable interconnects, and compliant adhesion reduce bending and interfacial mismatch.

nodes.label: Mechanically Tuned Capacitive LC Readout
nodes.description: Convert pressure, strain, or deformation-induced capacitance changes into wireless LC resonance shifts.
nodes.function: Provide battery-free wireless measurement of mechanical loading or deformation.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical displacement changes electrode geometry or separation, shifting capacitance and the inductively interrogated resonance frequency.
failure_modes: drift from water permeation or material degradation

nodes.label: Mechanics-Constrained Radial Electrode Modeling
nodes.description: Model strain and radial-displacement compatibility in concentric reactive Si/Ge layers during lithiation, including compressive constraint from differential expansion.
nodes.function: Guide radial layer selection and estimate strain buffering in layered electrodes.
nodes.mechanism: Layer-specific free expansion is constrained by force equilibrium and continuity of radial displacement at bonded concentric interfaces.
failure_modes: Invalidity for fracture, plasticity, or debonding
Uncertainty in fully lithiated material properties
invalidity under severe plasticity or morphological reconstruction

nodes.label: Mechanics–Electromagnetic Co-Design
nodes.description: Use mechanically predicted deformed geometries to calculate deformation-dependent electromagnetic, capacitive, inductive, or RF behavior.
nodes.function: Design and validate wireless or electromagnetic devices under bending, stretching, or buckling.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical models provide deformed geometry or strain; electromagnetic solvers or analytical field models compute capacitance, inductance, impedance, resonance, radiation, or coupling response.
failure_modes: Weak coupling at small coil size

nodes.label: Mechanics-Guided Functional Geometry Co-Design
nodes.description: Use mechanics-based relations or simulation to jointly select geometry, materials, and layout for a target functional, structural, or mechanical response under deformation or loading.
nodes.function: Co-design deformable structures against functional and mechanical objectives.
nodes.mechanism: Reduced or finite-element mechanics maps design parameters to impact transmission, electromagnetic drift, stress, overlap, inversion behavior, or effective material properties.

nodes.label: Mechanics–Optical Biophysical Modeling
nodes.description: Transfer mechanically predicted device or interface geometries into optical or coupled biophysical simulations to predict functional behavior.
nodes.function: Guide mechanically reconfigurable photonic or tissue-interfacing device design.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanics models determine buckling, spacing, strain, contact, or deformation fields, which are supplied to optical transport, electromagnetic, thermal, or tissue-interaction models.
failure_modes: Weak coupling at small coil size

nodes.label: Membrane and Plate Buckling Mechanics Model
nodes.description: Predict buckling geometry and strain of laterally extended thin films or membranes on compliant substrates by minimizing coupled plate or membrane and substrate energies.
nodes.function: Guide two-dimensional thin-film or membrane buckling design and interpretation.
nodes.mechanism: Plate or membrane elasticity is coupled to substrate deformation through a total-energy formulation whose minimization yields wavelength, amplitude, stress, and strain response.
failure_modes: Inadequate profile for very long inactivated regions
disagreement between thermal and actual film strain
fracture when predicted peak strain exceeds material limit
long herringbone wavelength may be energetically weakly selected

nodes.label: Metallized Opening Interconnects
nodes.description: Connect vertically separated layers by exposing buried contacts through etched or sloped openings and routing deposited metal across the resulting topology.
nodes.function: Route signals and power between stacked or topographically separated device layers.
nodes.mechanism: Planarization and patterned openings expose contacts, while evaporated or lithographically patterned metal bridges the openings and step transitions.

nodes.label: Microchannel Self-Registered Electrode Definition
nodes.description: Use a patterned microchannel or conformal fluidic carrier to define source/drain placement and transistor channel dimensions over an active semiconductor.
nodes.function: Form and register electrode structures while reducing lithographic alignment requirements.
nodes.mechanism: Channel walls, fluid plugs, or a laminated microfluidic carrier establish electrode locations and channel dimensions through geometric confinement and self-registration.

nodes.label: Miniaturized Flexible NFC Interface
nodes.description: Implement near-field communication with energy harvesting through a 13.56 MHz NFC antenna.
nodes.function: Provide wireless power and communication in a small flexible form factor.
nodes.mechanism: An inductive NFC antenna couples to an external reader; the NFC electronics rectify energy and process or transmit signals.
failure_modes: Electromagnetic degradation at sufficiently small bending radius
Reduced coupling as coil size decreases
reduced transmission distance with antenna miniaturization

nodes.label: Mismatch-Strain Crystalline-Substrate Growth
nodes.description: Directly grow compositionally tunable semiconductor nanowire arrays on mismatched crystalline substrates without metal catalyst particles or prepatterning.
nodes.function: Create ordered heteroepitaxial nanowire arrays directly integrated with crystalline substrates.
nodes.mechanism: Mismatch strain drives catalyst-free nucleation and one-dimensional epitaxial growth, while nanowire geometry laterally relaxes lattice mismatch.
failure_modes: Irregular nanoneedles or islands above the critical diameter

nodes.label: Model–Experiment Deformation Validation
nodes.description: Validate mechanics-based device or structure predictions against measured deformation, force, strain, shape, or functional response.
nodes.function: Assess whether modeled mechanics represent fabricated or biological systems under controlled loading.
nodes.mechanism: Numerical, theoretical, or constitutive predictions are compared with independent physical measurements or observed configurations.
failure_modes: Agreement does not establish experimental confirmation.
Agreement limited to tested parameter range
Model discrepancy at very compliant crease or base regions

nodes.label: Modulus-Tuned Relief Replication
nodes.description: Use higher-modulus PDMS formulations such as h-PDMS to improve nanoscale replication and reduce sagging under specified transfer conditions.
nodes.function: Tune stamp mechanics for accurate replication and selective pickup or placement.
nodes.mechanism: Higher modulus and yield stress limit deformation and collapse of fine or high-aspect-ratio relief, subject to a conformability tradeoff.

nodes.label: Molded Soft Fluid-Sealed Enclosure
nodes.description: Mold or cast a continuous low-modulus elastomer around electronics to create a fluid-sealed, mechanically buffering enclosure.
nodes.function: Protect electronics from water, biofluid, and external mechanical loading while preserving compliant operation.
nodes.mechanism: A continuous cured elastomer surrounds and electrically isolates components; its low modulus buffers rigid parts and limits stress transfer.

nodes.label: Monolithic Degradable Barrier Encapsulation
nodes.description: Use a single conformal degradable barrier layer whose composition, hydrophobicity, or dissolution rate delays fluid ingress before programmed resorption.
nodes.function: Maintain temporary device operation by postponing aqueous exposure with one degradable barrier layer.
nodes.mechanism: Polymer or other slowly dissolving films regulate water uptake and transport through composition, crystallinity, hydrophobicity, thickness, and hydrolytic erosion.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo Tissue Optical Propagation Modeling
nodes.description: Use Monte Carlo simulations to model spatial light illumination and propagation in turbid, absorptive, or scattering tissue-like media and compare selected predictions with experiments.
nodes.function: Predict illumination profiles, penetration, fluence, detector response, and optical dose in tissue.
nodes.mechanism: Photon packets are propagated through tissue geometry with wavelength-dependent absorption, scattering, and anisotropy; predictions may be compared with phantom, ex vivo, or in situ measurements.

nodes.label: Multi-Source Thermal Superposition
nodes.description: Estimate the temperature increase in a multi-source array from a single-source thermal response by superposition under a linear thermal-response assumption.
nodes.function: Extend single-source thermal solutions to arbitrary multi-source layouts.
nodes.mechanism: Evaluate each source response at the observation point and sum contributions under an approximately linear heat-transfer model; frequency and spacing determine coupling.
failure_modes: Strong source coupling not represented by linear superposition

nodes.label: Multiband Mechano-Acoustic Feature Extraction
nodes.description: Separate low- and high-frequency inertial signals to derive synchronized physiological, activity, orientation, and acoustic features.
nodes.function: Provide multi-observable monitoring from a shared inertial sensing stream.
nodes.mechanism: Frequency- and axis-selective filtering maps acceleration components to cardiopulmonary, behavioral, orientation, and acoustic observables.

nodes.label: Multichannel or multiresonant NFC networking
nodes.description: Use channel multiplexing, separate resonances, or multiple reader antennas to operate multiple wireless sensing or power domains.
nodes.function: Scale near-field operation across channels, loads, or distributed nodes.
nodes.mechanism: Multiplexers, frequency-separated coils, or sequentially selected antennas partition wireless paths.
failure_modes: Data loss if buffering is inadequate

nodes.label: Multilayer Barrier-Coupled Lifetime Model
nodes.description: Model transient-layer lifetime by coupling diffusion through one or more barrier or encapsulation layers to reaction-driven loss in an underlying functional layer.
nodes.function: Predict barrier-limited material loss and device lifetime.
nodes.mechanism: Layer-specific diffusion and reaction equations are coupled through concentration and flux continuity, and evolving thickness or resistance defines lifetime.
failure_modes: Ignoring intermediate eigenvalue regimes can substantially alter predicted thickness loss
Parameter transfer across environments without recalibration
Thin-layer approximation can be inaccurate for thick encapsulation
continuum approximation may not capture atomic-scale reactivity
extrapolation outside tested pH and temperature ranges

nodes.label: Multilayer biofluid-barrier encapsulation
nodes.description: Combine conformal fluid-barrier layers with soft tissue-facing encapsulation to protect implanted electronics while preserving compliant integration.
nodes.function: Suppress biofluid ingress, corrosion, and mechanical irritation during implantation.
nodes.mechanism: Dense conformal polymer or parylene barriers isolate electronics while elastomeric outer layers distribute load and match tissue mechanics.

nodes.label: Multilayer Compressive-Buckling Assembly
nodes.description: Assemble aligned, selectively bonded multilayer planar precursors and collectively buckle them to form coupled, nested, or entangled three-dimensional architectures.
nodes.function: Create multilayer 3D structures with topology and mechanical coupling unavailable to single-layer buckling.
nodes.mechanism: Layer-by-layer transfer and selective bonding coordinate independent 2D precursors during compressive buckling while preserving over-under or nested relationships.

nodes.label: Multilayer Transient Circuit Integration
nodes.description: Build transient circuits from stacked dissolvable conductor, dielectric, support, via, and component layers whose staged degradation or dissolution controls circuit lifetime.
nodes.function: Provide temporary multilayer interconnection, RF, sensing, or circuit functionality.
nodes.mechanism: Vertically stacked transient metal patterns, dielectric interlayers, vias, and soluble supports form a circuit whose layer-specific degradation produces staged functional loss or disappearance.

nodes.label: Multimodal implant performance validation
nodes.description: Validate implantable bioelectronic performance by combining mechanical endurance, functional operation, thermal or environmental safety, tissue integration, and application-level outcomes.
nodes.function: Establish that an implant remains mechanically reliable, functionally effective, and biologically tolerated under deployment conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Independent tests measure cyclic deformation, electrical or optical function, thermal exposure, tissue capture or integration, electrophysiology, histology, and behavioral or physiological compatibility.
failure_modes: Failure criterion dependent on measurement choice
Failure to separate function loss from material disappearance
False functional pass from device output without tissue capture

nodes.label: Multimodal Wearable Monitoring Platform
nodes.description: Use skin-interfaced wearable platforms to combine physiological, motion, biochemical, colorimetric, or electrochemical sensing for real-time or continuous monitoring.
nodes.function: Acquire and interpret multiple physiological or biochemical signals from a wearable interface.
nodes.mechanism: A compliant platform combines distinct sensors, assay modules, electronics, and communication or readout paths at a shared deployment site.

nodes.label: Nanostructure Coverage–Alignment Tradeoff
nodes.description: Increase catalyst-mediated nanostructure coverage only within a process regime that preserves alignment and limits bundling, oversized growth, and out-of-plane formation.
nodes.function: Select catalyst density and growth conditions for aligned arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Higher catalyst density increases nucleation and coverage but promotes larger elements and bundles that reduce alignment and block guided growth.

nodes.label: Near-Field Aligned Fibrous Jet Printing
nodes.description: Use near-field electrospinning with fast substrate motion to produce aligned structures.
nodes.function: Create continuous aligned nanoscale polymer features.
nodes.mechanism: A fibrous jet is deposited at short working distance while fast substrate motion stretches and aligns it and suppresses whipping.

nodes.label: Near-Field Phase-Shift Resist Patterning
nodes.description: Use a conformal relief-bearing elastomeric mask to create localized near-field exposure features in a resist or photosensitive layer.
nodes.function: Pattern nanoscale or submicrometer planar resist features over broad areas.
nodes.mechanism: Relief-induced phase shifts and near-field diffraction create spatial exposure maxima and minima that selectively expose or preserve resist regions.
failure_modes: Insufficient structure away from the mask surface
Loss of intensity visibility with depth

nodes.label: Neural Circuit and Behavioral Validation
nodes.description: Link intervention delivery to local neural activation, downstream circuit response, and organism-level behavior.
nodes.function: Establish causal neural and behavioral consequences of an intervention.
nodes.mechanism: Stimulus-evoked electrophysiology, downstream recordings, anatomical confirmation, and behavioral assays are aligned across intervention states.

nodes.label: Neutral-plane active-layer protection
nodes.description: Embed a strain-sensitive active layer within a stiffness-balanced multilayer so it lies near the neutral mechanical plane during deformation.
nodes.function: Protect active devices and interconnects from bending-induced strain.
nodes.mechanism: Layer thicknesses and moduli position the active layer near the zero-axial-strain plane.
failure_modes: Active layer displaced from neutral plane
Active-layer strain exceeding fracture or performance limits

nodes.label: Neutral-plane mechanical strain balancing
nodes.description: Place strain-sensitive functional layers near the zero-strain plane of a bent multilayer laminate by balancing layer thicknesses and stiffnesses.
nodes.function: Reduce bending strain and improve mechanical reliability of flexible systems.
nodes.mechanism: Symmetric or stiffness-balanced encapsulation positions the active layer near the plane of minimal axial strain during bending.

nodes.label: Neutral-plane strain balancing
nodes.description: Position a strain-sensitive functional layer near the neutral mechanical plane of a tunable multilayer stack to reduce bending-induced strain.
nodes.function: Improve bend tolerance and preserve functional-layer integrity.
nodes.mechanism: Layer stiffnesses and thicknesses locate the zero-bending-strain plane; placing the active layer near it reduces tensile and compressive strain during curvature.
failure_modes: Active layer positioned away from neutral plane
Fracture or delamination if strain is not balanced
fracture if active strain exceeds threshold
fracture or performance loss when active-layer strain exceeds allowable strain
loss of response if mechanical coupling is reduced excessively

nodes.label: Non-Imaging Ray-Tracing Validation
nodes.description: Use non-sequential ray transport through multilayer, concentrator, or scattering geometries to predict efficiency, angular response, coupling, irradiance, or losses and compare with measurements.
nodes.function: Validate optical transport and collection performance.
nodes.mechanism: Incident rays are propagated through three-dimensional interfaces and materials while accounting for reflection, absorption, dispersion, scattering, or total internal reflection.
failure_modes: Mismatch between simulated and fabricated geometry
Unmodeled geometric contact or gap defects

nodes.label: Noncoplanar Buckled Island–Bridge Interconnect
nodes.description: Use prestrain-generated buckling or waviness in compliant bridges to absorb substrate deformation while protecting rigid active islands.
nodes.function: Enable large deformation with low strain in active devices.
nodes.mechanism: Excess interconnect length converts in-plane deformation into out-of-plane buckling, arcs, or waves concentrated between islands.

nodes.label: Nonlinear Postbuckling FEA Design
nodes.description: Use nonlinear finite-element postbuckling simulations to select layouts and predict transformed geometry, strain, contact, and instability before fabrication.
nodes.function: Design and validate complex mechanically transformed 3D structures.
nodes.mechanism: Material, interface, contact, and geometric nonlinearities are solved under prescribed loading or triggering conditions to obtain postbuckled configurations and fields.

nodes.label: Nonplanar Buckled Interconnect
nodes.description: Use three-dimensional or buckled serpentine interconnect geometries to accommodate deformation through combined in-plane and out-of-plane motion.
nodes.function: Preserve electrical routing under multidirectional stretching, twisting, or articulation.
nodes.mechanism: Preformed or compliant serpentine paths bend, twist, buckle, and change height or projected geometry, suppressing strain localization in the conductor.
failure_modes: Resonance shift from altered spacing or geometry

nodes.label: Numerical Curved-Array Mechanics
nodes.description: Use finite-element or coupled structural mechanics to predict curved-array deformation, local strain, stress, contact, and transformation thresholds from layout and loading.
nodes.function: Assess curved integration, mechanical safety, and geometry selection before fabrication or operation.
nodes.mechanism: Numerical models resolve substrate, device layers, interfaces, contact, mismatch strain, and nonlinear deformation across the transformed array.
failure_modes: Mismatch between ideal and fabricated geometry
Model error outside assumed deformation regime
Model mismatch from uncertain adhesion or material properties
Neglected local effects at detector/interconnect boundaries

nodes.label: Numerical Mechanics Shape Optimization
nodes.description: Use numerical or coupled mechanics models to iteratively select geometry, material, substrate, or actuation parameters that approach a target deformation or strain state.
nodes.function: Optimize shape-producing designs under material, loading, and interface constraints.
nodes.mechanism: Forward mechanics or multiphysics models predict deformation and strain, and iterative refinement or constrained optimization reduces error to the target response.
failure_modes: High computational cost for nonlinear models

nodes.label: Open-Mesh Stretchable Interface
nodes.description: Use sparse open-mesh or serpentine interconnect architectures to provide deformable, low-constraint skin interfaces.
nodes.function: Maintain sensing contact across curved and moving tissue.
nodes.mechanism: Open conductive meshes and serpentine traces reduce effective stiffness and accommodate large in-plane deformation.

nodes.label: Opsin-Gated Cell-Targeted Modulation
nodes.description: Express excitatory or inhibitory opsins in selected neuronal populations and illuminate them to control activity with cellular specificity.
nodes.function: Activate or silence genetically defined neural populations.
nodes.mechanism: Wavelength-sensitive opsins alter membrane conductance, depolarization, or hyperpolarization when illuminated.

nodes.label: Optical Sacrificial Corrosion Indicator
nodes.description: Detect barrier breakthrough by visually monitoring dissolution or degradation of a sacrificial water-reactive indicator beneath the barrier.
nodes.function: Screen and compare barrier lifetime using an optical endpoint.
nodes.mechanism: Ingressing water reacts with the sacrificial metal, producing visible dissolution or defect formation; the first observable change defines breakthrough.
failure_modes: inability to distinguish bulk from pinhole failure
indicator response after an already-existing defect

nodes.label: Paired Comparator-Instrument or Assay Agreement
nodes.description: Validate a candidate measurement by comparing the same quantity with an independent instrument, assay, or modality and quantifying agreement.
nodes.function: Establish quantitative accuracy, calibration transfer, and correspondence to an accepted measurement standard.
nodes.mechanism: Acquire paired outputs under matched samples, locations, subjects, or perturbations, then compare values, trajectories, correlations, or agreement statistics.
failure_modes: Different optical or mechanical sampling volumes

nodes.label: Paired-Reference-Path Ratiometric Readout
nodes.description: Measure sample and reference optical paths together and use their ratio to suppress shared illumination and detector disturbances.
nodes.function: Provide robust optical quantification under variable conditions.
nodes.mechanism: A sample path and comparatively invariant reference path are measured under common conditions; their ratio is mapped to concentration, dose, or assay state.

nodes.label: Paired Reference-Response Calibration
nodes.description: Map sensor output to a quantitative measurand by pairing measurements with known standards or an independent reference under matched conditions.
nodes.function: Translate raw sensor, optical, or electrical responses into interpretable physical, chemical, or physiological quantities.
nodes.mechanism: Candidate and reference responses are acquired over known conditions, then related through a fitted curve, factor, lookup table, or response model.

nodes.label: Paired-Site Differential Mechanoacoustic Sensing
nodes.description: Coordinate mechanically coupled sensors at two anatomical sites to compare or jointly interpret local motion and tissue-conducted signals.
nodes.function: Disambiguate synchronized physiological events using spatially separated measurements.
nodes.mechanism: Two wireless or flexibly interconnected inertial sensors acquire time-aligned signals from complementary body locations for differential or joint analysis.
failure_modes: insufficient temperature accuracy in short measurements

nodes.label: Passive Channel-Reservoir Assay
nodes.description: Use passive skin-accessible channels and reservoirs to collect biofluid and expose it to localized assays.
nodes.function: Provide low-complexity on-body fluid collection and chemical analysis.
nodes.mechanism: Natural secretion pressure, capillarity, or passive channel geometry transports fluid from the skin to assay chambers or sensing regions.

nodes.label: Passive Compliant Thermal Encapsulation
