nodes.description: Use compliant layered encapsulation to seal and thermally buffer device components or actuators from the surrounding interface.
nodes.function: Provide environmental protection and reduce heat transfer or thermal noise at a conformal interface.
nodes.mechanism: Elastomeric, insulating, or dissipative layers increase thermal resistance, spread heat, suppress convection, and preserve compliant contact.

nodes.label: Passive Conformal Electrode Mesh
nodes.description: Use flexible distributed electrodes and compliant interconnects to maintain tissue contact during deformation without requiring active electronics at each array site.
nodes.function: Record or stimulate electrophysiology across curved or moving tissue surfaces with low mechanical and wiring burden.
nodes.mechanism: Thin flexible or stretchable electrode meshes conform to tissue geometry while routing signals to external acquisition or stimulation electronics.

nodes.label: Passive NFC Epidermal Electronics
nodes.description: Use ultrathin conformal NFC or resonant structures for battery-free skin sensing, optical interfacing, or wireless communication.
nodes.function: Enable unobtrusive near-field power, sensing, and data exchange on skin.
nodes.mechanism: Inductive NFC coupling or passive LC resonance powers or interrogates compliant epidermal electronics and sensing elements.

nodes.label: Passive-Sweat Microfluidic Multimodal Monitoring
nodes.description: Route naturally produced sweat through shared microfluidics to multiple biochemical assays while measuring sweat dynamics and auxiliary physiology.
nodes.function: Provide simultaneous or time-resolved biochemical and biophysical sweat monitoring.
nodes.mechanism: Microfluidic channels or sequential reservoirs distribute sweat to electrochemical, colorimetric, fluorescence, or immunoassay regions, with temperature, motion, conductivity, or flow sensing added for context.

nodes.label: PAT-Based Blood-Pressure Surrogate
nodes.description: Estimate blood pressure from synchronized ECG/PPG-derived PAT and HR after an initial calibration against reference BP, as demonstrated in specified subject cohorts.
nodes.function: Estimate SBP and DBP noninvasively and continuously.
nodes.mechanism: Extract PAT, optionally with HR, from synchronized ECG and PPG signals; fit the features to reference blood-pressure measurements and apply the calibrated model to subsequent observations.
design_handles: choice of linear or nonlinear model

nodes.label: Patterned-Adhesion Buckling Programming
nodes.description: Program buckled 3D thin-film geometry by combining spatially patterned adhesion with precursor layout and released substrate prestrain.
nodes.function: Control buckling wavelength, amplitude, phase, and topology during planar-to-3D transformation.
nodes.mechanism: Bonded regions anchor the precursor while released regions delaminate or buckle under compressive prestrain; layout and bonding pattern select the deformation mode.
failure_modes: Cracking from overly narrow inactive regions
Very long inactivated regions causing short-wave modes

nodes.label: Percolation-Network Resistance Modulation
nodes.description: Convert deformation into resistance change by altering connectivity and separation within a deformable percolating conductive network.
nodes.function: Measure strain, pressure, or motion through deformation-dependent electrical resistance.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical loading changes interparticle spacing, contact connectivity, and conductive-path percolation in a particle-filled elastomer.

nodes.label: Percolation-Threshold Striping
nodes.description: Use finite-width patterning and selective removal to raise the effective percolation threshold above the unwanted conduction population while preserving useful transport.
nodes.function: Improve transistor ON/OFF ratio while retaining substantial ON-current.
nodes.mechanism: Patterning shortens effective elements near boundaries and interrupts metallic-only spanning paths, shifting the effective threshold.
failure_modes: Excessively narrow stripes increase current variability
Residual metallic path bridges source and drain
Short channels remain vulnerable to direct metallic bridging

nodes.label: Perforated breathable skin interface
nodes.description: Introduce distributed openings into a skin-mounted platform to increase stretchability, moisture transport, and wear tolerance.
nodes.function: Improve breathable, compliant, continuous skin integration.
nodes.mechanism: Perforations interrupt continuous encapsulation or support layers, creating deformation and vapor pathways while retaining device integration.

nodes.label: Perfusion-Coupled Tissue Heat-Transfer Inversion
nodes.description: Infer vascular-flow dynamics by fitting transient multilayer tissue heat-transfer models with perfusion-dependent blood–tissue exchange to measured temperature histories.
nodes.function: Convert tissue-surface thermal transients into time-varying perfusion or blood-flow dynamics.
nodes.mechanism: A multilayer transient conduction model couples blood-flow-dependent artery-wall or perfusion heat exchange to tissue temperature, with flow parameters fitted to measurements.
failure_modes: confounding between fluid content and velocity
large sensor-heater distance causing high relative error

nodes.label: Periodic-Relief Equivalent-Crack Collapse
nodes.description: Model collapse of periodic compliant relief using an equivalent-crack representation and energy minimization over the contacting region.
nodes.function: Estimate collapse extent and equilibrium contact for periodic relief structures.
nodes.mechanism: Relief grooves are represented as periodic cracks; deformation energy is balanced against adhesion-energy gain as contact expands.
failure_modes: Incorrect prediction if material nonlinearities or kinetics dominate
Model invalid when collapse length exceeds post spacing
model assumptions violated by non-cylindrical patterns
poor transfer of calibrated parameter across geometries

nodes.label: Photoactivated Color Change
nodes.description: Use optical stimulus exposure to activate or transform indicator chemistry that produces a persistent measurable color change.
nodes.function: Visually estimate optical stimulus dose or exposure.
nodes.mechanism: Absorbed photons activate a photosensitive species or dye response, changing visible absorption or hue in a responsive matrix.

nodes.label: Photocurable Elastomeric Mold or Stamp Fabrication
nodes.description: Photocure an elastomeric precursor against a patterned master to create a conformable relief-bearing mold or stamp for repeated pattern transfer.
nodes.function: Create reusable elastomeric patterning elements.
nodes.mechanism: A liquid precursor fills or coats a patterned master and is crosslinked by light into a dimensionally stable elastomeric replica that can be released and reused.
failure_modes: incomplete transfer from insufficient conformal contact

nodes.label: Physics-Based Forward Response Modeling
nodes.description: Predict device or system responses from coupled constitutive, transport, optical, fluidic, or mechanical equations under specified geometry and loading conditions.
nodes.function: Translate physical inputs and design parameters into measurable electrical, optical, flow, or delivery responses.
nodes.mechanism: A forward analytical or reduced-order physics model maps material properties, geometry, loading, and boundary conditions to observables, optionally using nondimensional scaling or calibration.

nodes.label: Physics-Based Parameter Inversion
nodes.description: Recover material, geometric, or device parameters by fitting measured electrical, resonant, or wave responses to a physics-based forward model.
nodes.function: Estimate otherwise inaccessible properties such as modulus, density, thickness, or viscoelastic parameters.
nodes.mechanism: Measured observables are mapped through coupled mechanics, electromechanics, resonance, or viscoelastic relations and solved by fitting, minimization, or simultaneous inversion.

nodes.label: Physiological-Triggered Neuromodulation
nodes.description: Detect a physiological or neural state and conditionally activate a therapeutic stimulation actuator.
nodes.function: Deliver state-dependent real-time neuromodulation or electrotherapy.
nodes.mechanism: Physiological signals are processed into thresholds or state features that trigger electrical, optical, or related stimulation.

nodes.label: Piezoelectric Pair Modulus Sensing
nodes.description: Infer local soft-tissue modulus from the mechanically coupled electrical response of a driven piezoelectric actuator and neighboring piezoelectric sensor.
nodes.function: Measure localized modulus on compliant or biological surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Inverse-piezoelectric actuation deforms the substrate and tissue; adjacent direct-effect piezoelectric sensing produces a voltage or voltage ratio calibrated to modulus.
failure_modes: non-monotonic response at high or low modulus
reduced deformation and signal with overly stiff substrate

nodes.label: Piezoresistive Semiconductor Strain Gauge
nodes.description: Use a strained semiconductor resistor to convert mechanical deformation into a calibrated resistance change.
nodes.function: Measure mechanical strain.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical stress changes semiconductor carrier transport and resistance through the piezoresistive effect.
failure_modes: Mechanical constraint of the target organ
Reduced gauge factor from balanced tensile and compressive stresses

nodes.label: Planar Serpentine Interconnect
nodes.description: Route electrical connections through planar or filamentary serpentine paths that absorb substrate extension through bending, unfolding, and curvature change.
nodes.function: Maintain electrical continuity between rigid or strain-sensitive regions during stretching, bending, or body motion.
nodes.mechanism: Excess in-plane path length and curved segments convert macroscopic deformation into distributed geometric motion, reducing axial conductor strain.
failure_modes: Resonance shift from altered spacing or geometry

nodes.label: Polymer-Protected Release Tethering
nodes.description: Use patterned polymer supports or protective tethers to retain released structures while reducing substrate contact and shielding active regions during etching.
nodes.function: Preserve registration and protect active regions through release and pickup.
nodes.mechanism: Localized polymer supports carry the structure, limit sagging or adhesion, and mask active surfaces until the tether fractures during retrieval.

nodes.label: Prefabricated Wavy-Substrate Integration
nodes.description: Conformally integrate a stiff thin film with a compliant substrate that has prefabricated surface waviness to accommodate deformation without initial film strain.
nodes.function: Provide stretchable and compressible thin-film integration with low initial film strain.
nodes.mechanism: Preformed substrate relief supplies geometric excess length; applied deformation changes wave amplitude and curvature rather than directly stretching the film.
failure_modes: Fracture of the functional layer if geometric accommodation is insufficient
Interfacial delamination when bonding is inadequate
film yielding when maximum strain exceeds critical strain

nodes.label: Pressure-Driven Curved Geometry
nodes.description: Use fluid pressure to transform a compliant membrane carrying functional elements from a planar state into a controlled curved geometry.
nodes.function: Create tunable nonplanar device surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: A sealed fluidic chamber pressurizes an elastomeric membrane against a geometric constraint, producing a prescribed curved or hemispherical state.
failure_modes: high fill factor reduces achievable apex height
regions near constrained corners may remain flat

nodes.label: Pressure-Pulse Inkjet Deposition
nodes.description: Eject functional liquid droplets on demand using thermal or piezoelectric pressure pulses from a nozzle.
nodes.function: Pattern functional inks with digital placement and efficient material use.
nodes.mechanism: Thermal bubble formation or piezoelectric actuation generates a pressure impulse that ejects discrete droplets; pulse parameters tune deposition.

nodes.label: Pressure-Switched Microtip Transfer
nodes.description: Switch stamp adhesion between strong pickup and weak release by preload-induced contact-area collapse followed by elastic or viscoelastic recovery of microstructured tips.
nodes.function: Retrieve and deliver fragile discrete objects with directional adhesion control.
nodes.mechanism: Preload increases contact area for pickup; rapid retraction and subsequent relief recovery reduce contact area and adhesion for release.

nodes.label: Pressure-Threshold Valve Routing
nodes.description: Route or encode fluid sequentially using valves that open at ordered pressure thresholds.
nodes.function: Provide passive time, volume, or pressure-resolved fluid routing.
nodes.mechanism: Capillary bursting valves with distinct pressure thresholds open successively or encode the highest crossed threshold.
failure_modes: backflow or reagent washout if closure fails

nodes.label: Prestrain-Programmed Buckled Interconnect
nodes.description: Prestrain-induced buckling of arc-shaped interconnects can provide geometric stretchability by allowing the interconnects to straighten under applied strain.
nodes.function: Provide stretchable electrical connections between rigid components.
nodes.mechanism: Prestrain release buckles serpentine or ribbon interconnects; later extension unfolds the geometry while limiting conductor strain.

nodes.label: Prestrain-Release Buckled Film
nodes.description: Bond a stiff functional film or ribbon to a compliant prestrained substrate and release the prestrain to form reversible buckles that absorb later deformation.
nodes.function: Enable stretchable or compressible integration of strain-intolerant thin functional layers.
nodes.mechanism: Substrate relaxation converts excess in-plane length into out-of-plane waves whose amplitude, wavelength, or curvature changes under loading.
failure_modes: Fracture of the functional layer if geometric accommodation is insufficient
Interfacial delamination when bonding is inadequate
film yielding when maximum strain exceeds critical strain

nodes.label: Prestrain-Release Island–Bridge Buckling
nodes.description: Use selectively bonded islands and compliant bridges that buckle out of plane after prestrain release to isolate active regions from deformation.
nodes.function: Create highly stretchable electronic layouts while protecting strain-sensitive islands.
nodes.mechanism: Strongly bonded islands remain anchored while weakly bonded bridges convert released prestrain and later extension into bending, twisting, rotation, and buckling.
failure_modes: island fracture under highly localized folding

nodes.label: Prestrain-Release Thin-Film Buckling
nodes.description: Bond a thin stiff functional element to a compliant prestrained substrate and release the prestrain to create geometric buckling that accommodates later deformation.
nodes.function: Provide stretchability and compressibility for strain-intolerant thin materials.
nodes.mechanism: Substrate relaxation imposes compression; adhesion and bending compliance convert excess length into waves or buckles whose geometry changes under subsequent loading.
failure_modes: film fracture when peak strain exceeds fracture strain

nodes.label: Prestrain-Release Thin-Film Wrinkling
nodes.description: Bond a stiff thin film or mesh to a compliant prestrained substrate so release creates wrinkles that flatten under later tension.
nodes.function: Reserve geometric extension while limiting film strain.
nodes.mechanism: Mismatch compression produces wrinkles; applied tension progressively flattens them before direct film stretching dominates.

nodes.label: Prestrain-Timed Encapsulation
nodes.description: Apply solid encapsulation while the electronic system is pre-stretched, then release the prestretch afterward; this strategy can improve elastic stretchability relative to final-stage encapsulation.
nodes.function: Improve stretchability and compliance of encapsulated deformable systems.
nodes.mechanism: Encapsulation timing couples curing to a controlled prestrain or partial-release state; subsequent release creates or preserves compliant out-of-plane geometry.
failure_modes: Leakage or evaporation if liquid encapsulation is used

nodes.label: Programmable Transient Device Lifetime
nodes.description: Match temporary device operation and disappearance to an application interval by coordinating barrier protection, material degradation, geometry, and layer thickness.
nodes.function: Provide useful operation during a defined temporary interval followed by controlled degradation, resorption, or disappearance.
nodes.mechanism: Encapsulation or barrier layers delay fluid access, while material-specific dissolution or degradation kinetics determine later functional loss and clearance.

nodes.label: Programmed Bioresorption
nodes.description: Match device function and post-use disappearance by engineering bioresorption to occur after the required operating interval.
nodes.function: Avoid retrieval of temporary implanted devices.
nodes.mechanism: Bioresorbable materials and their degradation rates are selected to coordinate functional lifetime and clearance.
failure_modes: loss of function before therapeutic endpoint

nodes.label: PU-Embedded Semiconductor Array Transfer
nodes.description: Embed transferred crystalline semiconductor wires in cured PU to prevent movement during bending or twisting.
nodes.function: Provide a mechanically stable flexible plastic host for transferred semiconductor arrays.
nodes.mechanism: An elastomeric stamp transfers the semiconductor elements, while partially and then fully cured PU bonds and immobilizes them on PET.

nodes.label: Pulse-Controlled Droplet Sizing
nodes.description: Control printed feature dimensions by adjusting deposited droplet volume, droplet count, line spacing, or repeated printing passes.
nodes.function: Tune printed width and thickness through deposited material volume and placement density.
nodes.mechanism: Droplet size and the number or spacing of deposited units regulate the material volume delivered to the substrate and therefore feature geometry.
failure_modes: Feature size may be limited by ink spreading or process speed
Roughness for very thin or few-layer patterns

nodes.label: Pulse-Modulated EHD Droplet Sizing
nodes.description: Control EHD droplet size and jetting frequency by adjusting or time-modulating the applied voltage, including pulse-modulated voltage sources.
nodes.function: Expand the controllable droplet-size and printing-frequency operating range.
nodes.mechanism: Baseline voltage prepares the meniscus while pulse amplitude, duration, and interval trigger and size individual ejections.
failure_modes: Droplet-size/frequency coupling outside the controlled regime

nodes.label: Pulsed Thermal Load Management
nodes.description: Use pulse frequency, pulse width, duty cycle, and adequate cooling intervals to reduce tissue thermal load and prevent residual heat accumulation during pulsed operation.
nodes.function: Control transient heating during pulsed stimulation or sensing.
nodes.mechanism: Activation and cooling intervals determine residual heat accumulation and peak temperature.

nodes.label: Pulsed Transient Multilayer Conduction
nodes.description: Use transient layered heat-conduction models with periodic pulse representations to predict peak and time-dependent temperature rise from thin localized heat sources.
nodes.function: Estimate transient thermal exposure during pulsed operation.
nodes.mechanism: Represent pulsed heating through Fourier or equivalent temporal decomposition and solve transient conduction in an axisymmetric multilayer medium with interface and boundary conditions.
failure_modes: Breakdown of thin-source or axisymmetric approximation
Neglect of blood-flow heat loss in living tissue
accuracy degrades outside thin-device or large-substrate assumptions
localized gap temperature measurements can differ from active-device temperature
neglect of convection when it is non-negligible

nodes.label: Raised-Island Recessed-Trench Isolation
nodes.description: Protect strain-sensitive active regions by supporting them on raised stiff islands separated by compliant recessed trenches.
nodes.function: Isolate rigid or brittle devices from global substrate deformation while preserving stretchability and coverage.
nodes.mechanism: Stiffness and relief contrast localize extension, bending, and compression in recessed trench and interconnect regions.
failure_modes: interconnect metal fracture at large deformation

nodes.label: Random Percolation Channel
nodes.description: Use a random one-dimensional-conductor network as a gated thin-film transistor channel whose percolating connectivity is modulated by the gate.
nodes.function: Provide scalable field-effect switching with ensemble-averaged network transport.
nodes.mechanism: A mixed semiconducting and metallic network forms source-drain percolation paths, while gate bias modulates carrier transport through the network.
failure_modes: contact resistance domination at short channel lengths

nodes.label: Rate-Separated Pickup-and-Release Transfer
nodes.description: Separate pickup and release conditions by using rapid retrieval to favor stamp-object adhesion and slow, low-adhesion retraction to release the object onto a receiver.
nodes.function: Deterministically transfer discrete solid objects from donor to receiver.
nodes.mechanism: Rate-dependent viscoelastic adhesion and controlled contact or pressure state produce strong pickup and progressively reduced adhesion during release.
failure_modes: failure to release at low speed
receiver adhesion lower than stamp adhesion

nodes.label: Rate-Tuned Reversible Adhesive Transfer Printing
nodes.description: Control pickup and release of an object or film by tuning the separation rate of a viscoelastic stamp against competing interface fracture energies.
nodes.function: Enable deterministic, repeatable transfer without requiring a fixed adhesive layer.
nodes.mechanism: Viscoelastic stamp toughness increases with peel rate, favoring donor fracture during fast pickup and receiver fracture during slow release.
failure_modes: loss of kinetic control outside the accessible toughness range

nodes.label: RCWA Periodic Optical Validation
nodes.description: Use rigorous coupled-wave analysis to predict optical response of periodic or grating-like structures and compare the predictions with measured or fabricated results.
nodes.function: Model, validate, and tune periodic optical structures.
nodes.mechanism: Fourier-expanded electromagnetic fields and layerwise scattering calculations solve the periodic optical problem from geometry, material properties, and illumination conditions.
failure_modes: Model mismatch from inaccurate optical or material parameters
mismatch between modeled and fabricated geometry

nodes.label: Re-registerable crystal lamination
nodes.description: Laminate a fragile crystal onto a compliant electrode structure, then detach and relaminate it for rework or orientation changes.
nodes.function: Probe fragile anisotropic active crystals through repeated registration and measurement.
nodes.mechanism: Soft van der Waals contact supplies electrical coupling while allowing nondestructive removal and reattachment at a selected orientation.

nodes.label: Recursive Hierarchical Flexibility Modeling
nodes.description: Estimate effective flexibility, deformation, energy, or tensile stiffness of hierarchical and self-similar interconnects by recursively assembling lower-order mechanical representations.
nodes.function: Guide hierarchical geometry selection and enable reduced-order compliance prediction.
nodes.mechanism: Strain-energy equivalence or recursive energy integration propagates lower-order flexibility or stiffness across geometric orders.
failure_modes: inapplicable deformation mode when buckling or other effects dominate
model–experiment deviation at very small force resolution

nodes.label: Reduced Mechanics Cross-Validation
nodes.description: Validate a reduced or analytical mechanics model by comparing predicted deformation, strain, stability, or response with independent numerical calculations and controlled measurements.
nodes.function: Establish the accuracy, applicability range, and design usefulness of simplified mechanics models.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical or reduced-order equations are evaluated under matched geometry and loading, then compared with FEA or FEM fields and measured shapes, strains, forces, thresholds, or functional responses.
failure_modes: Apparent agreement caused by shared assumptions
False agreement from mismatched boundary conditions

nodes.label: Reduced-Order Postbuckling Design
nodes.description: Use analytical or energetic postbuckling relations to map planar geometry and loading to 3D mode, amplitude, wavelength, curvature, and strain.
nodes.function: Rapidly screen and design buckling architectures without full numerical simulation.
nodes.mechanism: Reduced beam, ribbon, energetic, or mode-selection models approximate equilibrium and postbuckling geometry as functions of layout and applied strain.

nodes.label: Reduced-Order Thermal Cross-Validation
nodes.description: Validate or calibrate a reduced analytical or scaling-law thermal model by comparing it with finite-element predictions and controlled measurements.
nodes.function: Assess simplified-model adequacy and support thermal design or parameter estimation.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical or reduced-order predictions are compared with detailed numerical fields and experimental temperature, flow, deformation, or feature-response data across controlled conditions.
failure_modes: Mismatch between experimental and modeled heating conditions

nodes.label: Reference-Calibrated Digital Colorimetry
nodes.description: Use reference-corrected digital color features and calibration curves to convert analyte-responsive color changes into concentration estimates.
nodes.function: Provide quantitative chemical readout with corrected digital imaging.
nodes.mechanism: Color measurements are normalized against a background or color reference, selected RGB or CIELAB features are extracted, and calibrated mappings convert them to analyte concentration.

nodes.label: Reference-Emitter Intensity Normalization
nodes.description: Normalize sample optical intensity by a colocated stable reference emitter or fluorescent region measured under the same conditions.
nodes.function: Reduce loading, illumination, packaging, and detector variability.
nodes.mechanism: Sample intensity is divided by or compared with stable reference-emitter intensity.

nodes.label: Reference-Layer Optical Thickness Calibration
nodes.description: Calibrate a surface-sensitive optical response with known refractive-index or thickness references to estimate unknown interfacial material coverage.
nodes.function: Convert optical contrast or spectral response into quantitative surface-layer thickness or binding estimates.
nodes.mechanism: Characterize reference layers, relate their optical response to thickness or refractive index, and transfer the calibrated relation to unknown samples.
failure_modes: calibration range does not cover thick structures
invalid transfer of calibration between sensors
reference and biological material have different refractive indices

nodes.label: Reference-Normalized Directional Temperature Difference
nodes.description: Normalize upstream–downstream thermal differences by a reference or actuator temperature to suppress common-mode heating and compare flow responses across conditions.
nodes.function: Improve flow-regime or flow-rate interpretation under varying actuation and ambient conditions.
nodes.mechanism: A directional temperature difference is divided by, or jointly referenced to, actuator or co-located reference temperature.

nodes.label: Reference–Replica Functional Comparison
nodes.description: Compare functional optical or device response of a reference structure and its assembled or replicated counterpart under matched conditions.
nodes.function: Determine whether replication or assembly preserves functional performance.
nodes.mechanism: Matched structures are tested through spectra, coupling, focal behavior, morphology, or other functional outputs.
failure_modes: inability to resolve sub-3 nm widths

nodes.label: Registered lenslet concentration
nodes.description: Register refractive or reflective lenslets so focal positions coincide with sparse photovoltaic or optoelectronic microcells.
nodes.function: Increase optical power density delivered to designated microcell receivers.
nodes.mechanism: Lenslet focal spots are aligned to active elements and concentrate incident light onto their small collection areas.

nodes.label: Tethered-Fracture Registered Transfer
nodes.description: Preserve the registration of released microstructures with engineered tethers or perimeter supports until controlled stress concentration fractures the release site during stamp transfer.
nodes.function: Enable deterministic, high-yield transfer of spatially registered beam or platelet arrays.
nodes.mechanism: Anchored structures remain fixed after undercut release; a PDMS stamp applies controlled force, and designed corners, tethers, or pedestals localize fracture for retrieval.
failure_modes: Crack propagation into anchors or beam body

nodes.label: Released anisotropic wire fabrication
nodes.description: Fabricate freestanding or transferable semiconductor wires and ribbons from crystalline wafers by lithographic definition and anisotropic undercutting.
nodes.function: Produce released semiconductor elements for transfer or device integration.
nodes.mechanism: Patterned masks define the geometry; anisotropic dry or wet etching removes surrounding crystal and undercuts the elements, optionally preserving integrated contacts.
failure_modes: Loss of registration if connection points are removed prematurely

nodes.label: Resistive Thermal Property Estimation
nodes.description: Estimate thermal conductivity, diffusivity, or volumetric heat capacity from transient temperature responses of resistive heater-sensor elements.
nodes.function: Characterize thermal transport properties of a contacted or layered material.
nodes.mechanism: Controlled Joule heating produces transient temperature or voltage responses that are fitted to a heat-transfer model or 3ω relation to infer thermal parameters.
failure_modes: Diffusivity is less precisely fitted than conductivity
Layered geometry and convection require calibration
Thermal perturbation from excessive device mass

nodes.label: Resonant inductive coil coupling
nodes.description: Use resonant magnetic coupling between tuned transmitter and receiver coils to deliver wireless operating power to compact electronics.
nodes.function: Provide battery-free or untethered power across a tissue or environmental gap.
nodes.mechanism: An alternating magnetic field induces voltage in a resonant receiver coil; matching, rectification, regulation, and optional local storage condition power for the load.

nodes.label: Resorbable Barb Tissue Anchoring
nodes.description: Use resorbable or biodegradable barbs to temporarily stabilize a probe at a tissue location after insertion.
nodes.function: Provide temporary fixation without permanent retrieval hardware.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical engagement stabilizes placement while the fixation element biodegrades or resorbs on a planned timescale.

nodes.label: Reusable elastomeric imprint molding
nodes.description: Reuse an elastomeric relief mold to transfer micro- or nanoscale patterns into curable materials across multiple cycles.
nodes.function: Produce repeated patterned replicas with low tooling replacement burden.
nodes.mechanism: A durable elastomeric mold retains relief geometry, contacts a curable target, and is peeled away after curing or solidification for reuse.

nodes.label: Reversible contact lamination
nodes.description: Form and release intimate skin contact through temporary supports or releasable compliant adhesion for repeated use.
nodes.function: Enable repeatable placement and removal of fragile skin-mounted devices.
nodes.mechanism: Temporary frames, dissolvable supports, soft adhesion, and compliant encapsulation establish contact without permanent rigid fixation.

nodes.label: Reversible Microtip Transfer Window
nodes.description: Choose compliant microtip relief height, geometry, and preload between lower recovery and upper delamination limits for reversible pickup and release.
nodes.function: Enable stable reversible transfer using collapsible relief structures.
nodes.mechanism: The lower bound ensures elastic recovery overcomes adhesion after unloading, while the upper bound limits restoring-force-driven delamination during retraction.

nodes.label: Reversible soft electrical contact
nodes.description: Establish and remove a conformal electrical contact through soft adhesion without permanent bonding or aggressive processing.
nodes.function: Enable nondestructive, repeatable electrical measurement or interface formation.
nodes.mechanism: A compliant conductor or stamp wets the target and uses van der Waals or weak interfacial adhesion for intimate contact; peeling reverses the interface.

nodes.label: RF antenna scavenging and rectification
nodes.description: Convert incident RF electromagnetic energy into usable DC power with an antenna, matching network, and rectifier.
nodes.function: Power temporary, embedded, or inaccessible electronics without wired connections.
nodes.mechanism: A receiving antenna captures RF energy; impedance elements and diode rectification produce regulated, stored, or directly usable electrical output.

nodes.label: Rigid-Backed Compliant Stamp
nodes.description: Support a compliant patterned elastomer with a rigid or dimensionally stable backing to suppress distortion while retaining conformal contact.
nodes.function: Improve flatness, registration, handling, and deformation control in flexible stamps.
nodes.mechanism: The backing constrains in-plane strain, sagging, thermal deformation, or curvature while the elastomeric surface conforms during contact and release.

nodes.label: Rigid-soft hybrid microfluidic skeleton
nodes.description: Embed dimensionally stable fluidic or optical structures within a compliant elastomeric interface to preserve channel geometry during deformation.
nodes.function: Maintain robust fluidic and optical operation on deformable interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: A stiff printed or molded skeleton defines channels and chambers, while a soft encapsulant supplies sealing, compliance, and skin coupling.

nodes.label: Sacrificial-support undercut release
nodes.description: Release patterned semiconductor films or devices by selectively removing an underlying sacrificial support layer after lithographic and plasma definition.
nodes.function: Produce transferable semiconductor microelements from supported thin films or completed devices.
nodes.mechanism: Patterning and plasma etching define the active elements, followed by isotropic or selective undercutting that removes the supporting layer while freeing the structures.

nodes.label: Sacrificial-Template Inverse Photonic Fabrication
nodes.description: Use a sacrificial three-dimensional polymer template to form an inverse higher-index photonic structure through conformal filling or coating and template removal.
nodes.function: Transfer a polymer-defined periodic three-dimensional geometry into a higher-index photonic structure.
nodes.mechanism: Conformal high-index deposition or filling follows the polymer template; selective removal of the template and intermediate layers leaves the inverse architecture.

nodes.label: Scheduled Sleep-Wake Burst Operation
nodes.description: Alternate low-power sleep states with scheduled sensing, processing, stimulation, or communication bursts.
nodes.function: Reduce average energy use while preserving periodic operation.
nodes.mechanism: Firmware or a controller disables peripherals during idle intervals and wakes selected functions at scheduled times.

nodes.label: Sealed elastomeric wearable enclosure
nodes.description: Seal flexible electronics inside bonded soft elastomer layers to support conformal, durable, and reusable skin deployment.
nodes.function: Protect wearable electronics from sweat, water, contamination, and localized mechanical stress.
nodes.mechanism: Top and bottom elastomer layers form a continuous enclosure around the populated flexible circuit and maintain a soft skin-facing interface.

nodes.label: Sealed multilayer skin lamination
nodes.description: Laminate functional electronics to skin using compliant adhesive, encapsulation, and protective support layers that preserve contact and environmental sealing.
nodes.function: Provide protected, comfortable, skin-conformal deployment.
nodes.mechanism: Low-modulus adhesive layers couple to skin, encapsulation protects electronics, and breathable or strain-limiting supports distribute deformation.

nodes.label: Selective-Bonded Island-Serpentine Isolation
nodes.description: Anchor functional islands selectively while allowing serpentine bridges to lift or buckle out of plane under deformation.
nodes.function: Protect active islands during large substrate deformation while maintaining continuity.
nodes.mechanism: Strong island bonding and weak bridge adhesion localize deformation in noncoplanar serpentine interconnects.

nodes.label: Selective-Bonding Prestrain Buckling
nodes.description: Transform cut planar membranes into deterministic 3D architectures by selectively anchoring them to a prestrained compliant substrate and releasing the prestrain.
nodes.function: Create programmed 3D thin-film architectures by mechanically driven kirigami assembly.
nodes.mechanism: Cuts define compliant deformation pathways, selective bonds anchor regions, and substrate relaxation generates compression, buckling, translation, and rotation in released regions.

nodes.label: Self-Heated Thermal Anemometry
nodes.description: Infer flow from the flow-dependent temperature or resistance of a heated resistive element.
nodes.function: Measure local flow.
nodes.mechanism: Joule heating establishes a thermal perturbation, flow removes heat, and the heated element's temperature-dependent resistance reports the change.

nodes.label: Self-Heated Thermal Property Mapping
nodes.description: Use resistive elements as heaters and thermometers to infer local thermal transport from transient responses.
nodes.function: Characterize thermal behavior or properties.
nodes.mechanism: Joule heating produces a transient, resistance reports temperature, and response analysis yields thermal maps or properties.
failure_modes: Diffusivity is less precisely fitted than conductivity
Layered geometry and convection require calibration

nodes.label: Semiconductor Band-Structure Strain Readout
nodes.description: Mechanical stress or strain in SiC can alter its band structure and produce a piezoresistive response usable in strain or pressure sensing.
nodes.function: Measure deformation electrically in a thin or flexible sensing element.
nodes.mechanism: Mechanical loading alters semiconductor energy bands and carrier transport, producing a calibrated resistance, conductance, or current change.

nodes.label: Semiconductor Thermoresistive Temperature Sensing
nodes.description: Infer temperature from the temperature-dependent electrical conductance or resistance of a semiconductor.
nodes.function: Measure temperature electrically.
nodes.mechanism: Thermal activation of charge carriers changes semiconductor conductance or resistance, which is converted to temperature through calibration.

nodes.label: Separately Optimized Host-Subsystem Integration
nodes.description: Combine a separately optimized active material, device layer, barrier, or geometry with a host substrate or subsystem selected for different mechanical, optical, thermal, or chemical requirements.
nodes.function: Preserve specialized component performance while embedding it in a mechanically compliant, resonant, photovoltaic, transient, or otherwise constrained host.
nodes.mechanism: Functional layers or devices are formed under one set of conditions and then coupled to the host through lamination, bonding, embedding, cavity assembly, geometric strain isolation, or thickness-enabled conformal integration.

nodes.label: Sequential Transfer-Printed Layer Buildup
nodes.description: Build multilayer architectures by repeatedly transferring or printing patterned layers with controlled registration and interlayer joining.
nodes.function: Create stacked, cross-oriented, or three-dimensional functional systems from repeated layer-transfer cycles.
nodes.mechanism: Preformed patterned layers are sequentially printed or transferred; cold welding, dielectric formation, or common etch development preserves coupling between successive levels.

nodes.label: Sequential Wavy-Mold Replication
nodes.description: Use sequential molding from a rigid relief template to create a controlled wavy elastomeric substrate, optionally retaining or transferring a thin surface film.
nodes.function: Fabricate compliant substrates with controlled periodic relief.
nodes.mechanism: Rigid relief is smoothed or shaped, replicated through one or more elastomer molding steps, and cured to preserve the wavy profile.

nodes.label: Serpentine Capacitive RF-Coupling Antenna
nodes.description: Use capacitive coupling between adjacent serpentine traces for RF power harvesting, with a reported 200 MHz bandwidth that broadens the tolerated transmitting-frequency range; retention of harvesting during deformation or environmental detuning is not established.
nodes.function: Harvest and couple RF power in deformable platforms.
nodes.mechanism: Adjacent serpentine conductive traces provide capacitive coupling and geometric strain accommodation; broad or separated resonant channels preserve intended activation under deformation and mismatch.

nodes.label: Serpentine Geometric-Strain-Relief Interconnect
nodes.description: Use serpentine conductive interconnects to reduce strain and accommodate stretching on deformable or conformal substrates.
nodes.function: Provide stretchable, fatigue-tolerant electrical routing between rigid or semi-rigid modules.
nodes.mechanism: Serpentine paths unfold or flex under extension and bending, limiting axial strain in the conductor; compliant encapsulation or neutral-plane placement can further reduce strain transfer.

nodes.label: Serpentine Interconnect Buckling Design Model
nodes.description: Use geometry- and applied-strain-based analytical or numerical relations to predict buckling onset or mode and postbuckling strain in serpentine interconnects.
nodes.function: Guide serpentine interconnect geometry and deformation-mode selection.
nodes.mechanism: Analytical buckling and postbuckling scaling relations combine material stiffness, cross-sectional geometry, segment dimensions, and mode or ripple-count criteria, with numerical validation.

nodes.label: Serpentine Path Interconnect
nodes.description: Route conductors through periodic serpentine paths that accommodate extension, bending, and twisting through distributed geometric deformation.
nodes.function: Maintain electrical continuity between rigid or semi-rigid modules during substrate deformation.
nodes.mechanism: Curved segments rotate, bend, buckle, and unfold, converting global deformation into path-shape change and limiting direct conductor strain.

nodes.label: Shape-Matched Enclosing 3D Framework
nodes.description: Use a compliant shape-matched enclosing framework to maintain distributed tissue proximity around a volumetric biological object.
nodes.function: Provide low-constraint, large-area volumetric tissue contact.
nodes.mechanism: Curved or adjustable compliant elements surround the tissue and conform to changing biological geometry.
failure_modes: Loss of contact during growth or handling
Poor contact due to curvature mismatch

nodes.label: Shape-Memory-Triggered 2D-to-3D Assembly
nodes.description: Use a shape-memory substrate or phase transition to trigger and retain mechanically buckled 3D architectures.
nodes.function: Produce shape-fixed 3D structures after thermally controlled assembly.
nodes.mechanism: Thermal activation changes substrate stiffness or shape-memory state, enabling buckling followed by fixation on cooling or transition completion.
failure_modes: Elastic recovery after release if shape fixation is omitted
Poor deformation prediction if material viscoelasticity is neglected

nodes.label: Shape-Transforming Elastomer Transfer
nodes.description: Temporarily flatten or reshape a compliant molded transfer element, attach a planar device mesh, and relax it to deploy the device onto a prescribed curved geometry.
nodes.function: Map planar-fabricated arrays onto curved receivers through elastic shape transformation.
nodes.mechanism: Radial tension or another controlled deformation creates a planar pickup state; adhesion transfers the device; release restores the molded curvature and accommodates mismatch through compliant interconnect deformation.

nodes.label: Shared-link NFC power and data
nodes.description: Use one resonantly coupled near-field link to power a device and exchange sensor or control data with an external reader.
nodes.function: Enable compact battery-free or low-power wireless sensing and readout.
nodes.mechanism: A tuned receiver antenna harvests RF energy while the same NFC interface supports communication.
failure_modes: Data loss if buffering is inadequate

nodes.label: Shared Resistive Thermosensing-Heater
nodes.description: Use the same or co-located resistive elements to generate local Joule heat and measure temperature through resistance-dependent electrical readout.
nodes.function: Deliver controlled local heating while sensing temperature for monitoring or feedback regulation.
nodes.mechanism: A resistive trace or adjacent temperature-sensitive element converts electrical power to heat and temperature-dependent resistance into a thermal signal.

nodes.label: Shear-Assisted Transfer Printing
nodes.description: Apply lateral shear to a compliant stamp during delamination to reduce normal pull-off force and promote controlled object release onto a receiver.
nodes.function: Release transferred objects on challenging or structured receiver surfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Lateral displacement creates stamp shear, interfacial moment, and asymmetric normal stress that lowers the force required for delamination.
failure_modes: interface fracture outside the intended region

nodes.label: Shear-Flow Nanotube Alignment
nodes.description: Use directed shear or laminar flow during deposition to orient elongated nanostructures along a prescribed direction.
nodes.function: Control film anisotropy and directional transport-path geometry.
nodes.mechanism: Velocity gradients or substrate-flow fields bias nanotube long axes toward the flow direction during deposition.
failure_modes: Weak alignment near poorly defined flow regions

nodes.label: Single-Layer Reactive Dissolution Model
nodes.description: Model dissolution or degradation of a single reactive layer by coupling environmental-species diffusion, reaction kinetics, and thickness evolution to estimate material loss or lifetime.
nodes.function: Estimate single-layer dissolution kinetics and degradation timescales.
nodes.mechanism: Environmental species diffuse into the reactive layer, react throughout or at its surface, and reduce remaining thickness according to kinetic and transport parameters.
failure_modes: Ignoring intermediate eigenvalue regimes can substantially alter predicted thickness loss
Parameter transfer across environments without recalibration
Thin-layer approximation can be inaccurate for thick encapsulation
continuum approximation may not capture atomic-scale reactivity
extrapolation outside tested pH and temperature ranges

nodes.label: Single-Site Inertial Mechanoacoustic Sensing
nodes.description: Use a mechanically coupled high-bandwidth inertial sensor at one body site to capture low-frequency motion and tissue-conducted higher-frequency vibrations.
nodes.function: Acquire localized physiological, behavioral, or acoustic-mechanical signals from a conformal wearable.
nodes.mechanism: Skin or tissue motion is transferred directly to an embedded accelerometer or IMU, with bandwidth-aware processing separating motion and mechanoacoustic features.
failure_modes: insufficient temperature accuracy in short measurements

nodes.label: Single-Stage Sacrificial Release Transfer
nodes.description: Release a completed device or device collection from a temporary carrier by selectively removing an underlying sacrificial layer, then transfer it to a receiving substrate.
nodes.function: Decouple device fabrication from final-substrate integration.
nodes.mechanism: Selective etching or dissolution undercuts the fabricated device, after which pickup, printing, or assembly relocates it to the receiver.

nodes.label: Skin-Coupled Accelerometric Sensing
nodes.description: Measure broadband body-surface acceleration to recover motion, vocal, respiratory, cardiac, and interaction-related mechanical signals.
nodes.function: Infer physiological and behavioral state from tissue-conducted vibration.
nodes.mechanism: A skin-coupled accelerometer transfers low- to high-frequency body vibrations into a time-series signal that is separated into application-specific features.
failure_modes: Insufficient IMU sensitivity for subtle sounds

nodes.label: Skin-Integrated Actuation Platform
nodes.description: Combine conformal skin coupling with distributed actuation or intervention functions in a body-worn electronic platform.
nodes.function: Deliver tactile stimulation or other interventions while preserving soft body contact.
nodes.mechanism: Thin compliant platforms integrate independently addressable stimulators or therapeutic subsystems with skin-compatible sensing and electronics.

nodes.label: Slender-Ribbon Buckling Mechanics Model
nodes.description: Predict buckling wavelength, amplitude, mode, and strain of slender, patterned, or segmented ribbons on compliant substrates from coupled beam or ribbon mechanics.
nodes.function: Guide ribbon geometry and estimate buckling response or strain limits.
nodes.mechanism: Beam or ribbon kinematics combine bending, membrane, substrate, segment, bonding, and prestrain effects; minimization or post-buckling relations map inputs to deformation.
failure_modes: Inadequate profile for very long inactivated regions
disagreement between thermal and actual film strain
fracture when predicted peak strain exceeds material limit
long herringbone wavelength may be energetically weakly selected

nodes.label: Soft Core-Shell Strain Isolation
nodes.description: Use a very soft core and tougher enclosing shell to isolate embedded electronics from deformation while retaining handling strength and environmental protection.
nodes.function: Reduce strain localization and interfacial stress in compliant electronic packages.
nodes.mechanism: The soft core permits out-of-plane interconnect deformation and mechanical decoupling; the shell supplies enclosure, toughness, and deployment support.
failure_modes: local wrinkling and metal yielding if the core is too stiff or absent
reduced mechanics if core thickness is too small

nodes.label: Soft-Laminated Electrical Contact
nodes.description: Laminate a patterned metal or conductive electrode supported by an elastomeric stamp into conformal contact with a semiconductor, organic, or electroluminescent functional layer to form an electrical or electroluminescent device interface.
nodes.function: Create top or source/drain electrodes without directly depositing metal on the active layer.
nodes.mechanism: Elastomer compliance follows surface contours and van der Waals adhesion establishes intimate metal/active-layer electrical coupling.

nodes.label: Soft-Lithographic Metal-Mesh MacEtch
nodes.description: Implement MacEtch with a lithographically defined metal mesh to produce ordered semiconductor nanowire or nanopillar arrays.
nodes.function: Provide an ordered catalyst pattern for vertical or high-aspect-ratio MacEtch structures.
nodes.mechanism: Soft lithography defines nanoscale mesh openings; deposited metal catalyzes localized oxidation and dissolution during wet etching.

nodes.label: Soft relief molding and curing
nodes.description: Use a compliant relief mold or stamp to conformally replicate surface geometry into a curable or thermoplastic target material, followed by curing or solidification.
nodes.function: Transfer micro- or nanoscale relief into a target material.
nodes.mechanism: A soft patterned element contacts a liquid, curable, or deformable target; wetting and conformity reproduce the relief, and curing, baking, or embossing locks the geometry.

nodes.label: Spacing–Filling-Ratio Tradeoff
nodes.description: Select island spacing to balance active-area filling ratio against the interconnect length and deformation capacity required for system stretchability.
nodes.function: Set spatial density under stretchability requirements.
nodes.mechanism: Smaller spacing increases coverage but reduces compliant interconnect length and increases mechanical interaction; spacing and interconnect amplitude are jointly selected.
failure_modes: plastic yielding at bends or island junctions

nodes.label: Sparse Conformal Open Mesh
nodes.description: Use sparse filamentary or self-similar open meshes to distribute deformation and conform over curved or textured surfaces.
nodes.function: Provide breathable, surface-conforming distributed interfaces with preserved conduction.
nodes.mechanism: Open area, filament rearrangement, and redundant mesh pathways reduce membrane and bending constraints while maintaining connectivity.

nodes.label: Spatial-Differential Thermal-Field Inversion
nodes.description: Infer thermal transport or flow-related properties from spatial temperature distributions or directional differences using a calibrated thermal field model.
nodes.function: Recover conductivity, diffusivity, flow, or perfusion information from spatially resolved thermal responses.
nodes.mechanism: Measured steady-state fields or upstream-downstream temperature differences are mapped through conductive and convective heat-transfer models to estimate hidden transport parameters.

nodes.label: Spatial Motion Reference Cancellation
nodes.description: Subtract synchronized signals from spatially separated motion sensors to suppress common global motion while retaining location-dependent physiological motion.
nodes.function: Recover local biomechanical or physiological signals during movement.
nodes.mechanism: Matched sensors experience similar artifact motion but different task-specific physiological motion amplitudes; subtraction cancels the shared component.
failure_modes: Reduced duty cycle and depth when pulsing
Reference sensor coupling too strongly to heater

nodes.label: Spatially Separated Reference Differential
nodes.description: Subtract a spatially separated reference measurement from a target measurement to remove shared environmental or baseline variation.
nodes.function: Suppress common thermal or subject-specific disturbances in localized sensing.
nodes.mechanism: A target sensor and spatially separated reference sensor or site measure under matched conditions; their difference isolates the target response.
failure_modes: Large local gradients at the reference site
Reference sensor receives substantially different environmental conditions
baseline site differs materially from target site

nodes.label: Staged degradation-and-biocompatibility validation
nodes.description: Validate transient systems by staging functional retention, degradation or dissolution, and biological compatibility measurements across the intended deployment interval.
nodes.function: Establish operational lifetime, resorption behavior, and preliminary biological safety.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical or application performance is tracked before and during aqueous or in vivo degradation, while dissolution, cytotoxicity, biodistribution, histology, immune, or inflammatory endpoints are measured at defined stages.
failure_modes: Failure criterion dependent on measurement choice
Failure to separate function loss from material disappearance
False functional pass from device output without tissue capture

nodes.label: Staged Transient Implant Validation
nodes.description: Validate transient implant function and cytotoxicity through in vitro testing, animal efficacy studies, and comparison with a commercial reference under stated conditions; long-term tissue-interface and degradation-product safety require further investigation.
nodes.function: Establish translation-relevant biological and operational safety.
nodes.mechanism: Combine complementary cell, degradation, functional, implantation, histological, immune, systemic, and comparator measurements across defined timepoints.
design_handles: Choice of direct versus extract exposure
failure_modes: Loss of function before therapy completion
Material-specific toxicity may remain hidden if exposure is prevented
Point defects may confound encapsulation conclusions
Short observation period may miss chronic effects
false safety inference from short assays
lifetime variability from swelling or environmental stimuli
short-term validation mistaken for long-term safety

nodes.label: Steady-State Multilayer Conduction
nodes.description: Use steady-state layered heat-conduction models to estimate temperature fields and compare thermal performance across thin heat-source, interface, and substrate configurations.
nodes.function: Estimate operating temperature and guide steady thermal-stack selection.
nodes.mechanism: Apply a planar or axisymmetric heat source to a multilayer geometry and solve steady conduction with layer properties, interfacial continuity, ambient, and convection boundary conditions.
failure_modes: Breakdown of thin-source or axisymmetric approximation
Neglect of blood-flow heat loss in living tissue
accuracy degrades outside thin-device or large-substrate assumptions
localized gap temperature measurements can differ from active-device temperature
neglect of convection when it is non-negligible

nodes.label: Stimulus-Triggered Transient Degradation
nodes.description: Initiate device degradation or disappearance at a selected time using an external stimulus and a responsive material pathway.
nodes.function: Provide on-demand destruction or functional transition.
nodes.mechanism: Heat, light, moisture, electrical input, or generated chemical species activates depolymerization, dissolution, fracture, or related degradation.

nodes.label: Stripe-Isolated Network Channel
nodes.description: Use spatially isolated network stripes to define thin-film transistor channels and suppress neighboring or parasitic conduction paths.
nodes.function: Provide reproducible network-transistor switching with reduced device-to-device crosstalk.
nodes.mechanism: Patterning or selective removal separates network regions and interrupts unwanted long conductive pathways while preserving a gated percolating channel.
failure_modes: contact resistance domination at short channel lengths

nodes.label: Structure- and Processing-Controlled Dissolution
nodes.description: Tune transient-material lifetime through composition, doping, protective layers, geometry, and fabrication history.
nodes.function: Engineer intrinsic degradation rate and delay dissolution initiation.
nodes.mechanism: Doping, surface barriers, composition, density, stoichiometry, thickness, geometry, and processing alter reaction access and degradation pathways.

nodes.label: Support-Assisted Layer Transfer
nodes.description: Use temporary supports, adhesives, or sequential layer operations to transfer and integrate fragile films or device layers after source-side processing.
nodes.function: Decouple fabrication conditions from final multilayer or flexible-system assembly.
nodes.mechanism: A support or adhesive carries layers during release and placement; repeated transfer, bonding, planarization, or support removal builds the final structure.

nodes.label: Suprasternal-Notch Mechanoacoustic Skin Interface
nodes.description: A soft sensor placed at the suprasternal notch can record high-fidelity respiratory and cardiac signals, including cough-related features.
nodes.function: Capture mechanoacoustic and motion signals from a small neck-mounted interface during continuous or structured monitoring.
nodes.mechanism: Direct coupling to the suprasternal notch transfers intrathoracic motion and sound to a soft accelerometer package while compliant mechanics preserve contact during neck motion.

nodes.label: Surface-Eroding Transient Lifetime Control
nodes.description: Control diffusion-driven water-penetration timescales in PBTPA encapsulation by selecting thickness and chemical composition under aqueous exposure.
nodes.function: Provide predictable disappearance timing for exposed device layers.
nodes.mechanism: Aqueous surface reactions remove material at a measurable rate, with lifetime determined by thickness, chemistry, and environment.

nodes.label: Temperature-Compensated Wheatstone Readout
nodes.description: Reduce thermal error in resistive strain or pressure readout by matching strain and reference responses within a Wheatstone bridge.
nodes.function: Produce a differential measurement with reduced temperature-induced drift.
nodes.mechanism: Matched bridge elements undergo similar temperature-dependent resistance changes that largely preserve arm ratios, while mechanical strain creates differential imbalance.
design_handles: gauge placement relative to neutral plane

nodes.label: Temporary-Support Membrane Transfer
nodes.description: Use a selectively removable support or handling layer to stabilize a released membrane or patterned structure during donor-to-receiver transfer, then remove the support.
nodes.function: Transfer fragile or stress-sensitive structures while preserving continuity, planarity, and structural integrity.
nodes.mechanism: The temporary support carries handling and residual-stress loads during release and printing; selective dissolution or etching leaves the functional structure on the receiver.
failure_modes: Folds, holes, or tears near edges

nodes.label: Therapeutic Tissue-Response and Lesion Validation
nodes.description: Validate localized tissue therapy by synchronizing intervention with distributed physiological, electrical, thermal, contact, and lesion measurements.
nodes.function: Assess treatment delivery, tissue response, contact, and therapeutic outcome in vivo.
nodes.mechanism: Electrical or thermal energy delivery is paired with local sensing and independent histological or spatial response measurements.

nodes.label: Thermal-Expansion Reservoir Pump
nodes.description: Convert localized heating of an expandable actuator into pressure that expels fluid from a sealed reservoir through a microfluidic outlet.
nodes.function: Deliver stored fluid without a mechanical piston or tethered external fluid source.
nodes.mechanism: Joule heating expands a gas-containing or otherwise thermally responsive composite, displacing reservoir fluid and opening or driving flow through the outlet.

nodes.label: Thermally Grown Oxide Fluid Barrier
nodes.description: Use thermally grown silicon dioxide encapsulation to prevent water permeation into active device regions and increase stable operating lifetime under PBS at 37°C.
nodes.function: Extend stable operation of transient silicon devices.
nodes.mechanism: A dense oxide suppresses water permeation until barrier degradation or breach exposes active materials.
failure_modes: water penetration at cracks or boundaries

nodes.label: Thermally Isolated Thermoresistive Readout
nodes.description: Thermally isolate a target-contacting temperature sensor, optionally paired with an ambient reference, to reduce environmental interference in physiological temperature readout.
nodes.function: Measure target or skin temperature with reduced ambient cross-sensitivity.
nodes.mechanism: Insulating layers or an air cavity limit unwanted heat exchange and spatially separated sensors provide differential correction when needed.
failure_modes: excessive thermal isolation causing response lag
increased thermal mass and response time

nodes.label: Thermally Transferable Conductive Polymer–Nanocarbon Composite
nodes.description: Combine polyaniline with single-wall carbon nanotubes to increase conductivity and enable thermally transferred printed conductive contacts or features.
nodes.function: Fabricate patterned conductive contacts or layers compatible with flexible and organic electronic structures.
nodes.mechanism: The doped polymer survives thermal imaging or transfer while dispersed nanotubes raise conductivity and the composite forms an electrical contact to the receiving device layer.
aliases: DNNSA-doped polyaniline with single-walled carbon nanotubes

nodes.label: Thermocapillary Exposure–Etch Purification
nodes.description: Use selective heating to drive thermocapillary opening of a coating over targeted array members, then remove the exposed members by etching.
nodes.function: Purify heterogeneous one-dimensional conductor arrays while preserving alignment and the retained material class.
nodes.mechanism: Material-selective electrical, microwave, or optical absorption creates localized heating and surface-tension-driven trenches that expose targeted elements for reactive-ion etching.

nodes.label: Thermomechanical Stamp-Release Transfer
nodes.description: Release and transfer prefabricated structures from a compliant stamp using laser-induced thermal-expansion mismatch and interfacial delamination.
nodes.function: Enable noncontact or difficult-surface placement of fragile prefabricated structures.
nodes.mechanism: Localized laser heating creates constrained thermal mismatch, bending energy, and interfacial crack driving force that overcomes stamp-object adhesion.

nodes.label: Thickness-Programmed Crease Localization
nodes.description: Program localized folds in a planar precursor by locally reducing thickness or bending stiffness during compressive buckling.
nodes.function: Create deterministic crease-localized folding and programmable 3D architectures.
nodes.mechanism: Thin, compliant, or selectively de-layered regions concentrate bending while thicker regions remain comparatively stiff; prestrain release or substrate deformation drives folding at the designed locations.

nodes.label: Thin compliant molded microfluidics
nodes.description: Use thin, relief-defined compliant microfluidic layers to collect, route, and store biofluid while following skin deformation.
nodes.function: Provide mechanically unobtrusive epidermal fluid handling.
nodes.mechanism: Thin elastomeric walls, surface relief, molded channels, valves, and reservoirs preserve fluidic function while reducing bending stiffness and interfacial strain.

nodes.label: Three-Dimensional Modular Transfer
nodes.description: Assemble transferred modules or layers into stacked, nonplanar, or three-dimensional systems using controlled placement, bonding, and temporary handling support.
nodes.function: Construct complex heterogeneous architectures from separately fabricated building blocks.
nodes.mechanism: Modules are retrieved, oriented, aligned, bonded, and optionally supported by dissolvable carriers or reusable tools during three-dimensional assembly.

nodes.label: Threshold-Triggered Accumulation Readout
nodes.description: Accumulate stimulus-derived charge or voltage and wake communication electronics only when a meaningful threshold is crossed, then read, report, and reset the accumulated state.
nodes.function: Provide intermittent exposure reporting with low idle power.
nodes.mechanism: A storage element integrates the measurand; a comparator detects threshold crossing, wakes the controller, initiates readout and wireless transmission, and resets the storage state.

nodes.label: Threshold-Triggered Haptic Feedback
nodes.description: Translate threshold crossings in monitored or computed state variables into immediate tactile cues with programmable patterns or duration.
nodes.function: Provide actionable feedback without continuous visual attention.
nodes.mechanism: Computed metrics are compared with personalized thresholds and actuator output is selected according to threshold state.

nodes.label: Threshold-Triggered User Feedback
nodes.description: Compare wearable-derived state metrics with configurable thresholds and trigger haptic, visual, or caregiver alerts when limits are crossed.
nodes.function: Prompt timely user behavior adjustment or care intervention.
nodes.mechanism: Measured or accumulated signals are evaluated against personalized or predefined thresholds that activate feedback outputs.

nodes.label: Threshold-Valve Sequential Sampling
nodes.description: Separate sequential surface-biofluid samples using passive pressure-thresholded routing into isolated chambers.
nodes.function: Provide time- or volume-resolved sampling with reduced mixing and cross-contamination.
nodes.mechanism: Ordered capillary-bursting or pressure-triggered valves redirect fluid as chambers fill, creating chronologically separated aliquots.

nodes.label: Tissue Loading and Contact Matching
nodes.description: Tune support, membrane, and interface mechanics so applied loading or contact pressure matches tissue requirements while minimizing physiological disturbance.
nodes.function: Achieve stable, low-trauma tissue contact and transferable loading conditions.
nodes.mechanism: Normalized loading relations and membrane mechanics connect geometry, stiffness, thickness, extension, and pressure to tissue loading equivalence and contact stability.
failure_modes: inaccurate prediction for strongly non-axisymmetric geometries

nodes.label: Top-Down Patterned Semiconductor Release
nodes.description: Create transferable or suspended semiconductor elements by lithographically patterning a wafer or film and selectively removing the underlying support.
nodes.function: Fabricate defined free-standing semiconductor microelements, membranes, or sensors.
nodes.mechanism: Patterned masks define geometry; directional or anisotropic etching shapes the semiconductor, and selective undercut or sacrificial-layer dissolution frees it.

nodes.label: Transcranial or Converter-Mediated Optical Delivery
nodes.description: Deliver activating optical wavelengths to deep neural targets through tissue or local optical converters without placing a conventional fiber at the target.
nodes.function: Enable less-invasive deep or transcranial optogenetic modulation.
nodes.mechanism: Penetrating red emission or nanoparticle upconversion converts externally delivered excitation into visible light near opsin-expressing neurons.

nodes.label: Transferred SWNT-channel TFT
nodes.description: Use a transferred SWNT network as the semiconducting channel of a flexible TFT, optionally pairing it with a high-capacitance dielectric for low-voltage operation.
nodes.function: Switch or amplify current in flexible electronics with a transferred nanotube channel.
nodes.mechanism: Gate-induced electrostatic charge modulation controls percolative transport through the transferred SWNT network; increased dielectric capacitance strengthens low-voltage coupling.

nodes.label: Transferred thermally grown oxide barrier
nodes.description: Grow dense, uniform thin SiO2 on a silicon donor wafer and release it for subsequent physical transfer.
nodes.function: Isolate electronics from aqueous and ionic environments while preserving thin flexible integration.
nodes.mechanism: Thermal oxidation forms a dense oxide on a pristine wafer; wafer removal or etching releases the film for physical transfer.

nodes.label: Transient Bioresorbable Neural Interface
nodes.description: Provide temporary neural sensing, stimulation, or modulation using implanted functional materials that resorb after the therapeutic or recording interval.
nodes.function: Support finite-duration neural interfacing without retrieval surgery.
nodes.mechanism: Resorbable conductors, dielectrics, semiconductors, substrates, and encapsulation retain function during use and then hydrolyze, dissolve, or disintegrate in tissue or biofluid.
failure_modes: loss of function before treatment ends

nodes.label: Transient Electrochemical Energy Storage
nodes.description: Store electrical energy temporarily in degradable electrochemical cells whose electrodes, electrolyte, separator, substrate, and packaging later dissolve or resorb.
nodes.function: Supply bounded-duration stored electrical power without persistent energy hardware.
nodes.mechanism: Transient electrodes and electrolytes provide capacitive or galvanic energy storage before sequential dissolution, hydrolysis, corrosion, or leaching removes the cell.

nodes.label: Transient Energy Harvesting
nodes.description: Generate temporary electrical power from optical, mechanical, radiofrequency, or environmental inputs using degradable conversion structures.
nodes.function: Power transient systems through harvested energy without persistent power hardware.
nodes.mechanism: Transient photovoltaic or other energy-conversion elements transform supplied or ambient energy before their active layers, conductors, substrates, or encapsulation dissolve or bioresorb.

nodes.label: Material-Specific Fully Transient Electronics
nodes.description: Implement a fully transient electronic system using a defined transient material family, device architecture, or integration process.
nodes.function: Adapt transient-system construction to specific active materials, circuits, fabrication flows, or interfaces.
nodes.mechanism: Material selection, nanomembrane processing, conductive printing, foundry integration, or wireless packaging provides the required transient subsystem function.

nodes.label: Transient Sensing Platform
nodes.description: Provide temporary physiological or environmental monitoring using degradable transducers or networked sensing nodes that disappear after deployment.
nodes.function: Acquire and communicate measurements during a finite interval without retrieval of the sensing hardware.
nodes.mechanism: Transient resistive, nanomembrane, or distributed sensing elements collect signals and use dissolvable materials, interconnects, and packaging for controlled end-of-life disappearance.

nodes.label: Tubular Peripheral-Nerve Cuff
nodes.description: Use a slit or compliant tubular electrode cuff to wrap a peripheral nerve and provide close circumferential electrical apposition.
nodes.function: Interface stimulation electrodes with a peripheral nerve.
nodes.mechanism: An exposed nerve-facing electrode is embedded in a compliant tubular polymer cuff that encircles the nerve.

nodes.label: Ultrathin Localized Microfluidic Delivery
nodes.description: Use an ultrathin bonded elastomeric channel structure to route fluid from reservoirs to a localized tissue interface with minimal mechanical burden.
nodes.function: Provide compliant localized fluid delivery through a narrow implantable or conformal probe.
nodes.mechanism: Patterned elastomer channel layers are bonded to a cover, accessed through vertical ports, and released as an ultrathin flexible probe.

nodes.label: Vector Optical Process Modeling
nodes.description: Use full-vector electromagnetic modeling to predict and diagnose polarization- and geometry-dependent exposure fields and patterned-process outcomes.
nodes.function: Explain deviations from scalar diffraction and guide optical process design and validation.
nodes.mechanism: Numerical Maxwell-equation solutions resolve polarization, interfaces, field distributions, and depth evolution; exposure fields can be mapped to predicted resist or crosslinked geometry.
failure_modes: Broadband incoherent exposure not represented by monochromatic simulation
Model mismatch from nonideal mask geometry
Pulse-duration and bandwidth effects are omitted in the reported calculations
Simplified threshold model ignores developer and photocatalyst diffusion
omission of resist dissolution kinetics and nonlinear exposure chemistry

nodes.label: Volumetric 3D Multimodal Framework
nodes.description: Distribute independently addressable electrical, optical, thermal, and chemical modules across a compliant three-dimensional tissue-conforming framework.
nodes.function: Record, stimulate, sense, and modulate volumetric biological systems.
nodes.mechanism: A shaped cage or multilayer 3D framework carries heterogeneous microelectronic modules around or across the tissue volume.

nodes.label: Volumetric Interference Phase-Mask Patterning
nodes.description: Use a conformal relief phase mask to generate a depth-dependent interference field that is converted into three-dimensional polymer or resist relief.
nodes.function: Fabricate volumetric, periodic, or complex three-dimensional nanostructures.
nodes.mechanism: Diffracted beams from the relief interfere through the photosensitive thickness; exposure and development threshold the volumetric intensity distribution into 3D structure.
failure_modes: Insufficient structure away from the mask surface
Loss of intensity visibility with depth

nodes.label: Wavy Silicon Semiconductor Integration
nodes.description: Integrate active semiconductor devices with geometrically strain-isolating wavy or buckled silicon structures on compliant substrates to preserve function during large deformation.
nodes.function: Provide stretchable electronic or optoelectronic building blocks.
nodes.mechanism: Buckled silicon ribbons or membranes accommodate substrate deformation through geometric shape change, reducing strain in active semiconductor regions while maintaining electrical interfaces.
failure_modes: PDMS chemical instability in severe conditions

nodes.label: Wheatstone Bridge Differential Readout
nodes.description: Convert resistance changes in four bridge elements into a differential voltage suitable for amplification and acquisition.
nodes.function: Condition resistive strain or pressure measurements while providing differential output and partial common-mode rejection.
nodes.mechanism: Resistance-dependent imbalance between bridge arms changes the bridge output ratio; an amplifier can increase the differential signal before digitization.

nodes.label: Wired Remote Electronics Module
nodes.description: Place sensing or actuation elements near the target and connect them by compliant wires to a remote module containing power, processing, and communication electronics.
nodes.function: Reduce local tissue burden while retaining powered sensing and signal processing.
nodes.mechanism: Spatial partitioning separates soft sensor heads from centralized electronics; flexible wired interconnects carry power and signals between the subsystems.

nodes.label: Wireless Distributed Thermal Control
nodes.description: Coordinate remotely programmed thermal elements using wireless sensing, feedback, and distributed control.
nodes.function: Regulate spatially distributed thermal environments or arrays.
